<!-- example-1: body_md -->
\label{ex:gh_not_h}
The function
$
  f(x)=x^2+\int_0^x(x-t)\sin(t^2)\mathrm{d}t
$
is $1$-strongly convex and satisfies~\eqref{as:gh} with $M_0=M_1=2$, but
it does not satisfy~\eqref{as:h}.
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- example-2: body_md -->
\label{ex:cosh_lh_not_gh}
The $1$-strongly convex function $f(x)=\cosh x-1$ satisfies~\eqref{as:lh} for every $\rho>0$ with $M_0=\sinh\rho$ and
$M_1=e^\rho$, but it does not satisfy~\eqref{as:gh}.
<!-- end example-2 -->
<!-- example-3: body_md -->
\label{ex:exp_lh_not_gh}
The convex function $f(x)=e^x-x-1$ satisfies~\eqref{as:lh} for every
$\rho>0$ with $M_0=M_1=e^\rho$, but it does not satisfy~\eqref{as:gh}.
<!-- end example-3 -->
<!-- example-4: body_md -->
\label{ex:quartic_lh_not_gh}
For $\mu\geq0$, consider
$
  f(x)=\frac{\mu}{2}\|{x} \|^2+\frac{1}{4}\|{x} \|^4
$
for $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$.
The function is convex for $\mu=0$ and $\mu$-strongly convex for $\mu>0$.
For every $\rho>0$, it satisfies~\eqref{as:lh} with $M_0=3\rho+4$ and
$M_1=2$, but it does not satisfy~\eqref{as:gh}.
<!-- end example-4 -->
<!-- example-5: body_md -->
\label{ex:poisson_lh_not_gh}
Let $a_i\in\mathbb{R}^d$ with $[a_i]_1=1$ and $b_i\in\mathbb{N}$, $i=1,\ldots,n$. The Poisson regression loss $f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\left( e^{\left\langle a_i,x\right\rangle}-b_i\left\langle a_i,x\right\rangle\right)$ is convex and satisfies~\eqref{as:lh} for every $\rho>0$ with $M_0=\|{b} \|_1c^3e^{c\rho}$ and $M_1=c^3e^{c\rho}$, where $c=\max_i\|{a_i} \|$, but it does not satisfy~\eqref{as:gh}.
<!-- end example-5 -->
<!-- example-6: body_md -->
\label{ex:lp_lh_not_gh}
Let $p>3$, $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$, $A\neq0$, and $b\in\mathbb{R}^n$. The $\ell_p$ regression loss $f(x)=\tfrac1p\|{Ax-b} \|_p^p$ is convex and satisfies~\eqref{as:lh} for every $\rho>0$ with 
\begin{equation*}
  M_0=(p-1)(p-2)\|{A} \|^3\left(1+2\|{b} \|_p+\|{A} \|\rho\right)^{p-3}, \qquad  M_1=3\sqrt{n}M_0/\sigma_+(A),
\end{equation*}
where $\sigma_+(A)$ is the smallest positive singular value of $A$, but it does not satisfy~\eqref{as:gh}.
<!-- end example-6 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:td_to_lh}
Suppose that, for some $L_0>0$ and $L_1\geq0$,
$\|{\nabla^2 f(x)} \| \leq L_0+L_1\|{\nabla f(x)} \|$.
If~\eqref{as:td} holds with constants $\widehat M_0$ and
$\widehat M_1$, then, for every $\rho>0$,~\eqref{as:lh} holds with
\begin{equation*}
    M_0(\rho)=\widehat M_0+
  \widehat M_1L_0\rho e^{L_1\rho},\qquad
  M_1(\rho)=\widehat M_1e^{L_1\rho}.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:ms}
  A Monteiro-Svaiter (MS) oracle at $x$ returns $y = x + s$ and $\tau > 0$ such that
  \begin{equation*}
    \|\nabla f(x + s) + \tau s\| \leq \tau \|s\| / 2.
  \end{equation*}
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:basic_pd_ms_convergence}
Suppose that $f$ is convex,~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} holds, and
either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds.
Let
$\ell_0:=\max\left\lbrace1,\tfrac{2D\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}},
      \tfrac{\eta_0D^2}{\sqrt6 B\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}\right\rbrace$.
For every $\varepsilon>0$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:basic_pd_ms} generates an iterate $x_N$
satisfying $f(x_N)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon$ within the following number of iterations
\begin{equation}
  N=\mathcal{O}\left(
    1+\log \ell_0
    +B\log_+\tfrac{f(x_0)-f^\ast}{\max\left\lbrace\varepsilon,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace}
      +\sqrt{\tfrac{M_0D^3}{\varepsilon}}+\tfrac{\delta D^2}{\varepsilon}
    \right).
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_complexity}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_damped_movement_main}
Suppose that $f$ is convex,~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} holds, and
either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds. 
Let $(y,\tau) := \textnormal{\textsc{MSBacktrack}}(x, \eta)$.
If at least one trial is rejected (equivalently $\tau>\eta$), then 
\begin{equation*}
  \|{s} \|>\min\left\lbrace\tfrac\rho2,\tfrac1{6\sqrt{M_1}}\right\rbrace~~\text{or}~~\tau\leq8\delta+24M_0\|{s} \|
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:basic_pd_ms_strong_main}
Suppose that $f$ is $\mu$-strongly convex,~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} holds,
and either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds. Let
\begin{equation*}
  \overline\tau:=\max\left\lbrace
    \eta_0,8\delta+48M_0\sqrt{{2(f(x_0)-f^\ast)}/\mu},
    {2(f(x_0)-f^\ast)}/{r_0^2}\right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
Every completed iteration $k$ of Algorithm~\ref{alg:basic_pd_ms}
satisfies $\tau_k\leq\overline\tau$ and 
\begin{equation*}
  \tau_k\leq8\max_{0\leq j\leq k}2^{j-k}\delta_j
    +\overline\tau\left( 1-\tfrac{2\mu}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^k, \quad
  f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast
  \leq\left(1-\tfrac{2\mu}{3\tau_k+2\mu}\right)^2
    (f(x_k)-f^\ast).
\end{equation*}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:basic_pd_ms_relative_main}
Suppose that $f$ is $\mu$-strongly convex, either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds, and~\eqref{as:basic_pd_ms_relative_global} holds for some $\nu>0$.
Algorithm~\ref{alg:basic_pd_ms} converges globally superlinearly.
Every completed iteration $k$ satisfies
\begin{equation*}
  \tau_k\leq
  \max\left\lbrace\tfrac{2^{-k}\eta_0}{\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|},
    \tfrac{24M_0}{\mu}+8\nu,\tfrac2{r_0}\right\rbrace
  \|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|,~ 
  f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast
  \leq\left(1-\tfrac{2\mu}{3\tau_k+2\mu}\right)^2
    \left( f(x_k)-f^\ast\right).
\end{equation*}
Let $C:=
  \tfrac{9\left(\|{\nabla^2f(x^\ast)} \|+\mu\right)}{2\mu^2}
  \left(8\nu+\tfrac{24M_0}{\mu}\right)^2$.
Let for some $K_0\geq1$, $f(x_{K_0})-f^\ast
  \leq\min\left\lbrace\tfrac{\mu r_0^2}{8},\tfrac1{2C}\right\rbrace$.
Then, after finitely many additional iterations independent of $\varepsilon$,
the method converges quadratically:
\begin{equation*}
  f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast
  \leq C\left( f(x_k)-f^\ast\right)^2,
  \qquad k\geq  K\geq K_0.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:ahpe_damped_convergence}
Suppose that $f$ is convex,~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} holds, and
either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds.
For any $\varepsilon>0$, the method generates an iterate $w_N$ satisfying
$f(w_N)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon$ within
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal{O}\left(
    B\left(1+\log_+\tfrac{\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace R^2}{\max\left\lbrace\varepsilon,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace}\right)
    +\left(\tfrac{M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/7}
    +\sqrt{\tfrac{\delta R^2}{\varepsilon}}
  \right)
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_outer_complexity}
\end{equation}
iterations. Moreover, there exists iterate $K\geq1$ with
$K=\mathcal{O}\left( B\max\left\lbrace1,\log\tfrac{\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace R^2}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}\right\rbrace\right)$ such that
\begin{gather}
  f(w_k)-f^\ast
  =\mathcal{O}\left(\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace R^2\exp\left(-\tfrac{c(k-1)}B\right)\right),
  \qquad 1\leq k<K,
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_far_final}\\
  f(w_{K+n})-f^\ast
  =\mathcal{O}\left(\tfrac{M_0R^3}{(B+n)^{7/2}}+\tfrac{\delta R^2}{(B+n)^2}\right),
  \qquad n=0,1,\ldots.
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_near_final}
\end{gather}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:global_taylor_remainders}
Suppose that \eqref{as:gh} holds. Then, for all $x,s\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla f(x+s)-\nabla f(x)-\nabla^2 f(x)s} \|
  \leq \tfrac{L(x)}{2}\|{s} \|^2,\\
  \left|
    f(x+s)-f(x)-\left\langle\nabla f(x),s\right\rangle
    -\tfrac{1}{2}\left\langle\nabla^2 f(x)s,s\right\rangle
  \right|
  \leq \tfrac{L(x)}{6}\|{s} \|^3.
\end{gather*}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:local_taylor_remainders}
Suppose that \eqref{as:lh} holds. Then, for all $x,s\in\mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying
$\|{s} \|\leq\rho$,
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla f(x+s)-\nabla f(x)-\nabla^2 f(x)s} \|
  \leq \tfrac{L(x)}{2}\|{s} \|^2,\\
  \left|
    f(x+s)-f(x)-\left\langle\nabla f(x),s\right\rangle
    -\tfrac{1}{2}\left\langle\nabla^2 f(x)s,s\right\rangle
  \right|
  \leq \tfrac{L(x)}{6}\|{s} \|^3.
\end{gather*}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
We follow~\citet[Lemma~1.2.4]{nesterov2018lectures}. For $t\in[0,1]$,~\eqref{as:gh}, or~\eqref{as:lh} with $\|{ts} \|\leq\rho$, gives $\|{\nabla^2 f(x+ts)-\nabla^2 f(x)} \|\leq tL(x)\|{s} \|$. Hence,
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla f(x+s)-\nabla f(x)-\nabla^2 f(x)s} \|
  =\|{\int_0^1\left(\nabla^2 f(x+ts)-\nabla^2 f(x)\right) s\mathrm{d}t} \|\\
  \leq\int_0^1 tL(x)\|{s} \|^2\mathrm{d}t
  =\frac{L(x)}{2}\|{s} \|^2.
\end{gather*}
Since $\|{ts} \|\leq\|{s} \|$, the same bound holds for the step $ts$:
\begin{equation*}
  \|{\nabla f(x+ts)-\nabla f(x)-t\nabla^2 f(x)s} \|
  \leq\frac{L(x)}{2}t^2\|{s} \|^2,
  \qquad t\in[0,1].
\end{equation*}
Using $f(x+s)-f(x)=\int_0^1\left\langle\nabla f(x+ts),s\right\rangle\mathrm{d}t$ and $\int_0^1t\mathrm{d}t=\frac{1}{2}$, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \left|
    f(x+s)-f(x)-\left\langle\nabla f(x),s\right\rangle
    -\frac{1}{2}\left\langle\nabla^2 f(x)s,s\right\rangle
  \right|\\
  =\left|
    \int_0^1\left\langle\nabla f(x+ts)-\nabla f(x)-t\nabla^2 f(x)s,s\right\rangle\mathrm{d}t
  \right|
  \leq\int_0^1\frac{L(x)}{2}t^2\|{s} \|^3\mathrm{d}t
  =\frac{L(x)}{6}\|{s} \|^3.
\end{gather*}
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Direct differentiation gives
\begin{gather*}
  f'(x)=2x+\int_0^x\sin(t^2)\mathrm{d}t,\qquad
  f''(x)=2+\sin(x^2),\qquad
  f^{(3)}(x)=2x\cos(x^2).
\end{gather*}
Thus, $f''(x)\geq1$, so $f$ is $1$-strongly convex. Moreover,
$f'(0)=0$ and
\begin{equation*}
  |f'(x)|
  =\left|\int_0^x f''(t)\mathrm{d}t\right|
  \geq |x|.
\end{equation*}
If $|y-x|\leq1$, then
\begin{gather*}
  |f''(y)-f''(x)|
  =|\sin(y^2)-\sin(x^2)|
  \leq |y^2-x^2|
  \leq \left(2|x|+1\right)|y-x|
  \leq \left(2+2|f'(x)|\right)|y-x|.
\end{gather*}
If $|y-x|>1$, then
\begin{equation*}
  |f''(y)-f''(x)|
  \leq2
  \leq2|y-x|
  \leq\left(2+2|f'(x)|\right)|y-x|.
\end{equation*}
Hence,~\eqref{as:gh} holds with $M_0=M_1=2$. On the other hand, for
$x_n=\sqrt{2\pi n}$,
\begin{equation*}
  |f^{(3)}(x_n)|=2\sqrt{2\pi n}\longrightarrow+\infty.
\end{equation*}
Condition~\eqref{as:h} would imply $|f^{(3)}(x)|\leq L$ by taking the
directional limit in~\eqref{as:h}. Therefore,~\eqref{as:h} does not hold.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
We have
\begin{gather*}
  f'(x)=\sinh x,\qquad
  f''(x)=\cosh x,\qquad
  f^{(3)}(x)=\sinh x.
\end{gather*}
Since $f''(x)\geq1$, the function is $1$-strongly convex. Let
$h=y-x$ and $|h|\leq\rho$. For every $t\in[0,1]$,
\begin{gather*}
  |\sinh(x+th)|
  \leq |\sinh x|\cosh(th)+\cosh x|\sinh(th)|\\
  \leq |\sinh x|\cosh\rho+\cosh x\sinh\rho
  \leq \sinh\rho+e^\rho|\sinh x|,
\end{gather*}
where we used $\cosh x\leq1+|\sinh x|$. Therefore,
\begin{equation*}
  |f''(y)-f''(x)|
  \leq |h|\int_0^1|\sinh(x+th)|\mathrm{d}t 
  \leq\left(\sinh\rho+e^\rho|f'(x)|\right)|y-x|.
\end{equation*}
This proves~\eqref{as:lh}. If~\eqref{as:gh} held, then the choice $x=0$
would give
\begin{equation*}
  \cosh y-1\leq M_0|y|,
  \qquad y\in\mathbb{R},
\end{equation*}
which is impossible as $y\to+\infty$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
We have
\begin{gather*}
  f'(x)=e^x-1,\qquad
  f''(x)=f^{(3)}(x)=e^x.
\end{gather*}
Let $h=y-x$ and $|h|\leq\rho$. The mean value theorem gives
\begin{equation*}
  |f''(y)-f''(x)|
  =e^x|e^h-1|
  \leq e^\rho e^x|h|
  \leq e^\rho\left(1+|f'(x)|\right)|y-x|.
\end{equation*}
Hence,~\eqref{as:lh} holds with $M_0=M_1=e^\rho$. If~\eqref{as:gh}
held, then the choice $x=0$ would give
\begin{equation*}
  e^y-1\leq M_0|y|,
  \qquad y\in\mathbb{R},
\end{equation*}
which is impossible as $y\to+\infty$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
We have
\begin{gather*}
  \nabla f(x)=\left(\mu+\|{x} \|^2\right) x,\qquad
  \nabla^2f(x)=\left(\mu+\|{x} \|^2\right) I+2xx^\top.
\end{gather*}
Hence, $\nabla^2f(x)\succeq\mu I$. Let $s=y-x$ and
$r=\|{s} \|\leq\rho$. Using
\begin{equation*}
  yy^\top-xx^\top=xs^\top+sx^\top+ss^\top,
\end{equation*}
we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla^2f(y)-\nabla^2f(x)} \|
  \leq\left|\|{y} \|^2-\|{x} \|^2\right|
  +2\|{yy^\top-xx^\top} \|\\
  \leq\left(2\|{x} \|+r\right) r
  +2\left(2\|{x} \|r+r^2\right)
  =\left(6\|{x} \|+3r\right) r.
\end{gather*}
For every $t\geq0$,
\begin{equation*}
  4+2t^3-6t=2(t-1)^2(t+2)\geq0.
\end{equation*}
Since
$\|{\nabla f(x)} \|=\left(\mu+\|{x} \|^2\right)\|{x} \|\geq\|{x} \|^3$,
we have
\begin{equation*}
  6\|{x} \|\leq4+2\|{\nabla f(x)} \|.
\end{equation*}
Consequently,
\begin{equation*}
  \|{\nabla^2f(y)-\nabla^2f(x)} \|
  \leq\left(3\rho+4+2\|{\nabla f(x)} \|\right)\|{y-x} \|,
\end{equation*}
which proves~\eqref{as:lh} with the stated constants. At $x=0$,
\begin{equation*}
  \|{\nabla^2f(y)-\nabla^2f(0)} \|=3\|{y} \|^2,
  \qquad \nabla f(0)=0.
\end{equation*}
Thus,~\eqref{as:gh} would require $3\|{y} \|^2\leq M_0\|{y} \|$ for
all $y\in\mathbb{R}^d$, which is impossible.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Let $\mu_i(x):= e^{\left\langle a_i,x\right\rangle}$. We have
\begin{gather*}
  \nabla f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\left(\mu_i(x)-b_i\right) a_i,\qquad
  \nabla^2f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\mu_i(x)a_ia_i^\top\succeq0.
\end{gather*}
Since $[a_i]_1=1$ and $b_i\geq0$, the first coordinate of $\nabla f(x)$ equals $\sum_{i=1}^n\mu_i(x)-\|{b} \|_1$. Hence,
\begin{equation}
  \sum_{i=1}^n\mu_i(x)\leq\|{b} \|_1+\|{\nabla f(x)} \|.
  \label{eq:poisson_intensity}
\end{equation}
Let $s=y-x$ and $\|{s} \|\leq\rho$. Then $|\left\langle a_i,s\right\rangle|\leq c\|{s} \|\leq c\rho$. Using $|e^u-1|\leq e^{|u|}|u|$ for $u\in\mathbb{R}$, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla^2f(y)-\nabla^2f(x)} \|
  =\left\|\sum_{i=1}^n\mu_i(x)\left( e^{\left\langle a_i,s\right\rangle}-1\right) a_ia_i^\top\right\|
  \leq c^3e^{c\rho}\|{s} \|\sum_{i=1}^n\mu_i(x)\\
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:poisson_intensity}}{\leq}
  \left(\|{b} \|_1c^3e^{c\rho}+c^3e^{c\rho}\|{\nabla f(x)} \|\right)\|{y-x} \|.
\end{gather*}
This proves~\eqref{as:lh} with the stated constants. Let $e_1$ be the first coordinate vector. Since $\left\langle a_i,e_1\right\rangle=1$, we have $\nabla^2f(x+te_1)=e^t\nabla^2f(x)$ for $t\in\mathbb{R}$ and
\begin{equation*}
  \|{\nabla^2f(x)} \|
  \geq\left\langle\nabla^2f(x)e_1,e_1\right\rangle
  =\sum_{i=1}^n\mu_i(x)>0.
\end{equation*}
If~\eqref{as:gh} held, then, for all $t>0$,
\begin{equation*}
  \left( e^t-1\right)\|{\nabla^2f(x)} \|
  =\|{\nabla^2f(x+te_1)-\nabla^2f(x)} \|
  \leq\left( M_0+M_1\|{\nabla f(x)} \|\right) t,
\end{equation*}
which is impossible as $t\to+\infty$.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Let $a_i^\top$ be the rows of $A$, $r:= Ax-b$, and $\psi(u):=|u|^{p-2}u$ for $u\in\mathbb{R}$. We have
\begin{gather*}
  \nabla f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\psi(r_i)a_i,\qquad
  \nabla^2f(x)=(p-1)\sum_{i=1}^n|r_i|^{p-2}a_ia_i^\top\succeq0.
\end{gather*}
First, we bound $\|{r} \|_p$ by $\|{\nabla f(x)} \|$. Let $P$ be the orthogonal projector onto the range of $A^\top$. The gradient $\nabla f(x)=A^\top\psi(r)$ belongs to this range, and $\|{Az} \|\geq\sigma_+(A)\|{z} \|$ for all $z$ in this range. Therefore, H\"older's inequality and $\|{v} \|\leq\sqrt{n}\|{v} \|_\infty\leq\sqrt{n}\|{v} \|_p$ for $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$ give
\begin{gather*}
  \|{r} \|_p^p-\|{r} \|_p^{p-1}\|{b} \|_p
  \leq\sum_{i=1}^n\psi(r_i)\left( r_i+b_i\right)
  =\left\langle\nabla f(x),x\right\rangle
  =\left\langle\nabla f(x),Px\right\rangle
  \leq\frac{\|{\nabla f(x)} \|\|{APx} \|}{\sigma_+(A)}\\
  =\frac{\|{\nabla f(x)} \|\|{r+b} \|}{\sigma_+(A)}
  \leq\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sigma_+(A)}\|{\nabla f(x)} \|\left(\|{r} \|_p+\|{b} \|_p\right).
\end{gather*}
If $\|{r} \|_p>\max\left\lbrace1,2\|{b} \|_p\right\rbrace$, then $\|{r} \|_p-\|{b} \|_p>\|{r} \|_p/2$ and $\|{r} \|_p+\|{b} \|_p<3\|{r} \|_p/2$. In this case, the previous display gives $\|{r} \|_p^{p-1}<\frac{3\sqrt{n}}{\sigma_+(A)}\|{\nabla f(x)} \|=\frac{M_1}{M_0}\|{\nabla f(x)} \|$, and $\|{r} \|_p>1$ implies
\begin{gather*}
  \left(\|{r} \|_p+\|{A} \|\rho\right)^{p-3}
  \leq(1+\|{A} \|\rho)^{p-3}\|{r} \|_p^{p-3}
  \leq(1+\|{A} \|\rho)^{p-3}\|{r} \|_p^{p-1}\\
  <\left(1+2\|{b} \|_p+\|{A} \|\rho\right)^{p-3}\frac{M_1}{M_0}\|{\nabla f(x)} \|.
\end{gather*}
Otherwise, $\|{r} \|_p\leq1+2\|{b} \|_p$ and $\left(\|{r} \|_p+\|{A} \|\rho\right)^{p-3}\leq\left(1+2\|{b} \|_p+\|{A} \|\rho\right)^{p-3}$. In both cases, the definition of $M_0$ gives
\begin{equation}
  (p-1)(p-2)\|{A} \|^3\left(\|{r} \|_p+\|{A} \|\rho\right)^{p-3}
  \leq M_0+M_1\|{\nabla f(x)} \|.
  \label{eq:lp_residual}
\end{equation}
Now let $s=y-x$ and $\|{s} \|\leq\rho$. Then $Ay-b=r+As$ and $|\left\langle a_i,s\right\rangle|\leq\|{A} \|\|{s} \|\leq\|{A} \|\rho$. By the mean value theorem and $|r_i|\leq\|{r} \|_p$,
\begin{gather*}
  \left||r_i+\left\langle a_i,s\right\rangle|^{p-2}-|r_i|^{p-2}\right|
  \leq(p-2)\left(|r_i|+|\left\langle a_i,s\right\rangle|\right)^{p-3}|\left\langle a_i,s\right\rangle|\\
  \leq(p-2)\left(\|{r} \|_p+\|{A} \|\rho\right)^{p-3}\|{A} \|\|{s} \|.
\end{gather*}
Since $\|{\sum_{i=1}^nw_ia_ia_i^\top} \|\leq\max_i|w_i|\|{A^\top A} \|$ for $w\in\mathbb{R}^n$, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla^2f(y)-\nabla^2f(x)} \|
  =(p-1)\left\|\sum_{i=1}^n\left(|r_i+\left\langle a_i,s\right\rangle|^{p-2}-|r_i|^{p-2}\right) a_ia_i^\top\right\|\\
  \leq(p-1)(p-2)\|{A} \|^3\left(\|{r} \|_p+\|{A} \|\rho\right)^{p-3}\|{s} \|
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:lp_residual}}{\leq}
  \left( M_0+M_1\|{\nabla f(x)} \|\right)\|{y-x} \|.
\end{gather*}
This proves~\eqref{as:lh}. Since $A\neq0$, there is $j$ with $a_j\neq0$. For $t\geq|b_j|/\|{a_j} \|^2$,
\begin{equation*}
  \|{\nabla^2f(ta_j)} \|\|{a_j} \|^2
  \geq\left\langle\nabla^2f(ta_j)a_j,a_j\right\rangle
  \geq(p-1)\left( t\|{a_j} \|^2-|b_j|\right)^{p-2}\|{a_j} \|^4.
\end{equation*}
If~\eqref{as:gh} held, then the choice $x=0$ and $y=ta_j$ would give
\begin{equation*}
  \|{\nabla^2f(ta_j)} \|
  \leq\|{\nabla^2f(0)} \|+\left( M_0+M_1\|{\nabla f(0)} \|\right) t\|{a_j} \|,
  \qquad t>0.
\end{equation*}
Since $p-2>1$, this contradicts the previous display as $t\to+\infty$.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
For any $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, $\|{u} \|=1$, and all sufficiently small $|t|$,
either pairwise condition gives
\begin{gather*}
  \frac{\|{\nabla^2 f(x+tu)-\nabla^2 f(x)} \|}{|t|}
  \leq M_0+M_1\|{\nabla f(x)} \|.
\end{gather*}
Taking $t\to0$ and then the supremum over $\|{u} \|=1$
proves~\eqref{as:td}.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Let $s=y-x$, $r=\|{s} \|\leq\rho$, and
$g(t)=\|{\nabla f(x+ts)} \|$. The function $g$ is absolutely continuous.
For almost every $t\in[0,1]$, condition~\eqref{as:fo} gives
\begin{gather*}
  g'(t)
  \leq r\|{\nabla^2 f(x+ts)} \|
  \leq r\left( L_0+L_1g(t)\right).
\end{gather*}
Gr\"onwall's inequality yields
\begin{gather*}
  g(t)
  \leq e^{L_1rt}\left( g(0)+L_0rt\right)
  \leq e^{L_1\rho}\left(\|{\nabla f(x)} \|+L_0\rho\right).
\end{gather*}
Using~\eqref{as:td} along the segment from $x$ to $y$, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla^2 f(y)-\nabla^2 f(x)} \|
  \leq r\int_0^1
  \left(\widehat M_0+\widehat M_1g(t)\right)\mathrm{d}t 
  \leq\left(
    \widehat M_0+\widehat M_1L_0\rho e^{L_1\rho}
    +\widehat M_1e^{L_1\rho}\|{\nabla f(x)} \|
  \right) r.
\end{gather*}
This is~\eqref{as:lh} with the stated constants.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:basic_pd_ms_step}
Suppose that $f$ is convex. For every accepted step of
Algorithm~\ref{alg:basic_pd_ms}, set $s_k:= x_{k+1}-x_k$. Then
\begin{gather}
  \frac{\tau_k}{2}\|{s_k} \|
  \leq\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|
  \leq\frac{3\tau_k}{2}\|{s_k} \|,
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_output_gradient}\\
  f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})
  \geq\max\left\lbrace\frac{\tau_k}{2}\|{s_k} \|^2,
              \frac{2\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|^2}{3\tau_k}\right\rbrace,
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_decrease}\\
  \|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|
  \leq\frac2{\sqrt3}\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_gradient_growth}
\end{gather}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
By the $\mathsf{MS}$ condition in~\eqref{eq:pd_ms_tests} 
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|
  \geq\tau_k\|{s_k} \|-\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})+\tau_ks_k} \|
  \geq\frac{\tau_k}{2}\|{s_k} \|,\\
  \|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|
  \leq\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})+\tau_ks_k} \|+\tau_k\|{s_k} \|
  \leq\frac{3\tau_k}{2}\|{s_k} \|.
\end{gather*}
we prove ~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_output_gradient}.
Squaring the $\mathsf{MS}$ condition and expanding the left-hand side gives
\begin{equation}
  \|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})+\tau_ks_k} \|^2
  =\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|^2
    +2\tau_k\left\langle\nabla f(x_{k+1}),s_k\right\rangle
    +\tau_k^2\|{s_k} \|^2
  \leq\frac{\tau_k^2}{4}\|{s_k} \|^2.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_squared_test}
\end{equation}
Next, by convexity,~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_squared_test}, and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_output_gradient},
\begin{gather*}
  f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})
  \geq-\left\langle\nabla f(x_{k+1}),s_k\right\rangle
  \geq\frac{\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|^2}{2\tau_k}
    +\frac{3\tau_k}{8}\|{s_k} \|^2\\
  \geq\frac{1}{2\tau_k}\left(\frac{\tau_k}{2}\|{s_k} \|\right)^2
    +\frac{3\tau_k}{8}\|{s_k} \|^2
  =\frac{\tau_k}{2}\|{s_k} \|^2.
\end{gather*}
Using instead $\|{s_k} \|\geq2\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|/(3\tau_k)$
from~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_output_gradient}, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})
  \geq\frac{\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|^2}{2\tau_k}
    +\frac{3\tau_k}{8}
       \left(\frac{2\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|}{3\tau_k}\right)^2
  =\frac{2\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|^2}{3\tau_k}.
\end{gather*}
This proves~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_decrease}.
For~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_gradient_growth}, convexity at both endpoints gives
\begin{equation*}
  \left\langle\nabla f(x_k),s_k\right\rangle
  \leq f(x_{k+1})-f(x_k)
  \leq\left\langle\nabla f(x_{k+1}),s_k\right\rangle.
\end{equation*}
Next, \eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_squared_test} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|^2+\frac34\tau_k^2\|{s_k} \|^2
  \leq-2\tau_k\left\langle\nabla f(x_{k+1}),s_k\right\rangle
  \leq-2\tau_k\left\langle\nabla f(x_k),s_k\right\rangle
  \leq2\tau_k\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|\|{s_k} \|.
\end{equation*}
Rearranging and completing the square gives
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|^2
  \leq2 \tau_k \|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|\|{s_k} \|
       -\frac34\tau_k^2\|{s_k} \|^2\\
  =\frac43\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|^2
   -\frac34\left(\tau_k\|{s_k} \|-\frac43\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|\right)^2
  \leq\frac43\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|^2.
\end{gather*}
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:pd_ms_backtracking}
Suppose that $f$ is convex,~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} holds, and
either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds.
Set
\begin{equation}
  \label{eq:backtrack_upper_bound}
  \overline\tau(x):=
  \begin{cases}
    \max\left\lbrace4\delta,2\sqrt{L(x)\|{\nabla f(x)} \|}\right\rbrace,
    & \text{under~\eqref{as:gh}},\\
    \max\left\lbrace4\delta,2\sqrt{L(x)\|{\nabla f(x)} \|},
      \frac{2\|{\nabla f(x)} \|}{\rho}\right\rbrace,
    & \text{under~\eqref{as:lh}}.
  \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Every trial of $\textnormal{\textsc{MSBacktrack}}$ with
$\tau\geq\overline\tau(x)$ satisfies both tests in~\eqref{eq:pd_ms_tests}.
Consequently, initialized with $\tau=\eta>0$, the algorithm terminates
after at most
\begin{equation*}
  1+\left\lceil\log_2\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{\overline\tau(x)}{\eta}\right\rbrace\right\rceil
\end{equation*}
trials, and its accepted parameter satisfies
\begin{equation*}
  \eta\leq\tau\leq\max\left\lbrace\eta,2\overline\tau(x)\right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Fix a trial parameter $\tau\geq\overline\tau(x)$.
By convexity and~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian}, $H(x)\succeq-\delta I$.
Since $\tau\geq4\delta$,
\begin{equation*}
  H(x)+\tau I\succeq(\tau-\delta)I
  \succeq\frac{3\tau}{4}I\succ0.
\end{equation*}
Thus $\mathsf{PD}(x,\tau)$ holds, and the linear system
$(H(x)+\tau I)s=-\nabla f(x)$ has a unique solution satisfying
\begin{equation*}
  \|{s} \|
  =\|{(H(x)+\tau I)^{-1}\nabla f(x)} \|
  \leq\frac{\|{\nabla f(x)} \|}{\tau-\delta}
  \leq\frac{2\|{\nabla f(x)} \|}{\tau}.
\end{equation*}
Under~\eqref{as:lh}, the definition of $\overline\tau(x)$ also gives
$\|{s} \|\leq\rho$.
The gradient remainder bound in Lemma~\ref{lem:global_taylor_remainders}
or Lemma~\ref{lem:local_taylor_remainders}, together
with~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} and the linear system, yields
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla f(x+s)+\tau s} \|
  =\|{\nabla f(x+s)-\nabla f(x)-H(x)s} \|\\
  \leq\frac{L(x)}2\|{s} \|^2+\delta\|{s} \|
  \leq\left(\frac{L(x)\|{\nabla f(x)} \|}{\tau}+\delta\right)\|{s} \|\\
  \leq\left(\frac\tau4+\frac\tau4\right)\|{s} \|
  =\frac\tau2\|{s} \|.
\end{gather*}
Hence $\mathsf{MS}(x,\tau,s)$ also holds.
The trial parameters are $2^j\eta$, $j=0,1,\ldots$, so the first index
with $2^j\eta\geq\overline\tau(x)$ gives the stated trial bound.
If no trial is rejected, the accepted parameter is $\tau=\eta$.
Otherwise, $\tau/2$ was rejected, so $\tau/2<\overline\tau(x)$ and
$\tau<2\overline\tau(x)$.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_damped_movement}
Suppose that $f$ is convex,~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} holds, and
either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds. Set
\begin{equation}
  r_0:=
  \begin{cases}
    \frac1{6\sqrt{M_1}},
    & \text{under~\eqref{as:gh}},\\
    \min\left\lbrace\frac\rho2,\frac1{6\sqrt{M_1}}\right\rbrace,
    & \text{under~\eqref{as:lh}},
  \end{cases}
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_movement_radius}
\end{equation}
where $1/\sqrt{M_1}=+\infty$ when $M_1=0$.
Suppose that $\textnormal{\textsc{MSBacktrack}}$, initialized at $x$ with
$\tau=\eta>0$, returns $(y,\tau)$. Set $s:= y-x$.
If at least one trial is rejected (equivalently $\tau>\eta$), then
\begin{equation}
  \|{s} \|>r_0
  \quad\text{or}\quad
  \tau\leq8\delta+24M_0\|{s} \|.
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_movement}
\end{equation}
If, in addition, $\tau\geq16\delta$, then
\begin{equation}
  \|{s} \|\geq\min\left\lbrace r_0,\frac{\tau}{48M_0}\right\rbrace.
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_movement_lower_bound}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
We prove~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_movement} by considering three cases.

First, if $\tau<4\delta$, then $\tau\leq8\delta+24M_0\|{s} \|$,
so the second inequality holds.

Second, if $\tau\geq4\delta$ and $\|{s} \|>r_0$, the first inequality holds.

It remains to consider the case $\tau\geq4\delta$ and $\|{s} \|\leq r_0$.
Since $\tau>\eta$, the trial with parameter $\tau/2$ was rejected.
Convexity and~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} give
\begin{equation}
  H(x)+\frac{\tau}{2}I
  \succeq\left(\frac{\tau}{2}-\delta\right) I
  \succeq\frac{\tau}{4}I\succ0,
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_rejected_matrix_bound}
\end{equation}
so this trial failed the $\mathsf{MS}$ test. Its step $s_{1/2}$ and the accepted
step $s$ satisfy
\begin{gather*}
  \left( H(x)+\frac{\tau}{2}I\right) s_{1/2}=-\nabla f(x),\\
  \left( H(x)+\tau I\right) s=-\nabla f(x).
\end{gather*}
Subtracting these equations gives
\begin{equation}
  s_{1/2}-s
  =\frac{\tau}{2}\left( H(x)+\frac{\tau}{2}I\right)^{-1}s,
  \qquad
  \|{s_{1/2}-s} \|\leq2\|{s} \|,
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_trial_difference}
\end{equation}
where the last inequality follows from~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_rejected_matrix_bound}.
For every $t\in[0,1]$,~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_trial_difference} gives
\begin{gather*}
  \|{x+ts_{1/2}-y} \|
  =\|{t(s_{1/2}-s)-(1-t)s} \|\\
  \leq t\|{s_{1/2}-s} \|+(1-t)\|{s} \|
  \leq(1+t)\|{s} \|\leq2\|{s} \|.
\end{gather*}
Under~\eqref{as:lh},~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_movement_radius} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \|{x-y} \|=\|{s} \|\leq r_0\leq\frac\rho2, \qquad
  \|{x+ts_{1/2}-y} \|\leq2\|{s} \|\leq2r_0\leq\rho.
\end{equation*}
Thus, applying~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} at $y$ gives
\begin{gather}
  \|{\nabla^2f(x+ts_{1/2})-\nabla^2f(x)} \|
  \leq\|{\nabla^2f(x+ts_{1/2})-\nabla^2f(y)} \|
  +\|{\nabla^2f(x)-\nabla^2f(y)} \| \notag\\
  \leq L(y)\left(\|{x+ts_{1/2}-y} \|+\|{x-y} \|\right)
  \leq3L(y)\|{s} \|.
\label{eq:ahpe_damped_hessian_variation}
\end{gather}
Since the trial with parameter $\tau/2$ fails the $\mathsf{MS}$ test, we have
\begin{equation}
  \frac{\tau}{4}\|{s_{1/2}} \|
  <\|{\nabla f(x+s_{1/2})+\frac{\tau}{2}s_{1/2}} \|.
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_failed_ms_test}
\end{equation}
The linear system for $s_{1/2}$ gives
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{\tau}{2}s_{1/2}=-\nabla f(x)-H(x)s_{1/2}.
\end{equation*}
Therefore,
\begin{gather}
  \nabla f(x+s_{1/2})+\frac{\tau}{2}s_{1/2}
  =\nabla f(x+s_{1/2})-\nabla f(x)-H(x)s_{1/2} \notag \\
  =\int_0^1\left(\nabla^2f(x+ts_{1/2})-H(x)\right) s_{1/2}dt.
\label{eq:ahpe_damped_residual_integral}
\end{gather}
Therefore, by~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_failed_ms_test},~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_residual_integral},~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_hessian_variation}, and~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian},
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{\tau}{4}\|{s_{1/2}} \|
  <\|{\int_0^1\left(\nabla^2f(x+ts_{1/2})-H(x)\right) s_{1/2}dt} \|
  \leq\left(\delta+3L(y)\|{s} \|\right)\|{s_{1/2}} \|.
\end{equation*}
Since this trial fails $\mathsf{MS}$, its step $s_{1/2}$ is nonzero.
The accepted $\mathsf{MS}$ test in~\eqref{eq:pd_ms_tests} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \|{\nabla f(y)} \|
  \leq\|{\nabla f(y)+\tau s} \|+\tau\|{s} \|
  \leq\frac{3\tau}{2}\|{s} \|.
\end{equation*}
Dividing by $\|{s_{1/2}} \|$ and using this bound, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \frac{\tau}{4}
  <\delta+3L(y)\|{s} \|
  =\delta+3M_0\|{s} \|+3M_1\|{\nabla f(y)} \|\|{s} \|\\
  \leq\delta+3M_0\|{s} \|+\frac92M_1\tau\|{s} \|^2
  \leq\delta+3M_0\|{s} \|+\frac{\tau}{8}.
\end{gather*}
The last inequality follows from $\|{s} \|\leq r_0$ and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_movement_radius}.
Indeed, if $M_1>0$, then
\begin{equation*}
  M_1\|{s} \|^2\leq M_1r_0^2
  \leq M_1\left(\frac1{6\sqrt{M_1}}\right)^2=\frac1{36}.
\end{equation*}
If $M_1=0$, then $M_1\|{s} \|^2=0$. Thus, in both cases,
\begin{equation*}
  \frac92M_1\tau\|{s} \|^2
  \leq \frac{\tau}{8}.
\end{equation*}
Rearranging proves~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_movement}.
Finally, if $\tau\geq16\delta$,~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_movement} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \|{s} \|
  \geq\min\left\lbrace r_0,\frac{\tau-8\delta}{24M_0}\right\rbrace
  \geq\min\left\lbrace r_0,\frac{\tau}{48M_0}\right\rbrace,
\end{equation*}
which proves~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_movement_lower_bound}.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:basic_pd_ms_rejection}
Suppose that $f$ is convex,~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} holds, and
either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds.
If iteration $k$ of Algorithm~\ref{alg:basic_pd_ms} rejects at least one trial,
then
\begin{equation}
  \tau_k\leq\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|).
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_rejection}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Set $s_k:= x_{k+1}-x_k$ and apply Lemma~\ref{lem:ahpe_damped_movement}
with $x=x_k$, $y=x_{k+1}$, $\eta=\eta_k$, and $\tau=\tau_k$.
If $\|{s_k} \|>r_0$, then~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_output_gradient}
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_threshold} give
\begin{equation*}
  \tau_k<\frac{2\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|}{r_0}
  \leq\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|).
\end{equation*}
If $\|{s_k} \|\leq r_0$,~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_movement}
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_output_gradient} imply
\begin{gather*}
  \tau_k\leq8\delta+24M_0\|{s_k} \|
  \leq8\delta+\frac{48M_0\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|}{\tau_k},\\
  \tau_k\leq4\delta+\sqrt{16\delta^2+48M_0\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|}
  \leq8\delta+\sqrt{48M_0\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|},
\end{gather*}
which proves~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_rejection}.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:basic_pd_ms_tracking}
Under the assumptions of Lemma~\ref{lem:basic_pd_ms_rejection}, suppose that
$m$ iterations of Algorithm~\ref{alg:basic_pd_ms} are completed and $f(x_m)>f^\ast$.
If $m_{\rm c}$ of these iterations are controlled, then
\begin{equation}
  m\leq\frac54m_{\rm c}
   +\log_2\frac{U_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_m)} \|)}.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_tracking_count}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_threshold},
$\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|)\leq U_k$ for every $k\geq0$.
The function $\Theta_{\rm c}$ is nondecreasing, and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_threshold} gives
$\Theta_{\rm c}(ag)\leq a\Theta_{\rm c}(g)$ for $g\geq0$ and $a\geq1$.

If iteration $k$ is controlled, then $\tau_k\leq\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|)$
by~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_controlled}. The definition of $U_{k+1}$
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_gradient_growth} give
\begin{equation*}
  U_{k+1}=\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|)
  \leq\frac2{\sqrt3}\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|)
  \leq\frac2{\sqrt3}U_k.
\end{equation*}
If iteration $k$ is not controlled, then
$\tau_k>\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|)$, so $U_{k+1}=\tau_k$ by definition.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:basic_pd_ms_rejection}, this iteration has no rejected trials,
so $\tau_k=\eta_k$.
For $k\geq1$, line~\ref{line:basic_pd_ms_eta_update} of
Algorithm~\ref{alg:basic_pd_ms}, applied at iteration $k-1$, gives
$\eta_k\leq\tau_{k-1}/2$.
Hence,
\begin{equation*}
  U_{k+1}=\tau_k=\eta_k\leq\frac{\tau_{k-1}}2\leq\frac{U_k}{2}.
\end{equation*}
For $k=0$, the same bound holds because
$U_1=\tau_0=\eta_0\leq U_0/2$. Applying these bounds over the $m_{\rm c}$ controlled iterations and
$m-m_{\rm c}$ remaining iterations gives
\begin{equation*}
  \Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_m)} \|)\leq U_m
  \leq U_0\left(\frac2{\sqrt3}\right)^{m_{\rm c}}2^{-(m-m_{\rm c})}.
\end{equation*}
Taking logarithms and rearranging, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
  m\leq\left(1+\log_2\frac2{\sqrt3}\right) m_{\rm c}
       +\log_2\frac{U_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_m)} \|)}.
\end{equation*}
Since $(2/\sqrt3)^4=16/9<2$, this
proves~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_tracking_count}.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:basic_pd_ms_controlled_count}
For the prefix and count of Lemma~\ref{lem:basic_pd_ms_tracking}, assume
in addition that $0<D<+\infty$. Then
\begin{equation}
  m_{\rm c}\leq\int_{f(x_m)-f^\ast}^{f(x_0)-f^\ast}\frac{1+\Phi(t)}t dt.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_controlled_count}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
For a controlled iteration, we have
\begin{gather*}
  f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_decrease}}{\geq}
  \frac{2\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|^2}{3\tau_k}
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_controlled}}{\geq}
  \frac{2\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|^2}
       {3\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|)}\\
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_threshold}}{=}
  \min\left\lbrace
      \frac{2\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|^2}
           {3\left(8\delta+\sqrt{48M_0\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|}\right)},
      \frac{r_0\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|}3
     \right\rbrace.
\end{gather*}
By convexity and Cauchy-Schwarz,
\begin{equation*}
  f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast
  \leq\left\langle\nabla f(x_{k+1}),x_{k+1}-x^\ast\right\rangle
  \leq\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|\|{x_{k+1}-x^\ast} \|
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_localization}}{\leq}
  2D\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|.
\end{equation*}
Substituting $\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|\geq\frac{f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast}{2D}$ gives
\begin{gather*}
  f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})
  \geq\min\left\lbrace
      \frac{(f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast)^2}
           {48\delta D^2+12\sqrt{6}\sqrt{M_0D^3(f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast)}},
      \frac{r_0(f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast)}{6D}
     \right\rbrace\\
  =\frac{f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast}{\Phi(f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast)}.
\end{gather*}
By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_decrease},
$f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast\leq f(x_k)-f^\ast$.
For every $t\in[f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast,f(x_k)-f^\ast]$,
the monotonicity of $t(1+\Phi(t))$ gives
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{1+\Phi(t)}t
  \geq\frac{(f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast)(1+\Phi(f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast))}{t^2}.
\end{equation*}
Thus, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \int_{f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast}^{f(x_k)-f^\ast}\frac{1+\Phi(t)}t dt 
  \geq(f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast)(1+\Phi(f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast))
       \int_{f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast}^{f(x_k)-f^\ast}\frac{dt}{t^2}\\
  =(f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast)(1+\Phi(f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast))
       \left(\frac1{f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast}-\frac1{f(x_k)-f^\ast}\right)\\
  =(1+\Phi(f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast))
        \frac{f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})}{f(x_k)-f^\ast}
  \geq\frac{1+\Phi(f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast)}{\Phi(f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast)+1}
  =1.
\end{gather*}
Summing over the controlled iterations
proves~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_controlled_count}.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:basic_pd_ms_convergence_appendix}
Suppose that $f$ is convex,~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} holds, and
either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds.
Define
\begin{equation}
  B:=\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{2D}{\rho},6\sqrt{M_1}D\right\rbrace,
  \qquad
  \varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}:=\max\left\lbrace\frac{M_0D^3}{B^2},\frac{\delta D^2}{B}\right\rbrace,
  \label{eq:app_basic_pd_ms_scales}
\end{equation}
where $\rho=+\infty$ under~\eqref{as:gh}.
For every $\varepsilon>0$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:basic_pd_ms} generates an iterate $x_N$
satisfying $f(x_N)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon$ within
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  N\leq 2+\log_2\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{2D\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}},
    \frac{\eta_0D^2}{\sqrt6 B\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}\right\rbrace
  +100B\log_+\frac{f(x_0)-f^\ast}{\max\{\varepsilon,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}\}}
    +80\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{\varepsilon}}+64\frac{\delta D^2}{\varepsilon}.
\end{aligned}
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_explicit_complexity}
\end{equation}
iterations.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Each search terminates by Lemma~\ref{lem:pd_ms_backtracking}.
Consider a prefix $x_0,\ldots,x_m$ with
$f(x_m)-f^\ast>\varepsilon$.
By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_localization},
$\|{\nabla f(x_m)} \|>\varepsilon/(2D)$.
Combining~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_tracking_count}
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_controlled_count} gives
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  m&\leq\frac54\int_{f(x_m)-f^\ast}^{f(x_0)-f^\ast}\frac{1+\Phi(t)}t dt
       +\log_2\frac{U_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_m)} \|)}\\
  &\leq\frac54\int_\varepsilon^{f(x_0)-f^\ast}\frac{1+\Phi(t)}t dt
       +\log_{2,+}\frac{U_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\varepsilon/(2D))}.
\end{aligned}
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_prefix_count}
\end{equation}
Let $N$ be the first index with
$f(x_N)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon$.
If $N\geq1$, then $f(x_{N-1})-f^\ast>\varepsilon$. Therefore,
\begin{equation}
  N\leq1+\frac54\int_\varepsilon^{f(x_0)-f^\ast}\frac{1+\Phi(t)}t dt
       +\log_{2,+}\frac{U_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\varepsilon/(2D))}.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_integral_count}
\end{equation}
We begin with bounding integral term in~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_integral_count}. 

By~\eqref{eq:app_basic_pd_ms_scales} and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_count_scale},
$1+\Phi(t)\leq79B$ for $t\geq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$.
For $0<t\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$, we have
\begin{gather*}
  \max\left\lbrace\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{t}},\frac{\delta D^2}{t}\right\rbrace
  \geq B\geq\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{D}{r_0}\right\rbrace,
  1+\Phi(t)
  \leq(12\sqrt{6}+1)\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{t}}
       +49\frac{\delta D^2}{t}.
\end{gather*}
If $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}\leq\varepsilon<f(x_0)-f^\ast$, the whole integration interval
lies above $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$, so
\begin{equation*}
  \int_\varepsilon^{f(x_0)-f^\ast}\frac{1+\Phi(t)}t dt
  \leq79B\int_\varepsilon^{f(x_0)-f^\ast}\frac{dt}t
  =79B\log\frac{f(x_0)-f^\ast}{\varepsilon}.
\end{equation*}
If $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}\leq f(x_0)-f^\ast$, split the integral as
\begin{gather*}
  \int_\varepsilon^{f(x_0)-f^\ast}\frac{1+\Phi(t)}t dt
  =\int_\varepsilon^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}\frac{1+\Phi(t)}t dt
   +\int_{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}^{f(x_0)-f^\ast}\frac{1+\Phi(t)}t dt\\
  \leq(12\sqrt{6}+1)\sqrt{M_0D^3}
       \int_\varepsilon^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}\frac{dt}{t^{3/2}}
    +49\delta D^2\int_\varepsilon^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}\frac{dt}{t^2}
    +79B\int_{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}^{f(x_0)-f^\ast}\frac{dt}t\\
  =(24\sqrt{6}+2)\sqrt{M_0D^3}
      \left(\frac1{\sqrt\varepsilon}-\frac1{\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}}\right)
    +49\delta D^2\left(\frac1\varepsilon-\frac1{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}\right)
    +79B\log\frac{f(x_0)-f^\ast}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}\\
  \leq(24\sqrt{6}+2)\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{\varepsilon}}
    +49\frac{\delta D^2}{\varepsilon}
    +79B\log\frac{f(x_0)-f^\ast}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}.
\end{gather*}
If $0<\varepsilon<f(x_0)-f^\ast<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$, the whole interval lies below
$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$, so
\begin{gather*}
  \int_\varepsilon^{f(x_0)-f^\ast}\frac{1+\Phi(t)}t dt
  \leq(12\sqrt{6}+1)\sqrt{M_0D^3}
       \int_\varepsilon^{f(x_0)-f^\ast}\frac{dt}{t^{3/2}}
    +49\delta D^2\int_\varepsilon^{f(x_0)-f^\ast}\frac{dt}{t^2}\\
  =(24\sqrt{6}+2)\sqrt{M_0D^3}
      \left(\frac1{\sqrt\varepsilon}-\frac1{\sqrt{f(x_0)-f^\ast}}\right)
    +49\delta D^2\left(\frac1\varepsilon-\frac1{f(x_0)-f^\ast}\right)\\
  \leq(24\sqrt{6}+2)\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{\varepsilon}}
    +49\frac{\delta D^2}{\varepsilon}.
\end{gather*}
Here $\log_+\frac{f(x_0)-f^\ast}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}=0$ by definition.

Combining the three cases yields
\begin{equation}
  \int_\varepsilon^{f(x_0)-f^\ast}\frac{1+\Phi(t)}t dt
  \leq79B\log_+\frac{f(x_0)-f^\ast}{\max\{\varepsilon,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}\}}
  \quad+(24\sqrt{6}+2)\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{\varepsilon}}
    +49\frac{\delta D^2}{\varepsilon}.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_clipped_integral}
\end{equation}
Now, we need to bound the last term in~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_integral_count}.

For $g_2\geq g_1>0$,~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_threshold} gives
$\Theta_{\rm c}(g_2)\leq(g_2/g_1)\Theta_{\rm c}(g_1)$.
Together with monotonicity of $\Theta_{\rm c}$, this yields
\begin{equation*}
  \log_{2,+}\frac{U_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\varepsilon/(2D))}
  \leq\log_{2,+}\frac{U_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}/(2D))}
    +\log_{2,+}\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{\varepsilon}.
\end{equation*}
If $\varepsilon\geq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$, then $\log_{2,+}(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}/\varepsilon)=0$.
For $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$, we have
\begin{gather*}
  \log_2\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{\varepsilon}
  \leq3\sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{\varepsilon}}
  =\frac3B\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{\varepsilon}},
  \qquad\text{if }\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}=\frac{M_0D^3}{B^2},\\
  \log_2\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{\varepsilon}
  \leq2\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{\varepsilon}
  =\frac2B\frac{\delta D^2}{\varepsilon},
  \qquad\text{if }\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}=\frac{\delta D^2}{B}.
\end{gather*}
Since $B\geq1$,
\begin{equation}
  \log_{2,+}\frac{U_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\varepsilon/(2D))}
  \leq\log_{2,+}\frac{U_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}/(2D))}
    +3\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{\varepsilon}}+2\frac{\delta D^2}{\varepsilon}.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_clipped_tracking}
\end{equation}
Substituting~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_clipped_integral}
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_clipped_tracking}
into~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_integral_count}, and using
\begin{equation*}
  \frac54\cdot79\leq100,
  \qquad
  \frac54(24\sqrt{6}+2)+3\leq80,
  \qquad
  \frac54\cdot49+2\leq64,
\end{equation*}
we obtain
\begin{equation*}
  N\leq 2+\log_{2,+}\frac{U_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}/(2D))}
  +100B\log_+\frac{f(x_0)-f^\ast}{\max\{\varepsilon,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}\}}
    +80\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{\varepsilon}}+64\frac{\delta D^2}{\varepsilon}.
\end{equation*}
Recall that $\Theta_{\rm c}$ is nondecreasing and $\Theta_{\rm c}(ag)\leq a\Theta_{\rm c}(g)$
for $a\geq1$.
Thus,
\begin{gather*}
  \Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|)
  \leq\Theta_{\rm c}\left(
    \max\left\lbrace1,\frac{2D\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}\right\rbrace
    \frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{2D}\right)
  \leq\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{2D\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}\right\rbrace
    \Theta_{\rm c}\left(\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{2D}\right).
\end{gather*}
If $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}=M_0D^3/B^2$
\begin{equation*}
  \Theta_{\rm c}\left(\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{2D}\right)
  \geq\sqrt{\frac{24M_0\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}D}
  =\frac{2\sqrt6 B\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{D^2}.
\end{equation*}
Otherwise $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}=\delta D^2/B$
\begin{equation*}
  \Theta_{\rm c}\left(\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{2D}\right)
  \geq8\delta=\frac{8B\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{D^2}
  \geq\frac{2\sqrt6 B\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{D^2}.
\end{equation*}
Since $U_0=\max\left\lbrace2\eta_0,\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|)\right\rbrace$, these estimates give
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  \log_{2,+}\frac{U_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}/(2D))}
  &=\log_2\max\left\lbrace1,
    \frac{\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|)}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}/(2D))},
    \frac{2\eta_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}/(2D))}\right\rbrace\\
  &\leq\log_2\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{2D\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}},
    \frac{\eta_0D^2}{\sqrt6 B\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}\right\rbrace.
\end{aligned}
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_initial_log_bound}
\end{equation}
Substituting~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_initial_log_bound} into the bound for $N$
proves~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_explicit_complexity}.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:basic_pd_ms_rates}
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:basic_pd_ms_convergence_appendix},
suppose that $0<D<+\infty$.
Define
\begin{equation*}
  \ell_0:=\max\left\lbrace
    1,\frac{2D\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}},
    \frac{\eta_0D^2}{\sqrt6 B\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}
  \right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
For every $k\geq0$ with $f(x_k)-f^\ast>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$,
\begin{equation}
  f(x_k)-f^\ast\leq\left( f(x_0)-f^\ast\right)
    \exp\left(-\frac{(k-\log_2\ell_0)_+}{100B}\right),
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_far_rate_entry}
\end{equation}
where we write $(t)_+:=\max\left\lbrace0,t\right\rbrace$.
If $f(x_k)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$, the subsequent iterates satisfy
\begin{equation}
  f(x_{k+n})-f^\ast
  \leq\frac{7396M_0D^3}{\bigl(B+(n-\log_2\ell_0)_+\bigr)^2}
    +\frac{140\delta D^2}{B+(n-\log_2\ell_0)_+},
  \qquad n=0,1,\ldots,
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_near_rate_entry}
\end{equation}
where $t_+:=\max\left\lbrace t,0\right\rbrace$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
If $f(x_k)-f^\ast>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$,~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_prefix_count} gives
\begin{equation*}
  k\leq\frac54\int_{f(x_k)-f^\ast}^{f(x_0)-f^\ast}
    \frac{1+\Phi(t)}t dt
    +\log_2\frac{U_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|)}.
\end{equation*}
For $t\geq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$, definitions~\eqref{eq:app_basic_pd_ms_scales}
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_count_scale} give
\begin{gather*}
  \Phi(t)\leq\max\left\lbrace
    6B,12\sqrt6\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}}
      +48\frac{\delta D^2}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}
  \right\rbrace
  \leq\max\left\lbrace6B,(12\sqrt6+48)B\right\rbrace
  =(12\sqrt6+48)B.
\end{gather*}
Therefore, $1+\Phi(t)\leq79B$.
By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_localization}, monotonicity of $\Theta_{\rm c}$,
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_initial_log_bound},
\begin{equation*}
  \log_2\frac{U_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|)}
  \leq\log_{2,+}\frac{U_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}/(2D))}
  \leq\log_2\ell_0.
\end{equation*}
Substituting these bounds yields
\begin{gather*}
  k\leq\frac54\cdot79B
    \int_{f(x_k)-f^\ast}^{f(x_0)-f^\ast}\frac{dt}t+\log_2\ell_0\\
  =\frac{395}{4}B\log\frac{f(x_0)-f^\ast}{f(x_k)-f^\ast}+\log_2\ell_0
  \leq100B\log\frac{f(x_0)-f^\ast}{f(x_k)-f^\ast}+\log_2\ell_0.
\end{gather*}
Rearranging and using $f(x_k)\leq f(x_0)$ when $k\leq\log_2\ell_0$
proves~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_far_rate_entry}.

Now suppose that $f(x_k)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$.
Let $n_{\mathrm{tr}}\leq k$ be the first index with $f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}})-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$.
For $n\geq0$ with $f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})>f^\ast$,
the first inequality in~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_prefix_count},
applied from iteration $n_{\mathrm{tr}}$, gives
\begin{equation}
  n\leq\frac54\int_{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}^{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}})-f^\ast}
    \frac{1+\Phi(t)}t dt
    +\log_2\frac{U_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}}}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})} \|)}.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_segment_count}
\end{equation}
For $0<t\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$, the definitions of $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$ and $B$ give
\begin{equation*}
  \max\left\lbrace\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{t}},\frac{\delta D^2}{t}\right\rbrace
  \geq B=\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{D}{r_0}\right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
Hence, by the definition of $\Phi$ in~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_count_scale},
\begin{gather*}
  1+\Phi(t)\leq1+12\sqrt6\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{t}}
    +48\frac{\delta D^2}{t}
  \leq(12\sqrt6+1)\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{t}}
    +49\frac{\delta D^2}{t}.
\end{gather*}
Since $0<f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast\leq f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}})-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$,
\begin{gather*}
  \int_{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}^{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}})-f^\ast}\frac{1+\Phi(t)}t dt
  \leq(12\sqrt6+1)\sqrt{M_0D^3}
    \int_{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}^{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}})-f^\ast}\frac{dt}{t^{3/2}}
    +49\delta D^2\int_{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}^{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}})-f^\ast}\frac{dt}{t^2}\\
  =(24\sqrt6+2)\sqrt{M_0D^3}
    \left(\frac1{\sqrt{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}}-\frac1{\sqrt{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}})-f^\ast}}\right)\\
  +49\delta D^2\left(\frac1{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}-\frac1{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}})-f^\ast}\right)\\
  \leq(24\sqrt6+2)\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}}
    +49\frac{\delta D^2}{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}.
\end{gather*}
To bound the logarithm in~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_segment_count}, first express
$U_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}}$ through $\Theta_{\rm c}$.
If there is no controlled iteration before $n_{\mathrm{tr}}$, the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:basic_pd_ms_tracking} gives $U_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}}\leq U_0$.
Otherwise, let $i<n_{\mathrm{tr}}$ be the last controlled iteration. Then
\begin{equation*}
  U_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}}\leq U_{i+1}=\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_{i+1})} \|).
\end{equation*}
Next, by 
$f(x_0)-f^\ast>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}
=\max\left\lbrace M_0D^3/B^2,\delta D^2/B\right\rbrace$
\begin{equation*}
  \delta\leq\frac{B(f(x_0)-f^\ast)}{D^2},
  \qquad
  M_0\leq\frac{B^2(f(x_0)-f^\ast)}{D^3}.
\end{equation*}
By the definition of $B$,
\begin{equation*}
  \max\left\lbrace\frac4\rho,12\sqrt{M_1}\right\rbrace
  =\frac2D\max\left\lbrace\frac{2D}{\rho},6\sqrt{M_1}D\right\rbrace
  \leq\frac{2B}{D}.
\end{equation*}
If $\|{\nabla f(x_{i+1})} \|<(f(x_0)-f^\ast)/D$, then $B\geq1$ gives $\|{\nabla f(x_{i+1})} \|<B\frac{f(x_0)-f^\ast}{D}$.

Otherwise, since iteration $i$ is controlled, by~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_decrease},~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_controlled},
and the definition of $\Theta_{\rm c}$
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla f(x_{i+1})} \|
  \leq\frac32(f(x_0)-f^\ast)
  \max\left\lbrace
    \frac{8\delta}{\|{\nabla f(x_{i+1})} \|}
      +\sqrt{\frac{48M_0}{\|{\nabla f(x_{i+1})} \|}},
    \frac4\rho,12\sqrt{M_1}
  \right\rbrace\\
  \leq\frac{3(8+\sqrt{48})B(f(x_0)-f^\ast)}{2D}
  \leq\frac{23B(f(x_0)-f^\ast)}{D}.
\end{gather*}
Thus, 
\begin{equation*}
  \|{\nabla f(x_{i+1})} \|
  \leq23B\frac{f(x_0)-f^\ast}{D}
  \leq23B\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|.
\end{equation*}
Substituting into $\Theta_{\rm c}$ and using its monotonicity and
$\Theta_{\rm c}(ag)\leq a\Theta_{\rm c}(g)$ for $a\geq1$, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  U_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}}\leq\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_{i+1})} \|)
  \leq\Theta_{\rm c}(23B\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|) 
  \leq23B\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|)
  \leq23B U_0.
\end{gather*}
Using this bound, $\|{\nabla f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})} \|\geq(f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast)/(2D)$,
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_clipped_tracking}
with~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_initial_log_bound}, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \log_2\frac{U_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}}}{\Theta_{\rm c}(\|{\nabla f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})} \|)}
  \leq\log_2(23B)
    +\log_{2,+}\frac{U_0}{\Theta_{\rm c}((f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast)/(2D))}\\
  \leq\log_2\ell_0+\log_2(23B)
    +3\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}}
    +2\frac{\delta D^2}{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}.
\end{gather*}
Substitution into~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_segment_count} yields
\begin{equation}
  n\leq\log_2\ell_0+\log_2(23B)
    +80\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}}
    +64\frac{\delta D^2}{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_near_segment_count}
\end{equation}
The definition of $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$ and $f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$ imply
\begin{equation*}
  B\leq\max\left\lbrace
    \sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}},
    \frac{\delta D^2}{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}\right\rbrace,
  \qquad \log_2(23B)\leq5B.
\end{equation*}
Inequality~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_near_segment_count} therefore gives
\begin{gather*}
  B+(n-\log_2\ell_0)_+
  \leq6B+80\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}}
    +64\frac{\delta D^2}{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}\\
  \leq86\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}}
    +70\frac{\delta D^2}{f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast}.
\end{gather*}
Multiplying by $f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast$ and using $2ab\leq a^2+b^2$, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \left( B+(n-\log_2\ell_0)_+\right)\left( f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast\right)
  \leq86\sqrt{M_0D^3\left( f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast\right)}+70\delta D^2\\
  \leq\frac{\left( B+(n-\log_2\ell_0)_+\right)\left( f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast\right)}{2}
    +\frac{3698M_0D^3}{B+(n-\log_2\ell_0)_+}+70\delta D^2,\\
  f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})-f^\ast
  \leq\frac{7396M_0D^3}{\left( B+(n-\log_2\ell_0)_+\right)^2}
    +\frac{140\delta D^2}{B+(n-\log_2\ell_0)_+}.
\end{gather*}
Since $f(x_{k+n})\leq f(x_{n_{\mathrm{tr}}+n})$,
this proves~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_near_rate_entry}.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:basic_pd_ms_oracle_complexity}
Let $N:=\min\left\lbrace k\geq0:f(x_k)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon\right\rbrace$ and $g_0 = \|\nabla f(x_0)\|$.
The total number of rejected trials of Algorithm~\ref{alg:basic_pd_ms} before obtaining $x_N$,
including failed $\mathsf{PD}$ tests, is at most
\begin{equation}
  \frac54(N-1)+4
    +\log_{2,+}\frac{Bg_0}{D\eta_0}
    +\log_{2,+}\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{\varepsilon}.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_total_backtracking}
\end{equation}
Thus, the total number of gradient evaluations and rejected trials is
bounded by
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal{O}\bigg(1+\log\ell_0
    +\log_+\frac{Bg_0}{D\eta_0}
    +B\log_+\frac{f(x_0)-f^\ast}{\max\left\lbrace\varepsilon,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace}
    +\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{\varepsilon}}+\frac{\delta D^2}{\varepsilon}\bigg).
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_total_complexity}
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Let $b_j$ be the number of rejected trials on iteration $j$. Then, $b_0 = \log_2 \tfrac{\tau_0}{\eta_0}$ and $\tau_j = 2^{b_j}\eta_j$. Let $g_j = \|\nabla f(x_j)\|$ Therefore, for $j \geq 1$ by line~\ref{line:basic_pd_ms_eta_update} of Algorithm~\ref{alg:basic_pd_ms}
  \begin{equation*}
    b_j = \log_2 \frac{\tau_j}{\eta_j} = \log_2 \frac{2 \tau_j}{\tau_{j-1} \min \left\lbrace 1, g_j/g_{j-1}\right\rbrace} = 1 + \log_2 \frac{\tau_j}{\tau_{j-1}} + \log_2 \max\left\lbrace 1, \frac{g_{j-1}}{g_{j}}\right\rbrace.
  \end{equation*}
  Next, let us sum the number of rejected trials to obtain $x_N$
  \begin{equation*}
    \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} b_j = \log_2 \frac{\tau_0}{\eta_0} + (N - 1) + \log_2 \frac{\tau_{N-1}}{\tau_{0}} + \sum_{j=1}^{N-1} \log_{2, +} \frac{g_{j-1}}{g_{j}}.
  \end{equation*}
  Let us bound the last sum 
  \begin{equation*}
    \sum_{j=1}^{N-1} \log_{2, +} \frac{g_{j-1}}{g_{j}} = \sum_{j=1}^{N-1} \left(  \log_{2, +} \frac{g_{j}}{g_{j-1}} + \log_2 \frac{g_{j-1}}{g_j} \right)  = \sum_{j=1}^{N-1} \log_{2, +} \frac{g_{j}}{g_{j-1}} + \log_2 \frac{g_0}{g_{N-1}}
  \end{equation*}
  Therefore, 
  \begin{equation}
    \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_rejections_boundary}
    \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} b_j = N - 1 + \log_2 \frac{g_0 \tau_{N-1}}{\eta_0 g_{N-1}} + \sum_{j=1}^{N-1} \log_{2, +} \frac{g_{j}}{g_{j-1}}.
  \end{equation}
  By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_gradient_growth}, we have $g_j \leq (2/\sqrt{3}) g_{j-1}$. Therefore,
  \begin{equation}
    \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_gradient_log_sum}
     \sum_{j=1}^{N-1} \log_{2, +} \frac{g_{j}}{g_{j-1}} \leq (N-1) \log_{2, +} \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \leq \frac{N-1}{4}.
  \end{equation}
  Now, it remains to bound $\log_{2, + } (\tau_{N-1}/g_{N-1})$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:pd_ms_backtracking}, every accepted $\tau$ satisfies 
  \begin{equation*}
    \tau_j \leq \max \left\lbrace \eta_j, 8 \delta, 4 \sqrt{L(x_j)g_j}, \frac{4 g_j}{\rho}\right\rbrace.
  \end{equation*}
  Therefore,
  \begin{equation}
    \label{eq:app_tau_g_bound}
    \frac{\tau_j}{g_j} \leq \max \left\lbrace \frac{\eta_j}{g_j}, \frac{8 \delta}{g_j}, 4 \sqrt{\frac{M_0}{g_j} + M_1}, \frac{4}{\rho}\right\rbrace.
  \end{equation}
By the definitions~\eqref{eq:app_basic_pd_ms_scales} of $B$ and $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$
\begin{equation*}
  \delta\leq\frac{B\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{D^2},
  \qquad M_0\leq\frac{B^2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{D^3},
  \qquad M_1\leq\frac{B^2}{36D^2},
  \qquad \frac1\rho\leq\frac{B}{2D}.
\end{equation*}
Next, by definition, $N$ is the first iteration, such that $f(x_N) - f^\ast \leq \varepsilon$. Then for $j<N$ we have $g_j \geq \varepsilon / (2D)$. Therefore, 
\begin{gather*}
  \frac{8\delta}{g_j}
  \leq\frac{16\delta D}{\varepsilon}
  \leq\frac{16B}{D}\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{\varepsilon},
\qquad   \frac4\rho\leq\frac{2B}{D}\leq\frac{16B}{D}\\
  4\sqrt{\frac{M_0}{g_j}+M_1}
  \leq4\sqrt{\frac{2M_0D}{\varepsilon}+M_1}
  \leq\frac{4B}{D}\sqrt{2\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{\varepsilon}+\frac1{36}}
  \leq\frac{16B}{D}\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{\varepsilon}\right\rbrace,
\end{gather*}
Moreover, for $j\geq1$, the update for $\eta_j$ gives
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{\eta_j}{g_j}
  =\frac{\tau_{j-1}}{2g_{j-1}}
    \min\left\lbrace1,\frac{g_{j-1}}{g_j}\right\rbrace
  \leq\frac{\tau_{j-1}}{2g_{j-1}}.
\end{equation*}
Substituting these estimates
into~\eqref{eq:app_tau_g_bound} gives for $1\leq j<N$
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{\tau_0}{g_0}
  \leq\max\left\lbrace\frac{\eta_0}{g_0},\frac{16B}{D}\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{\varepsilon}\right\rbrace\right\rbrace,
  \quad
  \frac{\tau_j}{g_j}
  \leq\max\left\lbrace\frac{\tau_{j-1}}{2g_{j-1}},\frac{16B}{D}\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{\varepsilon}\right\rbrace\right\rbrace. 
\end{equation*}
Induction therefore gives
\begin{equation}
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_oracle_normalized_bound}
  \frac{\tau_j}{g_j}
  \leq\max\left\lbrace\frac{\eta_0}{g_0},\frac{16B}{D}\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{\varepsilon}\right\rbrace\right\rbrace,
  \qquad 0\leq j<N.
\end{equation}
Finally, by combining~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_rejections_boundary},~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_gradient_log_sum}, and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_oracle_normalized_bound}, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
   \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} b_j \leq\frac54(N-1)
    +\log_2\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{16Bg_0}{D\eta_0}\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}{\varepsilon}\right\rbrace\right\rbrace\\
  \leq\frac54(N-1)+4
    +\log_{2,+}\frac{Bg_0}{D\eta_0}
    +\log_{2,+}\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}\varepsilon.
\end{gather*}
This proves~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_total_backtracking}.

Each trial requires at most one
new gradient evaluation. Hence, the total number of gradient
evaluations is at most $1+N+\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}b_j$. Next, by the definition of $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$, we have $\max\left\lbrace
    \sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}},
    \frac{\delta D^2}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}
\right\rbrace=B\geq1$. Using $\log_2 t\leq\min\left\lbrace2\sqrt t,t\right\rbrace$ for $t\geq1$, we obtain $\log_{2,+}\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}\varepsilon \leq2\sqrt{\frac{M_0D^3}{\varepsilon}}+\frac{\delta D^2}{\varepsilon}$. Combining these bounds with~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_complexity}
proves~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_total_complexity}.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:basic_pd_ms_strong_step}
Under~\eqref{as:basic_pd_ms_strong}, every completed iteration of
Algorithm~\ref{alg:basic_pd_ms} satisfies
\begin{gather}
  f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast
  \leq\left(\frac{3\tau_k}{3\tau_k+2\mu}\right)^2
       (f(x_k)-f^\ast),
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_step}\\
  \|{s_k} \|\leq
  \frac{\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|}{\mu+\tau_k/2}
  \leq\frac{\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|}\mu.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_length}
\end{gather}
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_squared_test},
\begin{equation*}
  -\left\langle\nabla f(x_{k+1}),s_k\right\rangle
  \geq\frac{\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|^2}{2\tau_k}
    +\frac{3\tau_k}{8}\|{s_k} \|^2.
\end{equation*}
Apply~\eqref{as:basic_pd_ms_strong} at $x_{k+1}$, then
use~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_output_gradient}
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_gap}:
\begin{gather*}
  f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})
  \geq-\left\langle\nabla f(x_{k+1}),s_k\right\rangle+\frac\mu2\|{s_k} \|^2
  \geq\frac{\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|^2}{2\tau_k}
    +\left(\frac{3\tau_k}{8}+\frac\mu2\right)\|{s_k} \|^2\\
  \geq\left(\frac1{2\tau_k}
      +\frac4{9\tau_k^2}\left(\frac{3\tau_k}{8}+\frac\mu2\right)\right)
      \|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|^2
  =\left(\frac2{3\tau_k}+\frac{2\mu}{9\tau_k^2}\right)
      \|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|^2\\
  \geq\left(\frac{4\mu}{3\tau_k}+\frac{4\mu^2}{9\tau_k^2}\right)
      (f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast).
\end{gather*}
The last inequality uses~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_gap} at $x_{k+1}$:
\begin{equation*}
  \|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})} \|^2
  \geq2\mu(f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast).
\end{equation*}
Adding $f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast$ to the bound for $f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})$
and completing the square gives
\begin{gather*}
  f(x_k)-f^\ast
  \geq\left(1+\frac{4\mu}{3\tau_k}+\frac{4\mu^2}{9\tau_k^2}\right)
      (f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast)\\
  =\left(1+\frac{2\mu}{3\tau_k}\right)^2
      (f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast),
\end{gather*}
which is~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_step}.
For~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_length}, recall that $s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k$.
Strong convexity gives
\begin{equation*}
  \mu\|{s_k} \|^2
  \leq\left\langle\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k),s_k\right\rangle.
\end{equation*}
The accepted $\mathsf{MS}$ test~\eqref{eq:pd_ms_tests} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})+\tau_k s_k} \|
  \leq\frac{\tau_k}{2}\|{s_k} \|.
\end{equation*}
Hence, by Cauchy-Schwarz,
\begin{gather*}
  \left\langle\nabla f(x_{k+1}),s_k\right\rangle
  =\left\langle\nabla f(x_{k+1})+\tau_k s_k,s_k\right\rangle-\tau_k\|{s_k} \|^2\\
  \leq\|{\nabla f(x_{k+1})+\tau_k s_k} \|\|{s_k} \|
    -\tau_k\|{s_k} \|^2
  \leq\frac{\tau_k}{2}\|{s_k} \|^2-\tau_k\|{s_k} \|^2
  =-\frac{\tau_k}{2}\|{s_k} \|^2.
\end{gather*}
Combining the two bounds and applying Cauchy-Schwarz once more gives
\begin{gather*}
  \mu\|{s_k} \|^2
  \leq-\frac{\tau_k}{2}\|{s_k} \|^2-\left\langle\nabla f(x_k),s_k\right\rangle,\\
  \left(\mu+\frac{\tau_k}{2}\right)\|{s_k} \|^2
  \leq-\left\langle\nabla f(x_k),s_k\right\rangle
  \leq\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|\|{s_k} \|.
\end{gather*}
Dividing by $\|{s_k} \|>0$ and using $\tau_k>0$ gives
\begin{equation*}
  \|{s_k} \|\leq\frac{\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|}{\mu+\tau_k/2}
  \leq\frac{\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|}\mu.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:basic_pd_ms_strong_global}
Suppose that~\eqref{as:basic_pd_ms_strong}
and~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} hold, and either~\eqref{as:gh}
or~\eqref{as:lh} holds. Define
\begin{equation}
  \overline\tau:=\max\left\lbrace
    \eta_0,\ 8\delta+48M_0\sqrt{\frac{2(f(x_0)-f^\ast)}\mu},
    \frac{2(f(x_0)-f^\ast)}{r_0^2}\right\rbrace.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_scale}
\end{equation}
Every completed iteration satisfies $\tau_k\leq\overline\tau$, and
\begin{equation}
  f(x_k)-f^\ast
  \leq\left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^{2k}
       (f(x_0)-f^\ast),\qquad k\geq0.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_global_rate}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
All searches terminate by Lemma~\ref{lem:pd_ms_backtracking}.
We prove $\tau_k\leq\overline\tau$ by induction.

Suppose that on iteration $k$ at least one trial is rejected, so $\tau_k>\eta_k$. If $\|{s_k} \|\leq r_0$, then~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_movement}
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_localization} give
\begin{gather*}
  \tau_k\leq8\delta_k+24M_0\|{s_k} \|
  \leq8\delta+24M_0\left(\|{x_k-x^\ast} \|
                         +\|{x_{k+1}-x^\ast} \|\right)\\
  \leq8\delta+48M_0\sqrt{\frac{2(f(x_0)-f^\ast)}\mu}
  \leq\overline\tau.
\end{gather*}
If $\|{s_k} \|>r_0$, then~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_decrease} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{\tau_k}{2}r_0^2
  <\frac{\tau_k}{2}\|{s_k} \|^2
  \leq f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\leq f(x_0)-f^\ast,
\end{equation*}
so again $\tau_k\leq\overline\tau$. 

Now, let's assume that in iteration $k$ there is no rejection.
For $k=0$, the accepted value is $\tau_0=\eta_0\leq\overline\tau$.
For $k\geq1$, line~\ref{line:basic_pd_ms_eta_update} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \tau_k=\eta_k\leq\frac{\tau_{k-1}}2\leq\overline\tau.
\end{equation*}
Thus the induction closes. Since $0<\tau_k\leq\overline\tau$,
\begin{gather*}
  \left(\frac{3\tau_k}{3\tau_k+2\mu}\right)^2
  =\left(1-\frac{2\mu}{3\tau_k+2\mu}\right)^2 
  \leq\left(1-\frac{2\mu}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^2
  =\left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^2.
\end{gather*}
Substitution into~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_step} and iteration
prove~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_global_rate}.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:basic_pd_ms_strong_gradient_complexity}
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:basic_pd_ms_strong_global},
let $0<\varepsilon<f(x_0)-f^\ast$ and
$N:=\min\left\lbrace k\geq0:f(x_k)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon\right\rbrace$.
The total number of gradient evaluations before obtaining $x_N$ is at most
\begin{equation}
  1+\frac94N
  +\log_{2,+}\left(\frac{\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}{\eta_0}
    \max\left\lbrace\frac{24M_0}{\mu}+\frac{8\delta}{\sqrt{2\mu\varepsilon}},
      \frac2{r_0}\right\rbrace\right).
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_gradient_cost}
\end{equation}
Consequently, it is bounded by
\begin{equation*}
  1+\frac94\left\lceil
    \frac{\log((f(x_0)-f^\ast)/\varepsilon)}
         {2\log\left(1+\frac{2\mu}{3\overline\tau}\right)}
  \right\rceil
  +\log_{2,+}\left(\frac{\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}{\eta_0}
    \max\left\lbrace\frac{24M_0}{\mu}+\frac{8\delta}{\sqrt{2\mu\varepsilon}},
      \frac2{r_0}\right\rbrace\right).
\end{equation*}
For $\delta=0$, the logarithmic term in~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_gradient_cost}
is independent of $\varepsilon$, and the bound holds for any $N\geq1$ completed
iterations.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Let $g_k:=\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|$ and let $b_k$ count the rejected trials
on iteration $k$.
By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_rejections_boundary} and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_gradient_log_sum},
\begin{equation*}
  \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}b_k
  \leq\frac54(N-1)+\log_2\frac{g_0\tau_{N-1}}{\eta_0g_{N-1}}.
\end{equation*}
We prove by induction that
\begin{equation}
  \frac{\tau_k}{g_k}
  \leq\max\left\lbrace\frac{2^{-k}\eta_0}{g_0},
    \frac{24M_0}{\mu}+\frac{8\delta}{g_k},
    \frac2{r_0}\right\rbrace.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_gradient_ratio}
\end{equation}
Suppose first that at least one trial is rejected.
If $\|{s_k} \|\leq r_0$, then~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_movement}
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_length} give
\begin{equation*}
  \tau_k\leq8\delta+24M_0\|{s_k} \|
  \leq8\delta+\frac{24M_0}{\mu}g_k.
\end{equation*}
If $\|{s_k} \|>r_0$, then~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_length} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \tau_k\leq\frac{2g_k}{\|{s_k} \|}
  <\frac{2g_k}{r_0}.
\end{equation*}
Both estimates imply~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_gradient_ratio}
for every $k\geq0$ with a rejection.

For $k=0$, the estimates above apply if a trial is rejected.
Otherwise, $\tau_0=\eta_0$, and
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{\tau_0}{g_0}=\frac{\eta_0}{g_0}
  \leq\max\left\lbrace\frac{\eta_0}{g_0},
    \frac{24M_0}{\mu}+\frac{8\delta}{g_0},\frac2{r_0}\right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
Thus~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_gradient_ratio} holds for $k=0$.
Now let $k\geq1$ and assume it holds for $k-1$.
If a trial is rejected, the estimates above apply again. If there is no
rejection, line~\ref{line:basic_pd_ms_eta_update} gives
\begin{gather*}
  \tau_k=\frac{\tau_{k-1}}2\min\left\lbrace1,\frac{g_k}{g_{k-1}}\right\rbrace
  \leq\max\left\lbrace2^{-k}\eta_0\frac{g_k}{g_0},
    4\delta+\frac{12M_0}{\mu}g_k,
    \frac{g_k}{r_0}\right\rbrace\\
  \leq\max\left\lbrace2^{-k}\eta_0\frac{g_k}{g_0},
    8\delta+\frac{24M_0}{\mu}g_k,
    \frac{2g_k}{r_0}\right\rbrace.
\end{gather*}
This proves~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_gradient_ratio} by induction.
By the definition of $N$, we have $f(x_{N-1})-f^\ast>\varepsilon$.
By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_gap}, $g_{N-1}>\sqrt{2\mu\varepsilon}$.
Substituting this into~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_gradient_ratio}, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \frac{g_0\tau_{N-1}}{\eta_0g_{N-1}}
  \leq\max\left\lbrace2^{-(N-1)},
    \frac{g_0}{\eta_0}\left(\frac{24M_0}{\mu}+\frac{8\delta}{g_{N-1}}\right),
    \frac{2g_0}{\eta_0r_0}\right\rbrace\\
  \leq\max\left\lbrace1,
    \frac{g_0}{\eta_0}\left(\frac{24M_0}{\mu}+\frac{8\delta}{\sqrt{2\mu\varepsilon}}\right),
    \frac{2g_0}{\eta_0r_0}\right\rbrace.
\end{gather*}
Each trial passing $\mathsf{PD}$ requires at most one new gradient evaluation.
The accepted gradient is reused at the next iteration. Hence the total
number of gradient evaluations is at most
\begin{equation*}
  1+N+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}b_k,
\end{equation*}
which, together with the preceding bounds, proves~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_gradient_cost}.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:basic_pd_ms_refined_global}
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:basic_pd_ms_strong_global},
let $\overline\tau$ be defined by~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_scale} and set
\begin{equation*}
  \begin{aligned}
    \overline\tau_k :=\min\left\lbrace\overline\tau,
      8\max_{0\leq j\leq k}2^{j-k}\delta_j
        +\overline\tau
          \left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^k\right\rbrace, \qquad
    \zeta_k :=
      \left(\frac{3\overline\tau_k}{3\overline\tau_k+2\mu}\right)^2.
  \end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
Every completed iteration satisfies
\begin{gather}
  \tau_k\leq\overline\tau_k,
  \nonumber\\
  f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast\leq\zeta_k(f(x_k)-f^\ast),
  \qquad 0<\zeta_k<1.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_refined_step}
\end{gather}
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
For every $i\geq1$, by~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_output_gradient}
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_length},
\begin{equation*}
  \|{\nabla f(x_i)} \|
  \leq\frac{3\tau_{i-1}}2\|{s_{i-1}} \|
  \leq\frac{3\tau_{i-1}}{\tau_{i-1}+2\mu}
    \|{\nabla f(x_{i-1})} \|.
\end{equation*}
Dividing by $\|{\nabla f(x_{i-1})} \|>0$ and substituting into the update
in line~\ref{line:basic_pd_ms_eta_update} gives
\begin{equation}
    \frac{\eta_i}{\tau_{i-1}}
    =\frac12\min\left\lbrace1,\frac{\|{\nabla f(x_i)} \|}
                              {\|{\nabla f(x_{i-1})} \|}\right\rbrace
    \leq\min\left\lbrace\frac12,
      \frac{3\tau_{i-1}}{2\tau_{i-1}+4\mu}\right\rbrace
    \leq\min\left\lbrace\frac12,
      \frac{3\overline\tau}{2\overline\tau+4\mu}\right\rbrace
    \leq\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu},
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_refined_first_trial}
\end{equation}
where we used $\tau_{i-1}\leq\overline\tau$ from
Theorem~\ref{thm:basic_pd_ms_strong_global}.
Fix a completed iteration $k$. 

If no trial was rejected during iterations $0,\ldots,k$, then
$\tau_i=\eta_i$ for $i=0,\ldots,k$. By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_refined_first_trial},
\begin{gather*}
  \tau_k=\eta_0\prod_{i=1}^k\frac{\eta_i}{\tau_{i-1}}
  \leq\eta_0\left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^k
  \leq\overline\tau\left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^k.
\end{gather*}
Otherwise, let $j$ be the last iteration among $0,\ldots,k$
on which a trial is rejected.
By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_gap}
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_global_rate},
\begin{gather*}
  \|{s_j} \|\leq\|{x_j-x^\ast} \|+\|{x_{j+1}-x^\ast} \|\\
  \leq\sqrt{\frac{2(f(x_j)-f^\ast)}\mu}
    +\sqrt{\frac{2(f(x_{j+1})-f^\ast)}\mu}
  \leq2\sqrt{\frac{2(f(x_0)-f^\ast)}\mu}
    \left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^j.
\end{gather*}
Since a trial is rejected on iteration $j$, the two cases in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:basic_pd_ms_strong_global} give the first bound below.
Substituting the step estimate above
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_global_rate}, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \tau_j\leq\max\left\lbrace8\delta_j+24M_0\|{s_j} \|,
    \frac{2(f(x_j)-f^\ast)}{r_0^2}\right\rbrace\\
  \leq\max\left\lbrace
    8\delta_j+48M_0\sqrt{\frac{2(f(x_0)-f^\ast)}\mu}
      \left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^j,
    \frac{2(f(x_0)-f^\ast)}{r_0^2}
      \left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^{2j}\right\rbrace.
\end{gather*}
By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_scale} we obtain
\begin{equation}
  \tau_j\leq8\delta_j
    +\overline\tau\left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^j.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_refined_rejected}
\end{equation}
By the choice of $j$, no trial is rejected on iterations $j+1,\ldots,k$,
so $\tau_i=\eta_i$ for $i=j+1,\ldots,k$.
Applying~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_refined_first_trial}, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \prod_{i=j+1}^k\frac{\eta_i}{\tau_{i-1}}
  \leq\prod_{i=j+1}^k\frac12=2^{j-k},\quad
  \prod_{i=j+1}^k\frac{\eta_i}{\tau_{i-1}}
  \leq\prod_{i=j+1}^k\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}
  =\left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^{k-j}.
\end{gather*}
Substituting~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_refined_rejected}, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \tau_k=\tau_j\prod_{i=j+1}^k\frac{\eta_i}{\tau_{i-1}}
  \leq\left(8\delta_j+\overline\tau
    \left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^j\right)
    \prod_{i=j+1}^k\frac{\eta_i}{\tau_{i-1}}
  \leq8\delta_j2^{j-k}+\overline\tau
    \left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^j
    \left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^{k-j}\\
  =8\delta_j2^{j-k}+\overline\tau
    \left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^k
  \leq8\max_{0\leq i\leq k}2^{i-k}\delta_i+\overline\tau
    \left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^k.
\end{gather*}
Thus, in both cases,
\begin{equation}
  \tau_k\leq8\max_{0\leq j\leq k}2^{j-k}\delta_j
    +\overline\tau\left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^k.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_refined_trial_bound}
\end{equation}
Combining~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_refined_trial_bound}
with $\tau_k\leq\overline\tau$ gives
$\tau_k\leq\overline\tau_k$.

Since $0<\tau_k\leq\overline\tau_k$,
\begin{equation*}
  \left(\frac{3\tau_k}{3\tau_k+2\mu}\right)^2
  =\left(1-\frac{2\mu}{3\tau_k+2\mu}\right)^2
  \leq\left(1-\frac{2\mu}{3\overline\tau_k+2\mu}\right)^2
  =\zeta_k.
\end{equation*}
Substitution into~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_step}
proves~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_refined_step}.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:basic_pd_ms_relative_complexity}
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:basic_pd_ms_strong_global},
suppose additionally that~\eqref{as:basic_pd_ms_relative_appendix} holds.
The method either returns a minimizer or converges superlinearly
in function value:
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast}{f(x_k)-f^\ast}
  \leq\left(\frac{3\tau_k}{3\tau_k+2\mu}\right)^2
  \longrightarrow0.
\end{equation*}
The first $N\geq1$ completed iterations require at most $N$ Hessian
evaluations and
\begin{equation}
  1+\frac94N
  +\log_{2,+}\left(
    \frac{\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}{\eta_0}
    \max\left\lbrace\frac{24M_0}{\mu}+8\nu,\frac2{r_0}\right\rbrace
  \right)
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_relative_gradient_cost}
\end{equation}
gradient evaluations.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Let $g_k:=\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|$.
In the proof of~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_gradient_ratio}, retain
the current error $\delta_k$ on iterations with a rejection and use
$\delta_k/g_k\leq\nu$ from~\eqref{as:basic_pd_ms_relative_appendix}.
The same bounds for the two cases give
\begin{gather*}
  \frac{\tau_0}{g_0}
  \leq\max\left\lbrace\frac{\eta_0}{g_0},
    \frac{24M_0}{\mu}+8\nu,\frac2{r_0}\right\rbrace, \qquad
  \frac{\tau_k}{g_k}
  \leq\max\left\lbrace\frac{\tau_{k-1}}{2g_{k-1}},
    \frac{24M_0}{\mu}+8\nu,\frac2{r_0}\right\rbrace,\quad k\geq1.
\end{gather*}
Iterating this inequality gives
\begin{equation}
  \frac{\tau_k}{g_k}
  \leq\max\left\lbrace\frac{2^{-k}\eta_0}{g_0},
    \frac{24M_0}{\mu}+8\nu,\frac2{r_0}\right\rbrace.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_relative_ratio}
\end{equation}
By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_decrease}
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_global_rate}, for $k\geq1$,
\begin{gather*}
  g_k^2
  \leq\frac{3\tau_{k-1}}2\left( f(x_{k-1})-f(x_k)\right)
  \leq\frac{3\overline\tau}2\left( f(x_{k-1})-f^\ast\right) 
  \leq\frac{3\overline\tau(f(x_0)-f^\ast)}2
    \left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^{2(k-1)}.
\end{gather*}
Substituting into~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_relative_ratio} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \tau_k
  \leq\sqrt{\frac{3\overline\tau(f(x_0)-f^\ast)}2}
    \left(\frac{3\overline\tau}{3\overline\tau+2\mu}\right)^{k-1}
    \max\left\lbrace\frac{2^{-k}\eta_0}{g_0},
      \frac{24M_0}{\mu}+8\nu,\frac2{r_0}\right\rbrace
  \longrightarrow0.
\end{equation*}
Thus,~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_step} proves superlinear convergence.

Let $b_k$ count the rejected trials on iteration $k$. By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_rejections_boundary}
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_gradient_log_sum},
\begin{equation*}
  \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}b_k
  \leq\frac54(N-1)
    +\log_2\frac{g_0\tau_{N-1}}{\eta_0g_{N-1}}.
\end{equation*}
By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_relative_ratio},
\begin{gather*}
  \frac{g_0\tau_{N-1}}{\eta_0g_{N-1}}
  \leq\max\left\lbrace2^{-(N-1)},
    \frac{g_0}{\eta_0}\left(\frac{24M_0}{\mu}+8\nu\right),
    \frac{2g_0}{\eta_0r_0}\right\rbrace
  \leq\max\left\lbrace1,
    \frac{g_0}{\eta_0}\left(\frac{24M_0}{\mu}+8\nu\right),
    \frac{2g_0}{\eta_0r_0}\right\rbrace.
\end{gather*}
Hence
\begin{equation*}
  \sum_{k=0}^{N-1}b_k
  \leq\frac54(N-1)
    +\log_{2,+}\left(\frac{g_0}{\eta_0}
      \max\left\lbrace\frac{24M_0}{\mu}+8\nu,\frac2{r_0}\right\rbrace\right).
\end{equation*}
The gradient count is at most $1+N+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}b_k$,
which proves~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_relative_gradient_cost}.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:basic_pd_ms_quadratic}
Under the assumptions of Corollary~\ref{cor:basic_pd_ms_relative_complexity},
set
\begin{equation*}
  C:=\frac{9\left(\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|+\mu\right)}{2\mu^2}
    \left(8\nu+\frac{24M_0}{\mu}\right)^2.
\end{equation*}
Unless a minimizer is returned earlier, let $K_0\geq1$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
  f(x_{K_0})-f^\ast
  \leq\min\left\lbrace\frac{\mu r_0^2}{8},\frac1{2C}\right\rbrace
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_quadratic_entry}
\end{equation}
and define
\begin{equation}
  K:= K_0+\left\lceil\log_{2,+}
    \frac{\tau_{K_0-1}}
    {2\left(8\nu+\frac{24M_0}{\mu}\right)
      \sqrt{2\mu(f(x_{K_0-1})-f^\ast)}}
    \right\rceil.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_quadratic_entry_index}
\end{equation}
Then, for every $k\geq K$,
\begin{equation}
  f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast\leq C\left( f(x_k)-f^\ast\right)^2.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_quadratic_gap}
\end{equation}
The gradient norms and the distances to $x^\ast$ also converge
quadratically. After a finite initial cost independent of $\varepsilon$,
attaining $f(x)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon$ requires
$\mathcal{O}(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))$ additional iterations, Hessian evaluations,
and gradient evaluations.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{thm:basic_pd_ms_strong_global}, an index $K_0$
satisfying~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_quadratic_entry} exists unless
a minimizer is returned earlier.
Since $\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|\geq\mu$, the definition of $C$ gives
\begin{equation*}
  C\geq\frac9\mu\left(\frac{24M_0}{\mu}\right)^2
  \geq\frac{4M_0^2}{\mu^3},
  \qquad
  \frac1{2C}\leq\frac{\mu^3}{8M_0^2}.
\end{equation*}
Together with monotonicity and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_gap},
condition~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_quadratic_entry} gives, for $k\geq K_0$,
\begin{gather*}
  \|{x_k-x^\ast} \|
  \leq\sqrt{\frac{2(f(x_k)-f^\ast)}{\mu}}
