  \leq\frac12\min\left\lbrace r_0,\frac{\mu}{M_0}\right\rbrace,\\
  \|{s_k} \|
  \leq\|{x_k-x^\ast} \|+\|{x_{k+1}-x^\ast} \|
  \leq2\sqrt{\frac{2(f(x_{K_0})-f^\ast)}{\mu}}
  \leq r_0.
\end{gather*}
Let $g_k:=\|{\nabla f(x_k)} \|$.
Since $\|{s_k} \|\leq r_0$, the proof
of~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_relative_ratio} applies without the term
$2/r_0$. Starting at $K_0$, it gives, for $j\geq0$,
\begin{gather*}
  \frac{\tau_{K_0+j}}{g_{K_0+j}}
  \leq\max\left\lbrace
    \frac{2^{-j-1}\tau_{K_0-1}}{g_{K_0-1}},
    8\nu+\frac{24M_0}{\mu}\right\rbrace
  \leq\max\left\lbrace
    \frac{2^{-j-1}\tau_{K_0-1}}
      {\sqrt{2\mu(f(x_{K_0-1})-f^\ast)}},
    8\nu+\frac{24M_0}{\mu}\right\rbrace.
\end{gather*}
By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_quadratic_entry_index}, for every $k\geq K$,
\begin{equation}
  \tau_k\leq\left(8\nu+\frac{24M_0}{\mu}\right) g_k.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_quadratic_shift}
\end{equation}
Combining~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_output_gradient}
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_length}, we obtain
\begin{equation}
  g_{k+1}
  \leq\frac{3\tau_k}{2}\|{s_k} \|
  \leq\frac{3\tau_k}{2\mu}g_k
  \leq\frac{3}{2\mu}\left(8\nu+\frac{24M_0}{\mu}\right) g_k^2.
  \label{eq:basic_pd_ms_quadratic_gradient}
\end{equation}
Thus, the gradient norms converge quadratically.
Next, we relate the gradient norm to the function gap.
For $\|{z-x^\ast} \|\leq\min\left\lbrace r_0,\mu/M_0\right\rbrace$,
either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \|{\nabla^2 f(z)} \|
  \leq\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|+M_0\|{z-x^\ast} \|
  \leq\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|+\mu,
\end{equation*}
since $\nabla f(x^\ast)=0$ and $r_0\leq\rho/2$ under~\eqref{as:lh}.
Thus, $f$ has $(\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|+\mu)$-Lipschitz gradient on this ball.
Hence, for $k\geq K_0$,
\begin{gather*}
  g_k\leq\left(\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|+\mu\right)\|{x_k-x^\ast} \|,\\
  \left \| x_k-\frac{\nabla f(x_k)}{\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|+\mu}-x^\ast \right \|
  \leq\|{x_k-x^\ast} \|+\frac{g_k}{\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|+\mu}
  \leq2\|{x_k-x^\ast} \|\leq\min\left\lbrace r_0,\frac{\mu}{M_0}\right\rbrace.
\end{gather*}
By Lipschitznes of the gradient, for any $y$ in the ball,
\begin{equation*}
  f(y)\leq f(x_k)+\left\langle\nabla f(x_k),y-x_k\right\rangle
  +\frac{\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|+\mu}{2}\|{y-x_k} \|^2.
\end{equation*}
Substituting the point above, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  f^\ast\leq f\left( x_k-\frac{\nabla f(x_k)}{\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|+\mu}\right)
  \leq f(x_k)-\frac{g_k^2}{\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|+\mu}
  +\frac{\left(\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|+\mu\right) g_k^2}
    {2\left(\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|+\mu\right)^2}\\
  =f(x_k)-\frac{g_k^2}{2\left(\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|+\mu\right)}.
\end{gather*}
Rearranging gives
\begin{equation*}
  g_k^2\leq2\left(\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|+\mu\right)(f(x_k)-f^\ast).
\end{equation*}
Substituting this and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_quadratic_shift}
into~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_strong_step}, for $k\geq K$ we get
\begin{gather*}
  f(x_{k+1})-f^\ast
  \leq\left(\frac{3\tau_k}{3\tau_k+2\mu}\right)^2
    (f(x_k)-f^\ast)\\
  \leq\frac{9}{4\mu^2}\left(8\nu+\frac{24M_0}{\mu}\right)^2
    g_k^2(f(x_k)-f^\ast)
  \leq C(f(x_k)-f^\ast)^2.
\end{gather*}
This proves~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_quadratic_gap}.
For the distances, strong convexity
and~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_quadratic_gradient} give
\begin{equation*}
  \|{x_{k+1}-x^\ast} \|
  \leq\frac{g_{k+1}}{\mu}
  \leq\frac{3\left(\|{\nabla^2 f(x^\ast)} \|+\mu\right)^2}{2\mu^2}
    \left(8\nu+\frac{24M_0}{\mu}\right)\|{x_k-x^\ast} \|^2.
\end{equation*}
By~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_quadratic_entry},
$C(f(x_K)-f^\ast)\leq1/2$.
Iterating~\eqref{eq:basic_pd_ms_quadratic_gap} gives
\begin{equation*}
  f(x_{K+n})-f^\ast
  \leq\frac1C\left( C(f(x_K)-f^\ast)\right)^{2^n}
  \leq\frac{2^{-2^n}}C,\qquad n\geq0.
\end{equation*}
Thus, $f(x_{K+n})-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon$ after
$n=\mathcal{O}(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))$ additional iterations.
By Corollary~\ref{cor:basic_pd_ms_relative_complexity}, this requires
$\mathcal{O}(K+\log\log(1/\varepsilon))$ Hessian and gradient evaluations in total.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{thm:global_convergence}
Assume that $f$ is convex,~\eqref{as:gh} and~\eqref{eq:inital_cnd} hold. For every
$\varepsilon>0$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:global_accelerated_cubic} returns an iterate
$w_{N}$ satisfying $f(w_{N})-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon$ for
\begin{equation}
  \label{eq:gh_conv_rate}
  N = \mathcal{O} \left(
    \left(\tfrac{M_0\bar R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{1/3} + \left(1+\sqrt{M_1}\bar R\right)
    \log\max\left\lbrace
      1,
      \min\left\lbrace
        \tfrac{M_1^{3/2}\bar R^3\Gamma_0}{M_0},
        \tfrac{\Gamma_0\bar R^3}{\varepsilon}
      \right\rbrace
    \right\rbrace
  \right).
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- head-1: body_md -->
We use the standard accelerated-cubic estimating sequence technique~\cite{nesterov2008accelerating}. The main obstruction is that under~\eqref{as:gh} the regularization coefficient $\mathcal{M}_k$ must dominate the generalized smoothness parameter $L(w_{k+1})$ at the \emph{output} $w_{k+1}$ of the cubic step~\eqref{eq:cubic_step}, although this output is not known when the coefficient is selected. Inspired by~\cite{tyurin2025near}, we provide an explicit way of choosing regularization parameter $\mathcal{M}_k$~\eqref{eq:regularization_parameter}, such that this condition is satisfied. The complete proof is given in Appendix~\ref{app:global_method_proof}.

Let us consider one step of Algorithm~\ref{alg:global_accelerated_cubic}. For some $\mathcal{M}>0$, let $A_+(\mathcal{M})$, $w(\mathcal{M})$, and $\psi_+(\cdot;\mathcal{M})$ denote the
quantities produced by one iteration, and set
$\psi_+^\ast(\mathcal{M})=\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\psi_+(x;\mathcal{M})$. Assume first that
$\mathcal{M}\geq L(w(\mathcal{M}))$. Then the standard accelerated-cubic estimating-sequence argument gives
\begin{equation}
  \label{eq:sketch_strengthened_estimate}
  A_+(\mathcal{M})f(w(\mathcal{M}))
  +\tfrac{A_+(\mathcal{M})}{9}
  \tfrac{\|{\nabla f(w(\mathcal{M}))} \|^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\mathcal{M}}}
  \leq\psi_+^\ast(\mathcal{M})
  \leq A_+(\mathcal{M})f^\ast+\tfrac{2}{3}\Gamma_0\bar R^3.
\end{equation}
Thus, conditioned on proper choice of $\mathcal{M} \geq L(w(\mathcal{M}))$, the usual estimating-sequence invariant closes. It remains to choose $\mathcal{M}$ before $w(\mathcal{M})$ is known. Consider the virtual family of steps and
set $\mathcal U_k=\left\lbrace \mathcal{M}>0:\mathcal{M}<L(w(\mathcal{M}))\right\rbrace$. If this set is nonempty, let
$\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger=\sup\mathcal U_k$. Since all sufficiently large $\mathcal{M}$ are admissible, $\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger<+\infty$,
and continuity gives
$\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger=L(w(\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger))$. Let $g^\dagger=\nabla f(w(\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger))$. Combining the two sides of
\eqref{eq:sketch_strengthened_estimate} at this boundary yields
\begin{equation*}
  \tfrac{\|{g^\dagger} \|^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger}}
  \leq6\Gamma_k\bar R^3,
  \qquad
  \mathcal{M}_k^\dagger
  \leq\max\left\lbrace
    2M_0,
    12\sqrt{2}M_1^{3/2}\bar R^3\Gamma_k
  \right\rbrace
  =\mathcal{M}_k.
\end{equation*}
Hence the explicit $\mathcal{M}_k$ used by the algorithm is admissible. This is why we retain the positive remainder
in~\eqref{eq:sketch_strengthened_estimate}. Although it can be
omitted in the standard convergence argument, here it controls the
gradient at the unknown output and closes the explicit choice of $\mathcal{M}$. For the actual step, admissibility gives
\begin{equation*}
  A_{k+1} (f(w_{k+1})-f^\ast)
  \leq\psi_{k+1}^\ast-A_{k+1}f^\ast
  \leq\tfrac{2}{3}\Gamma_0\bar R^3.
\end{equation*}
Then, recurrence for $\Gamma_k$ then gives the rate~\eqref{eq:gh_conv_rate}.
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:cubic_conjugate}
For any $a\geq0$, $g\in\mathbb{R}^d$, and $\beta>0$,
\begin{equation}
  \min_{h\in\mathbb{R}^d}
  \left\lbrace
    \frac{\beta}{3!}\|{h} \|^3+a\left\langle g,h\right\rangle
  \right\rbrace
  =-\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}
  \frac{a^{3/2}\|{g} \|^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\beta}}.
  \label{eq:cubic_conjugate}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:cubic_prox}
Let $h:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be convex, $x_0\in\mathbb{R}^d$, and $\theta>0$. Define
\begin{equation*}
  \varphi(x)
  :=
  h(x)
  +\frac{\theta}{3}\|{x-x_0} \|^3,
  \qquad
  \bar x:=\operatornamewithlimits{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\varphi(x).
\end{equation*}
Then, for every $u\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
\begin{equation*}
  \varphi(\bar x+u)
  \geq
  \varphi(\bar x)
  +\frac{\theta}{6}\|{u} \|^3.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:equivalent_weights}
The weight updates in Algorithm~\ref{alg:global_accelerated_cubic} admit the
following equivalent representation:
\begin{gather}
  a_{k+1} := A_{k+1}-A_k,~~
  \Gamma_k=\frac{\Gamma_0}{A_k},~~
  v_k=\frac{A_kw_k+a_{k+1}z_k}{A_{k+1}},~~
  a_{k+1}^3=\frac{\Gamma_0A_{k+1}^2}{72\mathcal{M}_k}.
  \label{eq:equivalent_weights}
\end{gather}
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Since $A_0=1$, the updates of $A_k$ and $\Gamma_k$~\eqref{eq:a_params} give
\begin{gather*}
  A_{k+1}\Gamma_{k+1}
  =\frac{A_k}{1-\alpha_k}(1-\alpha_k)\Gamma_k
  =A_k\Gamma_k
  =\Gamma_0,
\end{gather*}
and hence $\Gamma_k=\Gamma_0/A_k$. Moreover,
\begin{gather*}
  A_{k+1}-A_k
  =A_{k+1}-(1-\alpha_k)A_{k+1}
  =\alpha_kA_{k+1}
  =a_{k+1},\\
  A_{k+1}v_k
  =(1-\alpha_k)A_{k+1}w_k+\alpha_kA_{k+1}z_k
  =A_kw_k+a_{k+1}z_k.
\end{gather*}
Finally,
\begin{gather*}
  \frac{\alpha_k^3}{1-\alpha_k}
  =\frac{\Gamma_k}{72\mathcal{M}_k}
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \alpha_k^3A_{k+1}^3
  =\frac{\Gamma_kA_kA_{k+1}^2}{72\mathcal{M}_k}
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  a_{k+1}^3
  =\frac{\Gamma_0A_{k+1}^2}{72\mathcal{M}_k}.
\end{gather*}
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:backward_progress}
Fix $v\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathcal{M}>0$, and define
\begin{equation}
  s:=\operatornamewithlimits{argmin}_{h\in\mathbb{R}^d}
  \left\lbrace
    \left\langle\nabla f(v),h\right\rangle
    +\frac{1}{2}\left\langle\nabla^2 f(v)h,h\right\rangle
    +\frac{15\mathcal{M}}{6}\|{h} \|^3
  \right\rbrace.
  \label{eq:local_model}
\end{equation}
Set $w:= v+s$. Suppose that either~\eqref{as:gh} holds, or~\eqref{as:lh} holds and $\|{s} \|\leq\rho$. If
\begin{equation*}
  \mathcal{M}\geq L(w)=M_0+M_1\|{\nabla f(w)} \|,
\end{equation*}
then
\begin{gather}
  \|{\nabla f(w)} \|
  \leq 9\mathcal{M}\|{s} \|^2,
  \label{eq:q_step}\\
  \left\langle\nabla f(w),v-w\right\rangle
  \geq 6\mathcal{M}\|{s} \|^3,
  \label{eq:inner_step}\\
  \left\langle\nabla f(w),v-w\right\rangle
  \geq\frac{2}{9}
  \frac{\|{\nabla f(w)} \|^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\mathcal{M}}}.
  \label{eq:progress_final}
\end{gather}
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
By optimality condition for the cubic subproblem~\eqref{eq:local_model}
\begin{equation}
  \label{eq:opt_cnd}
  \nabla f(v)+\nabla^2 f(v)s+\frac{15\mathcal{M}}{2}\|{s} \|s=0.
\end{equation}
Under~\eqref{as:gh}, Lemma~\ref{lem:global_taylor_remainders} applies at $w$ with $v-w=-s$. Under~\eqref{as:lh}, Lemma~\ref{lem:local_taylor_remainders} applies in the same way, since $\|{s} \|\leq\rho$. Together with the corresponding smoothness condition, this gives
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla f(v)-\nabla f(w)+\nabla^2 f(w)s} \|
  \leq\frac{L(w)}{2}\|{s} \|^2
  \leq\frac{\mathcal{M}}{2}\|{s} \|^2,\\
  \|{\nabla^2 f(v)-\nabla^2 f(w)} \|
  \leq L(w)\|{s} \|
  \leq \mathcal{M}\|{s} \|.
\end{gather*}
By the triangle inequality
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla f(v)-\nabla f(w)+\nabla^2 f(v)s} \|
  \\
  \leq \|{\nabla f(v)-\nabla f(w)+\nabla^2 f(w)s} \|
  +\|{\nabla^2 f(v)-\nabla^2 f(w)} \|\|{s} \| \leq\frac{3\mathcal{M}}{2}\|{s} \|^2.
\end{gather*}
Combining this estimate with~\eqref{eq:opt_cnd}
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla f(w)} \|
  =
  \|{\nabla f(w) - \left( \nabla f(v)+\nabla^2 f(v)s+\tfrac{15\mathcal{M}}{2}\|{s} \|s\right)} \|
  \\
  \leq
  \|{\nabla f(v)-\nabla f(w)+\nabla^2 f(v)s} \|
  +\frac{15\mathcal{M}}{2}\|{s} \|^2
  \leq9\mathcal{M}\|{s} \|^2,
\end{gather*}
which proves \eqref{eq:q_step}. 

Next, 
\begin{gather*}
  \left\langle\nabla f(w),-s\right\rangle
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:opt_cnd}}{=}
  \left\langle\nabla f(v)-\nabla f(w)+\nabla^2 f(v)s,s\right\rangle
  +\frac{15\mathcal{M}}{2}\|{s} \|^3,\\
  \left\langle\nabla f(w),-s\right\rangle
  \geq-\frac{3\mathcal{M}}{2}\|{s} \|^3+\frac{15\mathcal{M}}{2}\|{s} \|^3
  =6\mathcal{M}\|{s} \|^3,
\end{gather*}
which proves \eqref{eq:inner_step}. Finally, \eqref{eq:q_step} implies
\begin{equation*}
  \|{s} \|\geq
  \sqrt{\frac{\|{\nabla f(w)} \|}{9\mathcal{M}}}.
\end{equation*}
Substituting this bound into \eqref{eq:inner_step} proves
\eqref{eq:progress_final}.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:one_safe_step}
Suppose that, at the beginning of iteration $k$,
\begin{equation}
  \psi_k^\ast:=\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\psi_k(x)
  \geq A_kf(w_k).
  \label{eq:current_invariant}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
  \psi_{k+1}^\ast
  \geq A_{k+1}f(w_{k+1})
  +A_{k+1}\left\langle\nabla f(w_{k+1}),v_k-w_{k+1}\right\rangle
  -\frac{A_{k+1}}{9}
  \frac{\|{\nabla f(w_{k+1})} \|^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k}}.
  \label{eq:raw_one_step}
\end{equation}
If, in addition, the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:backward_progress} hold for $v=v_k$ and $\mathcal{M}=\mathcal{M}_k$, then
\begin{equation}
  \psi_{k+1}^\ast
  \geq A_{k+1}f(w_{k+1})
  +\frac{A_{k+1}}{9}
  \frac{\|{\nabla f(w_{k+1})} \|^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k}}.
  \label{eq:strengthened_lower}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  \psi_{k+1}^\ast\geq A_{k+1}f(w_{k+1}).
  \label{eq:invariant_update}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
By the definition of $\psi_k$,
\begin{equation*}
  \psi_k(x)
  =f(x_0)+\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}a_{i+1}\ell_{w_{i+1}}(x)
  +\frac{\Gamma_0}{3}\|{x-x_0} \|^3.
\end{equation*}
The first two terms are affine and hence convex. Therefore,
Lemma~\ref{lem:cubic_prox} with $\theta=\Gamma_0$ gives for any $h \in \mathbb{R}^d$
\begin{equation}
  \psi_k(z_k+h)
  \geq\psi_k^\ast+\frac{\Gamma_0}{6}\|{h} \|^3.
  \label{eq:psi_lower_bound}
\end{equation}
Next, using assumption of this Lemma~\eqref{eq:current_invariant} and Lemma~\ref{lem:cubic_conjugate},
\begin{gather}
  \psi_{k+1}^\ast
  =\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\psi_{k+1}(x)
  =\min_{h\in\mathbb{R}^d}\left\lbrace
    \psi_k(z_k+h)+a_{k+1}\ell_{w_{k+1}}(z_k+h)
  \right\rbrace
  \notag\\
  =a_{k+1}f(w_{k+1})
  +\min_{h\in\mathbb{R}^d}\left\lbrace
    \psi_k(z_k+h)
    +a_{k+1}\left\langle\nabla f(w_{k+1}),z_k+h-w_{k+1}\right\rangle
  \right\rbrace
  \notag\\
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:psi_lower_bound}}{\geq}
  \psi_k^\ast+a_{k+1}f(w_{k+1})
  +a_{k+1}\left\langle\nabla f(w_{k+1}),z_k-w_{k+1}\right\rangle
  \notag\\
  +\min_{h\in\mathbb{R}^d}\left\lbrace
    \frac{\Gamma_0}{6}\|{h} \|^3
    +a_{k+1}\left\langle\nabla f(w_{k+1}),h\right\rangle
  \right\rbrace
  \notag\\
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:current_invariant}}{\geq}
  A_kf(w_k)+a_{k+1}f(w_{k+1})
  +a_{k+1}\left\langle\nabla f(w_{k+1}),z_k-w_{k+1}\right\rangle
  \notag\\
  +\min_{h\in\mathbb{R}^d}\left\lbrace
    \frac{\Gamma_0}{6}\|{h} \|^3
    +a_{k+1}\left\langle\nabla f(w_{k+1}),h\right\rangle
  \right\rbrace
  \notag\\
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:cubic_conjugate}}{=}
  A_kf(w_k)+a_{k+1}f(w_{k+1})
  +a_{k+1}\left\langle\nabla f(w_{k+1}),z_k-w_{k+1}\right\rangle
  -\tfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}
  \tfrac{a_{k+1}^{3/2}\|{\nabla f(w_{k+1})} \|^{3/2}}
  {\sqrt{\Gamma_0}}.
  \label{eq:one_step_lower}
\end{gather}
Relations~\eqref{eq:equivalent_weights} imply
\begin{gather}
  A_{k+1}v_k=A_kw_k+a_{k+1}z_k,
  \qquad
  A_{k+1}w_{k+1}=A_kw_{k+1}+a_{k+1}w_{k+1},
  \notag\\
  a_{k+1}(z_k-w_{k+1})
  =A_{k+1}(v_k-w_{k+1})-A_k(w_k-w_{k+1}).
  \label{eq:interpolation_identity}
\end{gather}
Consequently,
\begin{gather}
  A_kf(w_k)+a_{k+1}f(w_{k+1})
  +a_{k+1}\left\langle\nabla f(w_{k+1}),z_k-w_{k+1}\right\rangle
  \notag\\
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:interpolation_identity}}{=}
  A_{k+1}f(w_{k+1})
  +A_{k+1}\left\langle\nabla f(w_{k+1}),v_k-w_{k+1}\right\rangle
  \notag\\
  \phantom{\stackrel{\eqref{eq:interpolation_identity}}{=}{}}
  +A_k\left(
    f(w_k)-f(w_{k+1})
    -\left\langle\nabla f(w_{k+1}),w_k-w_{k+1}\right\rangle
  \right)
  \notag\\
  \geq A_{k+1}f(w_{k+1})
  +A_{k+1}\left\langle\nabla f(w_{k+1}),v_k-w_{k+1}\right\rangle,
  \label{eq:convex_combination_bound}
\end{gather}
where the inequality follows from convexity of $f$. By~\eqref{eq:equivalent_weights},
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}
  \frac{a_{k+1}^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\Gamma_0}}
  =\frac{A_{k+1}}{9\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k}}.
\end{equation*}
Substituting this identity and~\eqref{eq:convex_combination_bound} into~\eqref{eq:one_step_lower} proves~\eqref{eq:raw_one_step}. Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:backward_progress}, substituting~\eqref{eq:progress_final} into~\eqref{eq:raw_one_step} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \psi_{k+1}^\ast
  \geq A_{k+1}f(w_{k+1})
  +\left(
    \frac{2A_{k+1}}{9\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k}}
    -\frac{A_{k+1}}{9\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k}}
  \right)
  \|{\nabla f(w_{k+1})} \|^{3/2},
\end{equation*}
which proves~\eqref{eq:strengthened_lower}. Dropping the nonnegative second term
proves~\eqref{eq:invariant_update}.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:upper_estimate}
For every $k\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
  \label{eq:upper_estimate}
  \psi_k(x^\ast)
  \leq A_kf^\ast+\Delta_0+\frac{\Gamma_0R^3}{3},
\end{equation}
where $\Delta_0:= f(x_0)-f^\ast$.
Moreover, under~\eqref{eq:inital_cnd},
\begin{equation}
  \label{eq:upper_estimate_exact}
  \Delta_0+\frac{\Gamma_0R^3}{3}\leq\frac{2}{3}\Gamma_0\bar R^3.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
By convexity, $\ell_w(x^\ast)\le f^\ast$ for every $w$. Since $A_k=1+\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}a_{i+1}$,
\begin{gather*}
 \psi_k(x^\ast)
 =f(x_0)+\frac{\Gamma_0}{3}R^3
 +\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}a_{i+1}\ell_{w_{i+1}}(x^\ast)\\
 \leq f(x_0)+\frac{\Gamma_0}{3}R^3+(A_k-1)f^\ast
 =A_kf^\ast+\Delta_0+\frac{\Gamma_0R^3}{3}.
\end{gather*}
Finally,~\eqref{eq:inital_cnd} gives
$\Delta_0\leq\Gamma_0\bar R^3/3$, and $R\leq\bar R$ gives
$\Gamma_0R^3/3\leq\Gamma_0\bar R^3/3$, proving the statement.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:virtual_step_continuity}
The mappings $\mathcal{M}\mapsto\|{w(\mathcal{M})-v(\mathcal{M})} \|$ and $\mathcal{M}\mapsto\mathcal{M}-L(w(\mathcal{M}))$
are continuous on $(0,+\infty)$, and
\begin{equation}
  \|{w(\mathcal{M})-v(\mathcal{M})} \|\to0,
  \qquad
  \mathcal{M}-L(w(\mathcal{M}))\to+\infty
  \quad\text{as }\mathcal{M}\to+\infty.
  \label{eq:M_L_limit}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
The mapping $\alpha\mapsto\alpha^3/(1-\alpha)$ is continuous and strictly
increasing on $(0,1)$. Hence $\alpha(\mathcal{M})$ and $v(\mathcal{M})$ are continuous.

Let $s(\mathcal{M}):= w(\mathcal{M})-v(\mathcal{M})$. For any sequence $\mathcal{M}_j\to \mathcal{M}>0$, the optimality
condition of the cubic subproblem and $\nabla^2f(v(\mathcal{M}_j))\succeq0$ give
\begin{equation}
  \label{eq:s_bound}
  \|{s(\mathcal{M}_j)} \|^2
  \leq\frac{2\|{\nabla f(v(\mathcal{M}_j))} \|}{15\mathcal{M}_j}.
\end{equation}
By~\eqref{eq:interpolation_point_M} $\alpha(\mathcal{M}_j) \to \alpha(\mathcal{M})$ as $\mathcal{M}_j \to \mathcal{M}$, therefore $v(\mathcal{M}_j) \to v(\mathcal{M})$. Since $f$ is twice continuously differentiable $\nabla f(v(\mathcal{M}_j)) \to \nabla f(v(\mathcal{M}))$.
Thus $\{\nabla f(v(\mathcal{M}_j))\}$ is bounded and $\{s(\mathcal{M}_j)\}$ is bounded as well. 

Next, we show that $s(\mathcal{M}_j) \to s(\mathcal{M})$. By Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem bounded sequence $\{s(\mathcal{M}_j)\}$ has a convergent subsequence $\{s(\mathcal{M}_{j_l})\} \to \hat{s}$. Taking the limit in the optimality condition of cubic subproblem shows that $\hat{s}$  satisfies this optimality condition corresponding to $\mathcal{M}$. Since cubic subproblem is strictly convex, it has unique minimizer and $\hat{s} = s(\mathcal{M})$. The same argument applies to any convergent subsequence of $\{s(\mathcal{M}_j)\}$. Thus, $s(\mathcal{M}_j) \to s(\mathcal{M})$ since ${s(\mathcal{M}_j)}$ is bounded sequence with only one accumulation point. Therefore $w(\mathcal{M}_j)\to w(\mathcal{M})$ and thus $w(\mathcal{M})$ is continuous. Since $L(\cdot)$ is continuous, the mappings $\|{s(\mathcal{M})} \|$ and $\mathcal{M}-L(w(\mathcal{M}))$ are continuous as well.

The estimate~\eqref{eq:s_bound} gives
$s(\mathcal{M})\to0$ as $\mathcal{M}\to+\infty$, while
$\alpha(\mathcal{M})\to0$ by~\eqref{eq:alpha_M_equality} and $v(\mathcal{M})\to w_k$ by~\eqref{eq:interpolation_point_M}. Hence $w(\mathcal{M})\to w_k$, so $L(w(\mathcal{M}))$ remains bounded. This gives us~\eqref{eq:M_L_limit}.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{thm:explicit_regularization}
Suppose that~\eqref{as:gh} and~\eqref{eq:current_invariant} hold. Then the
parameter
\begin{equation*}
  \mathcal{M}_k=\max\left\lbrace
    2M_0,
    12\sqrt{2}M_1^{3/2}\bar R^3\Gamma_k
  \right\rbrace
\end{equation*}
used in Algorithm~\ref{alg:global_accelerated_cubic} satisfies
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal{M}_k\geq L(w_{k+1})
  =M_0+M_1\|{\nabla f(w_{k+1})} \|.
  \label{eq:explicit_regularization_validity}
\end{equation}
Consequently, estimates~\eqref{eq:strengthened_lower}
and~\eqref{eq:invariant_update} hold for the actual iteration.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Define
\begin{equation*}
  \mathcal U_k:=\left\lbrace \mathcal{M}>0:\mathcal{M}<L(w(\mathcal{M}))\right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
If $\mathcal U_k=\emptyset$, the statement is immediate. Otherwise, let $\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger:=\sup\mathcal U_k$. Lemma~\ref{lem:virtual_step_continuity} shows that $\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger<+\infty$.
By continuity,
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal{M}_k^\dagger=L(w(\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger)),
  \label{eq:boundary_admissibility}
\end{equation}
and every $\mathcal{M}\geq \mathcal{M}_k^\dagger$ is admissible.

Set
\begin{equation*}
  w^\dagger:= w(\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger),
  \qquad
  g^\dagger:=\nabla f(w^\dagger),
  \qquad
  A_+^\dagger:= A_+(\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger).
\end{equation*}
Applying~\eqref{eq:virtual_safe_step} at the admissible boundary and evaluating
$\psi_+(\cdot;\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger)$ at $x^\ast$, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  A_+^\dagger f(w^\dagger)
  +\frac{A_+^\dagger}{9}
  \frac{\|{g^\dagger} \|^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger}}
  \leq\psi_+^\ast(\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger)
  \leq\psi_+(x^\ast;\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger)
  \leq A_+^\dagger f^\ast
  +\Delta_0+\frac{\Gamma_0R^3}{3}.
\end{gather*}
Since $f(w^\dagger)\geq f^\ast$, $A_+^\dagger\geq A_k$, and
$\Gamma_k=\Gamma_0/A_k$, equation~\eqref{eq:upper_estimate_exact} gives
\begin{equation}
  \frac{\|{g^\dagger} \|^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger}}
  \leq6\Gamma_k\bar R^3.
  \label{eq:boundary_gradient_bound}
\end{equation}
For every $g\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
\begin{equation}
  M_0+M_1\|{g} \|
  \leq\max\left\lbrace
    2M_0,
    2\sqrt{2}M_1^{3/2}
    \frac{\|{g} \|^{3/2}}{\sqrt{M_0+M_1\|{g} \|}}
  \right\rbrace.
  \label{eq:L_max_bound}
\end{equation}
Indeed, the first term applies when $M_1\|{g} \|\leq M_0$. Otherwise,
$M_0+M_1\|{g} \|\leq2M_1\|{g} \|$ and
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{\|{g} \|^{3/2}}{\sqrt{M_0+M_1\|{g} \|}}
  \geq\frac{\|{g} \|}{\sqrt{2M_1}}.
\end{equation*}
Applying this bound with $g=g^\dagger$ and using
\eqref{eq:boundary_admissibility} and~\eqref{eq:boundary_gradient_bound},
we obtain
\begin{equation*}
  \mathcal{M}_k^\dagger
  \leq\max\left\lbrace
    2M_0,
    2\sqrt{2}M_1^{3/2}
    \frac{\|{g^\dagger} \|^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger}}
  \right\rbrace 
  \leq\max\left\lbrace
    2M_0,
    12\sqrt{2}M_1^{3/2}\bar R^3\Gamma_k
  \right\rbrace
  =\mathcal{M}_k.
\end{equation*}
Therefore $\mathcal{M}_k$ is admissible and~\eqref{eq:explicit_regularization_validity}
holds. The last statement follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:one_safe_step}.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{lem:global_invariant}
Suppose that~\eqref{as:gh} holds. For every $k\geq0$, the parameter $\mathcal{M}_k$ in
Algorithm~\ref{alg:global_accelerated_cubic} satisfies
\eqref{eq:explicit_regularization_validity}, and
\begin{equation}
  \psi_k^\ast\geq A_kf(w_k).
  \label{eq:global_invariant}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
  \psi_{k+1}^\ast
  \geq A_{k+1}f(w_{k+1})
  +\frac{A_{k+1}}{9}
  \frac{\|{\nabla f(w_{k+1})} \|^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k}}.
  \label{eq:global_strengthened}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
For $k=0$,
\begin{equation*}
  \psi_0^\ast
  =\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}\left\lbrace
    f(x_0)+\frac{\Gamma_0}{3}\|{x-x_0} \|^3
  \right\rbrace
  =f(x_0)
  =A_0f(w_0).
\end{equation*}
Suppose that~\eqref{eq:global_invariant} holds at iteration $k$.
Theorem~\ref{thm:explicit_regularization} gives
\eqref{eq:explicit_regularization_validity}. Hence,
Lemma~\ref{lem:one_safe_step} gives~\eqref{eq:global_strengthened} and
\begin{equation*}
  \psi_{k+1}^\ast\geq A_{k+1}f(w_{k+1}),
\end{equation*}
which closes the induction.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{lem:global_error_bounds}
Suppose that~\eqref{as:gh} holds. For every $k\geq0$,
\begin{equation}
  f(w_k)-f^\ast
  \leq\frac{\Delta_0+\Gamma_0R^3/3}{A_k}
  \leq\frac{2}{3}\Gamma_k\bar R^3.
  \label{eq:global_error_bound}
\end{equation}
Moreover, every cubic output satisfies
\begin{equation}
  f(w_{k+1})-f^\ast
  +\frac{1}{9}
  \frac{\|{\nabla f(w_{k+1})} \|^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k}}
  \leq\frac{\Delta_0+\Gamma_0R^3/3}{A_{k+1}}
  \leq\frac{2}{3}\Gamma_{k+1}\bar R^3.
  \label{eq:global_output_bound}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
Combining~\eqref{eq:global_invariant} and~\eqref{eq:upper_estimate},
\begin{gather*}
  A_kf(w_k)
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:global_invariant}}{\leq}\psi_k^\ast
  \leq\psi_k(x^\ast)
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:upper_estimate}}{\leq}
  A_kf^\ast+\Delta_0+\frac{\Gamma_0R^3}{3}.
\end{gather*}
Therefore,
\begin{gather*}
  f(w_k)-f^\ast
  \leq\frac{\Delta_0+\Gamma_0R^3/3}{A_k}
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:upper_estimate_exact}}{\leq}
  \frac{2\Gamma_0\bar R^3}{3A_k}
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:equivalent_weights}}{=}
  \frac{2}{3}\Gamma_k\bar R^3.
\end{gather*}
Similarly,
\begin{equation*}
  A_{k+1}f(w_{k+1})
  +\frac{A_{k+1}}{9}
  \frac{\|{\nabla f(w_{k+1})} \|^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k}}
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:global_strengthened}}{\leq}\psi_{k+1}^\ast
  \leq\psi_{k+1}(x^\ast)
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:upper_estimate}}{\leq}
  A_{k+1}f^\ast+\Delta_0+\frac{\Gamma_0R^3}{3}.
\end{equation*}
Dividing by $A_{k+1}$ and using~\eqref{eq:upper_estimate_exact} and
\eqref{eq:equivalent_weights} proves~\eqref{eq:global_output_bound}.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{lem:far_regime}
Suppose that $M_1>0$ and $\Gamma_k>\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}}$. Then
\begin{equation}
  \alpha_k
  \geq\frac{1}{12\sqrt[6]{2}\left(1+\sqrt{M_1}\bar R\right)},
  \label{eq:far_weight_bound}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
  \Gamma_{k+1}
  \leq\exp\left(
    -\frac{1}{12\sqrt[6]{2}\left(1+\sqrt{M_1}\bar R\right)}
  \right)\Gamma_k.
  \label{eq:far_contraction}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
In this regime,
\begin{equation*}
  \mathcal{M}_k=12\sqrt{2}M_1^{3/2}\bar R^3\Gamma_k,
\end{equation*}
and hence
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{\alpha_k^3}{1-\alpha_k}
  =\frac{1}{864\sqrt{2}M_1^{3/2}\bar R^3}.
\end{equation*}
If $\alpha_k>1/2$, then~\eqref{eq:far_weight_bound} holds immediately.
If $\alpha_k\leq1/2$, then
\begin{equation*}
  \alpha_k^3
  =\tfrac{1-\alpha_k}{864\sqrt{2}M_1^{3/2}\bar R^3}
  \geq\tfrac{1}{1728\sqrt{2}M_1^{3/2}\bar R^3}, \quad
  \alpha_k
  \geq\tfrac{1}{12\sqrt[6]{2}\sqrt{M_1}\bar R}.
\end{equation*}
Combining the two cases proves~\eqref{eq:far_weight_bound}. Finally,
$1-\alpha_k\leq\exp(-\alpha_k)$ proves~\eqref{eq:far_contraction}.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{lem:near_regime}
Suppose that~\eqref{as:gh} holds and
$\Gamma_K\leq\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}}$. Then $\mathcal{M}_j=2M_0$ for every
$j\geq K$, and
\begin{equation}
  A_{K+n}^{1/3}
  \geq A_K^{1/3}
  +\frac{n}{3}\left(\frac{\Gamma_0}{144M_0}\right)^{1/3},
  \qquad n\geq1.
  \label{eq:near_growth}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  \Gamma_{K+n}\leq\frac{3888M_0}{n^3},
  \qquad n\geq1,
  \label{eq:near_gamma_bound}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
  f(w_{K+n})-f^\ast
  \leq\frac{2592M_0\bar R^3}{n^3},
  \qquad n\geq1.
  \label{eq:near_function_bound}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
The monotonicity of $\Gamma_k$ and~\eqref{eq:gamma_transition} give
$\mathcal{M}_j=2M_0$ for every $j\geq K$. Therefore,
\eqref{eq:equivalent_weights} gives
\begin{equation*}
  a_{j+1}^3=\frac{\Gamma_0A_{j+1}^2}{144M_0}.
\end{equation*}
Using $A_{j+1}-A_j=a_{j+1}$,
\begin{equation*}
  A_{j+1}^{1/3}-A_j^{1/3}
  =\frac{a_{j+1}}
  {A_{j+1}^{2/3}+A_{j+1}^{1/3}A_j^{1/3}+A_j^{2/3}}
  \geq\frac{a_{j+1}}{3A_{j+1}^{2/3}}
  =\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{\Gamma_0}{144M_0}\right)^{1/3}.
\end{equation*}
Summing over $j=K,\ldots,K+n-1$ proves~\eqref{eq:near_growth}. Hence,
\begin{equation*}
  A_{K+n}
  \geq\frac{n^3\Gamma_0}{3888M_0}, \quad
  \Gamma_{K+n}
  \stackrel{\eqref{eq:equivalent_weights}}{=}
  \frac{\Gamma_0}{A_{K+n}}
  \leq\frac{3888M_0}{n^3},
\end{equation*}
which proves~\eqref{eq:near_gamma_bound}. Combining
\eqref{eq:global_error_bound} and~\eqref{eq:near_gamma_bound} proves
\eqref{eq:near_function_bound}.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{thm:explicit_global_complexity}
Suppose that $f$ is convex,~\eqref{as:gh} and~\eqref{eq:inital_cnd} hold. For every
$\varepsilon>0$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:global_accelerated_cubic} returns an iterate
$w_{N}$ satisfying
\begin{equation*}
  f(w_{N})-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon
\end{equation*}
after at most
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  N \leq \left\lceil
    12\sqrt[6]{2}\left(1+\sqrt{M_1}\bar R\right)
    \log\max\left\lbrace
      1,
      \min\left\lbrace
        \tfrac{6\sqrt{2}M_1^{3/2}\bar R^3\Gamma_0}{M_0},
        \tfrac{2\Gamma_0\bar R^3}{3\varepsilon}
      \right\rbrace
    \right\rbrace
  \right\rceil + 
  \left\lceil
    \left(\tfrac{2592M_0\bar R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{1/3}
  \right\rceil
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:global_complexity}
\end{equation}
iterations.
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
Define
\begin{equation*}
  \Gamma_\varepsilon:=\frac{3\varepsilon}{2\bar R^3}.
\end{equation*}
By~\eqref{eq:global_error_bound}, if $\Gamma_k\leq\Gamma_\varepsilon$, then
\begin{equation*}
  f(w_k)-f^\ast
  \leq\frac{2}{3}\Gamma_k\bar R^3
  \leq\frac{2}{3}\Gamma_\varepsilon\bar R^3
  =\varepsilon.
\end{equation*}
Suppose first that $M_1>0$, and set
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
  N_{\rm far}:=
  \left\lceil
    12\sqrt[6]{2}\left(1+\sqrt{M_1}\bar R\right)
    \log\max\left\lbrace
      1,
      \frac{\Gamma_0}{\max\left\lbrace\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}},\Gamma_\varepsilon\right\rbrace}
    \right\rbrace
  \right\rceil.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
Suppose that
$\Gamma_k>\max\left\lbrace\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}},\Gamma_\varepsilon\right\rbrace$ for every
$k=0,\ldots,N_{\rm far}-1$. Then~\eqref{eq:far_contraction} applies at
each of these iterations, and
\begin{equation*}
  \Gamma_{N_{\rm far}}
  \leq\exp\left(
    -\frac{N_{\rm far}}
    {12\sqrt[6]{2}\left(1+\sqrt{M_1}\bar R\right)}
  \right)\Gamma_0
  \leq\max\left\lbrace\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}},\Gamma_\varepsilon\right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
Therefore, after at most $N_{\rm far}$ iterations, either
$\Gamma_k\leq\Gamma_\varepsilon$, or $\Gamma_k\leq\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}}$ and the
near regime begins. Moreover,
\begin{gather*}
  \frac{\Gamma_0}{\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}}}
  =\frac{6\sqrt{2}M_1^{3/2}\bar R^3\Gamma_0}{M_0},
  \qquad
  \frac{\Gamma_0}{\Gamma_\varepsilon}
  =\frac{2\Gamma_0\bar R^3}{3\varepsilon},\\
  \frac{\Gamma_0}
  {\max\left\lbrace\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}},\Gamma_\varepsilon\right\rbrace}
  =\min\left\lbrace
    \frac{6\sqrt{2}M_1^{3/2}\bar R^3\Gamma_0}{M_0},
    \frac{2\Gamma_0\bar R^3}{3\varepsilon}
  \right\rbrace.
\end{gather*}
If the near regime is needed, Lemma~\ref{lem:near_regime} shows that
\begin{equation*}
  N_{\rm near}
  :=\left\lceil
    \left(\frac{2592M_0\bar R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{1/3}
  \right\rceil
\end{equation*}
additional iterations suffice. Hence,
$N \leq N_{\rm far}+N_{\rm near}$, which
proves~\eqref{eq:global_complexity}.

If $M_1=0$, then $\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}}=+\infty$ and the near regime starts at
$K=0$. The first term in~\eqref{eq:global_complexity} is zero, while
Lemma~\ref{lem:near_regime} gives the second term.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{lem:cubic_initialization}
Suppose that either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds. If
$\nabla f(x_0)=0$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:fully_adaptive_cubic} returns the
optimal point $x_0$. Otherwise, the initialization
backtracking (lines~\ref{line:adaptive_initial_start}-\ref{line:adaptive_initial_end} of Algorithm~\ref{alg:fully_adaptive_cubic}) satisfies~\eqref{eq:cubic_initial_test}  after at most $\left\lceil
    \log_2\max\left\lbrace
      1, \tfrac{T_{0}}{\tilde{\mathcal{M}}_0} \right\rbrace \right\rceil$ rejected trials, where 
\begin{equation}
  T_{0} = 
  \begin{cases}
    M_0+2M_1\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|,
    & \text{under~\eqref{as:gh}},\\
    \max\left\lbrace
      M_0+2M_1\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|,
      \tfrac{2\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}{15\rho^2}
    \right\rbrace,
    & \text{under~\eqref{as:lh}}.
  \end{cases}
  \label{eq:initial_safe_threshold}
\end{equation}
For the accepted step,
$\Gamma_0 := \tfrac{3 \|\nabla f(x_0)\|^3}{(f(x_0) - f(\tilde{x}))^2}$
is well defined and satisfies initial condition~\eqref{eq:inital_cnd2}.
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{thm:fully_adaptive_convergence}
Suppose that $f$ is convex and either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds.
All backtracking loops in Algorithm~\ref{alg:fully_adaptive_cubic} terminate.
For every $\varepsilon>0$, under~\eqref{as:gh}, the method returns an iterate $w_N$
satisfying $f(w_N)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon$ for
\begin{equation}
  N
  =\mathcal{O}\left(
    \left(\tfrac{M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{1/3}
  \right)
  +\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(
    1+\sqrt{M_1}R
  \right).
  \label{eq:adaptive_global_rate}
\end{equation}
Under~\eqref{as:lh}, the corresponding bound is
\begin{equation}
  N
  =\mathcal{O}\left(
    \left(\tfrac{M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{1/3}
  \right)
  +\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(
    1+\sqrt{M_1}R+\tfrac{R}{\rho}
  \right).
  \label{eq:adaptive_local_rate}
\end{equation}
The number of rejected initialization trials is bounded as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:cubic_initialization}. Before returning $w_N$, the main
backtracking loops reject at most
$
  \left\lceil
    \log_2\max\left\lbrace
      1,
      B,
      \tfrac{4M_0R^3}{3\varepsilon}
    \right\rbrace
  \right\rceil
$
trials in total, where $B$ is defined in~\eqref{eq:adaptive_B}.
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
Suppose that $\nabla f(x_0)\neq0$ and fix a trial value $\tilde{\mathcal{M}}>0$.
The optimality condition for~\eqref{eq:cubic_initial_step} is
\begin{equation}
  \nabla f(x_0)+\nabla^2f(x_0)\tilde s
  +\frac{15\tilde{\mathcal{M}}}{2}\|{\tilde s} \|\tilde s=0.
  \label{eq:initial_cubic_optimality}
\end{equation}
Since $f$ is convex, $\nabla^2f(x_0)\succeq0$. Taking the inner product
of~\eqref{eq:initial_cubic_optimality} with $\tilde s$, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \frac{15\tilde{\mathcal{M}}}{2}\|{\tilde s} \|^3
  \leq-\left\langle\nabla f(x_0),\tilde s\right\rangle
  \leq\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|\|{\tilde s} \|,
\end{gather*}
and hence
\begin{equation}
  \|{\tilde s} \|^2
  \leq\frac{2\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}{15\tilde{\mathcal{M}}}.
  \label{eq:initial_step_bound}
\end{equation}
Let $\tilde{\mathcal{M}}\geq T_0$, defined in~\eqref{eq:initial_safe_threshold}. Under~\eqref{as:lh},
equations~\eqref{eq:initial_safe_threshold}
and~\eqref{eq:initial_step_bound} give
\begin{equation*}
  \|{\tilde s} \|^2
  \leq\frac{2\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}{15\tilde{\mathcal{M}}}
  \leq\rho^2.
\end{equation*}
Therefore, the Taylor remainder at $x_0$ can be applied under both
assumptions. Using~\eqref{eq:initial_cubic_optimality}, we get
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla f(\tilde x)} \|
  \leq
  \|{\nabla f(\tilde x)-\nabla f(x_0)
  -\nabla^2f(x_0)\tilde s} \|
  +\frac{15\tilde{\mathcal{M}}}{2}\|{\tilde s} \|^2
  \\
  \leq
  \frac{M_0+M_1\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|+15\tilde{\mathcal{M}}}{2}
  \|{\tilde s} \|^2
  \\
  \leq
  \left(
    1+\frac{M_0+M_1\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}{15\tilde{\mathcal{M}}}
  \right)\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|
  \leq\frac{16}{15}\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|.
\end{gather*}
Consequently,
\begin{gather*}
  M_0+M_1\|{\nabla f(\tilde x)} \|
  \leq M_0+2M_1\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|
  \leq \tilde{\mathcal{M}}.
\end{gather*}
Since $\|{\tilde s} \|\leq\rho$ under~\eqref{as:lh}, the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:backward_progress} hold under both assumptions. Therefore,~\eqref{eq:progress_final} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \left\langle\nabla f(\tilde x),-\tilde s\right\rangle
  \geq\frac{2}{9\sqrt{\tilde{\mathcal{M}}}}\|{\nabla f(\tilde x)} \|^{3/2},
\end{equation*}
which is condition~\eqref{eq:cubic_initial_test}. Hence, every trial with
$\tilde{\mathcal{M}}\geq T_0$ is accepted.

Starting from the input value $\tilde{\mathcal{M}}_0$, the $j$-th trial uses
$2^j\tilde{\mathcal{M}}_0$. For
\begin{equation*}
  j=\left\lceil
    \log_2\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{T_0}{\tilde{\mathcal{M}}_0}\right\rbrace
  \right\rceil,
\end{equation*}
we have $2^j\tilde{\mathcal{M}}_0\geq T_0$. Therefore, the backtracking rejects at most $j$
trials.

It remains to verify~\eqref{eq:inital_cnd2}. If
$\nabla f(\tilde x)\neq0$, condition~\eqref{eq:cubic_initial_test} and
convexity give
\begin{equation*}
  f(x_0)-f(\tilde x)
  \geq\left\langle\nabla f(\tilde x),x_0-\tilde x\right\rangle
  >0.
\end{equation*}
If $\nabla f(\tilde x)=0$, then $\tilde x$ is optimal. Since
$\nabla f(x_0)\neq0$, in this case we also have
$f(x_0)-f(\tilde x)>0$. Moreover, by convexity,
\begin{gather*}
  0< f(x_0)-f(\tilde x)
  \leq f(x_0)-f^\ast
  \leq\left\langle\nabla f(x_0),x_0-x^\ast\right\rangle
  \leq\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|R.
\end{gather*}
Thus,
\begin{equation*}
  0<\frac{f(x_0)-f(\tilde x)}{\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}\leq R.
\end{equation*}
Using this estimate one more time, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  f(x_0)-f^\ast
  \leq\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|R
  =\left( f(x_0)-f(\tilde x)\right)
  \frac{\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|R}{f(x_0)-f(\tilde x)}
  \\
  \leq\left( f(x_0)-f(\tilde x)\right)
  \left(
    \frac{\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|R}{f(x_0)-f(\tilde x)}
  \right)^3
  =\frac{\Gamma_0R^3}{3}.
\end{gather*}
This proves~\eqref{eq:inital_cnd2}.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:adaptive_safe_trial}
Suppose that either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds and that
\eqref{eq:current_invariant} is satisfied. Every trial with
$\mathcal{M}\geq\max\left\lbrace2M_0,B\Gamma_k\right\rbrace$
satisfies~\eqref{eq:adaptive_certificate}.
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
By~\eqref{eq:inital_cnd2}, condition~\eqref{eq:inital_cnd} holds with
$\bar R=R$. Under~\eqref{as:gh}, we set $\rho=+\infty$. The trial with coefficient $\mathcal{M}$ coincides with the virtual step $w(\mathcal{M})$ defined after~\eqref{eq:interpolation_point_M}. Set $r(\mathcal{M}):=\|{w(\mathcal{M})-v(\mathcal{M})} \|$ and
\begin{equation*}
  \mathcal U_k:=\left\lbrace\mathcal{M}>0:r(\mathcal{M})>\rho\text{ or }\mathcal{M}<L(w(\mathcal{M}))\right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
For $\mathcal{M}\notin\mathcal U_k$, the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:backward_progress} hold for $v=v(\mathcal{M})$, and~\eqref{eq:progress_final} gives~\eqref{eq:adaptive_certificate}. Thus, it suffices to show that every $\mathcal{M}\geq\max\left\lbrace2M_0,B\Gamma_k\right\rbrace$ satisfies $\mathcal{M}\notin\mathcal U_k$.

If $\mathcal U_k=\emptyset$, there is nothing to prove. Otherwise, Lemma~\ref{lem:virtual_step_continuity} shows that $\mathcal U_k$ is open and bounded above. Let $\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger:=\sup\mathcal U_k<+\infty$. Then $\mathcal{M}\notin\mathcal U_k$ for every $\mathcal{M}\geq\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger$. By continuity,
\begin{equation}
  r^\dagger\leq\rho,
  \qquad
  \mathcal{M}_k^\dagger\geq L(w^\dagger),
  \qquad
  r^\dagger=\rho
  \text{ or }
  \mathcal{M}_k^\dagger=L(w^\dagger),
  \label{eq:adaptive_boundary}
\end{equation}
where a dagger denotes evaluation at $\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger$ and $g^\dagger:=\nabla f(w^\dagger)$.

By~\eqref{eq:adaptive_boundary}, the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:backward_progress} hold at $\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger$. Hence,~\eqref{eq:q_step},~\eqref{eq:inner_step}, and~\eqref{eq:progress_final} give
\begin{gather*}
  \left\langle g^\dagger,v^\dagger-w^\dagger\right\rangle
  -\frac{\|{g^\dagger} \|^{3/2}}{9\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger}}
  \geq
  6\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger(r^\dagger)^3
  -\frac{\left(9\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger(r^\dagger)^2\right)^{3/2}}{9\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger}}
  =3\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger(r^\dagger)^3,\\
  \left\langle g^\dagger,v^\dagger-w^\dagger\right\rangle
  -\frac{\|{g^\dagger} \|^{3/2}}{9\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger}}
  \geq
  \frac{\|{g^\dagger} \|^{3/2}}{9\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger}}.
\end{gather*}
Lemma~\ref{lem:one_safe_step} applies to the virtual step, as explained before~\eqref{eq:virtual_safe_step}. Therefore,~\eqref{eq:raw_one_step} and evaluation of $\psi_+(\cdot;\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger)$ at $x^\ast$ give
\begin{gather*}
  A_+^\dagger f(w^\dagger)
  +A_+^\dagger\max\left\lbrace
    3\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger(r^\dagger)^3,
    \frac{\|{g^\dagger} \|^{3/2}}{9\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger}}
  \right\rbrace
  \leq\psi_+^\ast(\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger)
  \leq\psi_+(x^\ast;\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger)
  \leq A_+^\dagger f^\ast
  +\Delta_0+\frac{\Gamma_0R^3}{3}.
\end{gather*}
Since $f(w^\dagger)\geq f^\ast$, $A_+^\dagger\geq A_k$, and
$\Gamma_k=\Gamma_0/A_k$, equation~\eqref{eq:upper_estimate_exact} with $\bar R=R$ gives
\begin{equation}
  \max\left\lbrace
    3\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger(r^\dagger)^3,
    \frac{\|{g^\dagger} \|^{3/2}}{9\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger}}
  \right\rbrace
  \leq\frac{2}{3}\Gamma_kR^3.
  \label{eq:adaptive_boundary_budget}
\end{equation}
If $r^\dagger=\rho$, then~\eqref{eq:adaptive_boundary_budget} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \mathcal{M}_k^\dagger\leq\frac{2R^3}{9\rho^3}\Gamma_k\leq B\Gamma_k.
\end{equation*}
If $\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger=L(w^\dagger)$, then~\eqref{eq:L_max_bound} and~\eqref{eq:adaptive_boundary_budget} give
\begin{equation*}
  \mathcal{M}_k^\dagger
  \leq\max\left\lbrace
    2M_0,
    2\sqrt{2}M_1^{3/2}
    \frac{\|{g^\dagger} \|^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger}}
  \right\rbrace
  \leq\max\left\lbrace
    2M_0,
    12\sqrt{2}M_1^{3/2}R^3\Gamma_k
  \right\rbrace
  \leq\max\left\lbrace2M_0,B\Gamma_k\right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
In both cases, every $\mathcal{M}\geq\max\left\lbrace2M_0,B\Gamma_k\right\rbrace$ satisfies $\mathcal{M}\geq\mathcal{M}_k^\dagger$, and hence $\mathcal{M}\notin\mathcal U_k$.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:adaptive_backtracking}
Suppose that either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds. Every main
backtracking loop in Algorithm~\ref{alg:fully_adaptive_cubic} terminates.
For every accepted iteration $k\geq0$,
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal{M}_k
  \leq\max\left\lbrace
    4M_0,
    \max\left\lbrace1,2B\right\rbrace\Gamma_k
  \right\rbrace.
  \label{eq:adaptive_regularization_upper}
\end{equation}
For every $K\geq1$, the total number of rejected main trials during
iterations $k=0,\ldots,K-1$ is at most
\begin{equation}
  \left\lceil
    \log_2\max\left\lbrace
      1,
      B,
      \frac{2M_0}{\Gamma_{K-1}}
    \right\rbrace
  \right\rceil.
  \label{eq:adaptive_rejected_prefix}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
At $k=0$,~\eqref{eq:current_invariant} holds with equality. Suppose that it
holds at the beginning of iteration $k$. Repeated doubling sends $\mathcal{M}_k$ to
$+\infty$. Hence, Lemma~\ref{lem:adaptive_safe_trial} shows that
condition~\eqref{eq:adaptive_certificate} is satisfied after finitely many
trials. For the accepted trial,~\eqref{eq:invariant_update} gives
\eqref{eq:current_invariant} at iteration $k+1$. Thus, every backtracking loop
terminates by induction.

It remains to prove~\eqref{eq:adaptive_regularization_upper}. At $k=0$, if
the first trial is accepted, then
\begin{equation*}
  \mathcal{M}_0=\Gamma_0
  \leq\max\left\lbrace1,2B\right\rbrace\Gamma_0.
\end{equation*}
If at least one trial is rejected, the coefficient immediately preceding the
accepted one is $\mathcal{M}_0/2$. Lemma~\ref{lem:adaptive_safe_trial} gives
$
  \frac{\mathcal{M}_0}{2}
  <\max\left\lbrace2M_0,B\Gamma_0\right\rbrace
$.
Therefore,
$
  \mathcal{M}_0
  <\max\left\lbrace4M_0,2B\Gamma_0\right\rbrace
$,
and~\eqref{eq:adaptive_regularization_upper} follows.

Suppose that~\eqref{eq:adaptive_regularization_upper} holds at iteration
$k-1$. If the first trial is accepted at iteration $k$, then
\begin{gather*}
  \mathcal{M}_k
  =\frac{\Gamma_k}{\Gamma_{k-1}}\mathcal{M}_{k-1}
  \leq
  \frac{\Gamma_k}{\Gamma_{k-1}}
  \max\left\lbrace
    4M_0,
    \max\left\lbrace1,2B\right\rbrace\Gamma_{k-1}
  \right\rbrace
  \leq\max\left\lbrace
    4M_0,
    \max\left\lbrace1,2B\right\rbrace\Gamma_k
  \right\rbrace,
\end{gather*}
where we used $\Gamma_k\leq\Gamma_{k-1}$. If at least one trial is rejected,
the same argument as for $k=0$ proves the bound. This closes the induction.

Finally, the initialization and the update of $\mathcal{M}_k$ in
Algorithm~\ref{alg:fully_adaptive_cubic} imply that the ratio
$\mathcal{M}_k/\Gamma_k$ is initially equal to one, remains unchanged between
accepted iterations, and doubles after every rejected trial. Since
$\Gamma_k$ is decreasing, for every $k=0,\ldots,K-1$,
\begin{equation*}
  \max\left\lbrace
    B,
    \frac{2M_0}{\Gamma_k}
  \right\rbrace
  \leq\max\left\lbrace
    B,
    \frac{2M_0}{\Gamma_{K-1}}
  \right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:adaptive_safe_trial}, every trial satisfying
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{\mathcal{M}_k}{\Gamma_k}
  \geq\max\left\lbrace
    B,
    \frac{2M_0}{\Gamma_{K-1}}
  \right\rbrace
\end{equation*}
is accepted. After $J$ rejected main trials, the current ratio is $2^J$.
This proves~\eqref{eq:adaptive_rejected_prefix}.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{lem:adaptive_error_bound}
Suppose that $f$ is convex and either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds.
For every accepted iterate of Algorithm~\ref{alg:fully_adaptive_cubic},
\begin{equation}
  f(w_k)-f^\ast
  \leq\frac{2}{3}\Gamma_kR^3.
  \label{eq:adaptive_error_bound}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
The induction in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:adaptive_backtracking} shows
that~\eqref{eq:current_invariant} holds for every accepted iteration. The
argument in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:global_error_bounds}, applied with
$\bar R=R$, proves~\eqref{eq:adaptive_error_bound}.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
\label{lem:adaptive_far_regime}
Suppose that $f$ is convex, either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds, and
$\Gamma_k>\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}}^{\rm ad}$. Then
\begin{equation}
  \alpha_k
  \geq
  \frac{1}{2+(144\widehat B)^{1/3}},
  \label{eq:adaptive_far_weight_bound}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
  \Gamma_{k+1}
  \leq
  \exp\left(
    -\frac{1}{2+(144\widehat B)^{1/3}}
  \right)\Gamma_k.
  \label{eq:adaptive_far_contraction}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
By~\eqref{eq:adaptive_gamma_transition},
$\widehat B\Gamma_k>4M_0$. Therefore,
equation~\eqref{eq:adaptive_regularization_upper} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \mathcal{M}_k\leq\widehat B\Gamma_k,
  \qquad
  \frac{\alpha_k^3}{1-\alpha_k}
  =\frac{\Gamma_k}{72\mathcal{M}_k}
  \geq\frac{1}{72\widehat B}.
\end{equation*}
If $\alpha_k\leq1/2$, then
\begin{equation*}
  \alpha_k^3\geq\frac{1}{144\widehat B}.
\end{equation*}
If $\alpha_k>1/2$, the bound $\alpha_k>1/2$ holds directly. Hence,
\begin{equation*}
  \alpha_k
  \geq
  \min\left\lbrace
    \frac12,
    \frac{1}{(144\widehat B)^{1/3}}
  \right\rbrace
  \geq
  \frac{1}{2+(144\widehat B)^{1/3}}.
\end{equation*}
This proves~\eqref{eq:adaptive_far_weight_bound}.
Equation~\eqref{eq:adaptive_far_contraction} follows from
$\Gamma_{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)\Gamma_k$ and
$1-t\leq\exp(-t)$.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
\label{lem:adaptive_near_regime}
Suppose that $f$ is convex, either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds, and
$\Gamma_K\leq\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}}^{\rm ad}$. Then, for every $j\geq K$,
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal{M}_j\leq4M_0.
  \label{eq:adaptive_near_regularization}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
  A_{K+n}^{1/3}
  \geq
  A_K^{1/3}
  +\frac{n}{3}\left(\frac{\Gamma_0}{288M_0}\right)^{1/3},
  \qquad n\geq1,
  \label{eq:adaptive_near_growth}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{gather}
  \Gamma_{K+n}\leq\frac{7776M_0}{n^3},
  \label{eq:adaptive_near_gamma_bound}\\
  f(w_{K+n})-f^\ast
  \leq\frac{5184M_0R^3}{n^3},
  \qquad n\geq1.
  \label{eq:adaptive_near_function_bound}
\end{gather}
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
The sequence $\{\Gamma_k\}_{k\geq0}$ is decreasing. Thus,
$\widehat B\Gamma_j\leq4M_0$ for every $j\geq K$, and
equation~\eqref{eq:adaptive_regularization_upper} proves
\eqref{eq:adaptive_near_regularization}. By~\eqref{eq:equivalent_weights},
\begin{equation*}
  a_{j+1}^3
  =\frac{\Gamma_0A_{j+1}^2}{72\mathcal{M}_j}
  \geq\frac{\Gamma_0A_{j+1}^2}{288M_0}.
\end{equation*}
Therefore,
\begin{gather*}
  A_{j+1}^{1/3}-A_j^{1/3}
  =\frac{a_{j+1}}
  {A_{j+1}^{2/3}+A_{j+1}^{1/3}A_j^{1/3}+A_j^{2/3}}\\
  \geq
  \frac{a_{j+1}}{3A_{j+1}^{2/3}}
  \geq
  \frac13\left(\frac{\Gamma_0}{288M_0}\right)^{1/3}.
\end{gather*}
Summing this inequality proves~\eqref{eq:adaptive_near_growth}. Hence,
\begin{equation*}
  A_{K+n}\geq\frac{n^3\Gamma_0}{7776M_0},
  \qquad
  \Gamma_{K+n}=\frac{\Gamma_0}{A_{K+n}}
  \leq\frac{7776M_0}{n^3}.
\end{equation*}
This proves~\eqref{eq:adaptive_near_gamma_bound}. Combining it with
\eqref{eq:adaptive_error_bound} proves
\eqref{eq:adaptive_near_function_bound}.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
If $\nabla f(x_0)=0$, then $x_0$ is optimal by convexity. Otherwise,
Lemma~\ref{lem:cubic_initialization} shows that the initialization
backtracking terminates, gives~\eqref{eq:inital_cnd2}, and proves the stated
bound on the number of rejected initialization trials.

  Lemma~\ref{lem:adaptive_error_bound} gives~\eqref{eq:adaptive_error_bound}.
It remains to consider $0<\varepsilon<f(w_0)-f^\ast$; otherwise the convergence
claim and the rejected-trial bound are immediate. In this case,
condition~\eqref{eq:inital_cnd2} implies
$\Gamma_0>3\varepsilon/R^3$, so the first index below is positive.
Let $N$ be the first index satisfying
\begin{equation*}
  \Gamma_N\leq\frac{3\varepsilon}{2R^3}.
\end{equation*}
Then~\eqref{eq:adaptive_error_bound} gives $f(w_N)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon$.

As long as
  $\Gamma_k>\max\left\lbrace\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}}^{\rm ad},3\varepsilon/(2R^3)\right\rbrace$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:adaptive_far_regime} gives geometric contraction. Therefore,
after at most
\begin{equation*}
  N_{\rm far}
  :=
  \left\lceil
    \left(2+(144\widehat B)^{1/3}\right)
    \log\max\left\lbrace
      1,
      \frac{\Gamma_0}
      {\max\left\lbrace\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}}^{\rm ad},3\varepsilon/(2R^3)\right\rbrace}
    \right\rbrace
  \right\rceil
\end{equation*}
iterations, either $\Gamma_k\leq3\varepsilon/(2R^3)$, or the near regime begins.
In the second case, Lemma~\ref{lem:adaptive_near_regime} shows that
\begin{equation*}
  N_{\rm near}
  :=
  \left\lceil
    \left(\frac{5184M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{1/3}
  \right\rceil
\end{equation*}
additional iterations suffice. Consequently, $N\leq N_{\rm far}+N_{\rm near}$.
By~\eqref{eq:adaptive_gamma_transition},
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{\Gamma_0}
  {\max\left\lbrace\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}}^{\rm ad},3\varepsilon/(2R^3)\right\rbrace}
  =
  \min\left\lbrace
    \frac{\widehat B\Gamma_0}{4M_0},
    \frac{2\Gamma_0R^3}{3\varepsilon}
  \right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
Thus,
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  N\leq
  \left\lceil
    \left(2+(144\widehat B)^{1/3}\right)
    \log\max\left\lbrace
      1,
      \min\left\lbrace
        \frac{\widehat B\Gamma_0}{4M_0},
        \frac{2\Gamma_0R^3}{3\varepsilon}
      \right\rbrace
    \right\rbrace
  \right\rceil
  +\left\lceil
    \left(\frac{5184M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{1/3}
  \right\rceil.
\end{aligned}
  \label{eq:adaptive_explicit_complexity}
\end{equation}
Under~\eqref{as:gh}, definition~\eqref{eq:adaptive_B} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \widehat B^{1/3}
  =\mathcal{O}\left(1+\sqrt{M_1}R\right).
\end{equation*}
Under~\eqref{as:lh}, it gives
\begin{equation*}
  \widehat B^{1/3}
  =\mathcal{O}\left(1+\sqrt{M_1}R+\frac{R}{\rho}\right).
\end{equation*}
Substituting these estimates into~\eqref{eq:adaptive_explicit_complexity}
proves~\eqref{eq:adaptive_global_rate} and
\eqref{eq:adaptive_local_rate}.

The minimality of $N$ gives
\begin{equation*}
  \Gamma_{N-1}>\frac{3\varepsilon}{2R^3},
  \qquad
  \frac{2M_0}{\Gamma_{N-1}}
  <\frac{4M_0R^3}{3\varepsilon}.
\end{equation*}
Therefore,~\eqref{eq:adaptive_rejected_prefix} proves that
the main
backtracking loops reject at most
$
  \left\lceil
    \log_2\max\left\lbrace
      1,
      B,
      \tfrac{4M_0R^3}{3\varepsilon}
    \right\rbrace
  \right\rceil
$
trials.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{thm:ahpe_convergence}
Suppose that $f$ is convex,~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} holds, and
either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds. Assume that $R>0$.
For every $\varepsilon>0$, the method generates an iterate $w_N$ satisfying
$f(w_N)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon$ within
\begin{equation*}
  N=\mathcal{O}\left(
    B\left(1+\log_+\tfrac{R^2}
                            {2A_1\max\left\lbrace\varepsilon,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace}\right)
    +\left(\tfrac{M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{1/3}
    +\sqrt{\tfrac{\delta R^2}{\varepsilon}}
  \right)
\end{equation*}
iterations. The number of rejections is at most
\begin{equation*}
  \left\lceil\log_2\max\left\lbrace
  1,\tfrac{4\delta}{\tau_0},
  \tfrac{2\sqrt{L(x_0)\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}}{\tau_0},
  \tfrac{2\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}{\rho\tau_0}
  \right\rbrace\right\rceil\allowbreak
  +\left\lceil\log_2\max\left\lbrace
  B^2,\tfrac{4\delta R^2}{\varepsilon},
  \left(\tfrac{20M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/3}
  \right\rbrace\right\rceil.
\end{equation*}
Moreover, there exists an integer $K\geq1$ with
$K=\mathcal{O}\left( B\max\left\lbrace1,\log\tfrac{R^2}{2A_1\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}\right\rbrace\right)$ such that
\begin{gather*}
  f(w_k)-f^\ast
  =\mathcal{O}\left(\tfrac{R^2}{A_1}\exp\left(-\tfrac{c(k-1)}B\right)\right),
  \qquad 1\leq k\leq K,\\
  f(w_{K+n})-f^\ast
  =\mathcal{O}\left(\tfrac{M_0R^3}{(B+n)^3}+\tfrac{\delta R^2}{(B+n)^2}\right),
  \qquad n=0,1,\ldots.
\end{gather*}
Here $c>0$ and the constants in $\mathcal{O}(\cdot)$ are universal.
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_weight_relations}
For every main-loop trial of Algorithm~\ref{alg:adaptive_ahpe},
the parameters defined in~\eqref{eq:ahpe_weights} satisfy
\begin{equation*}
  A_{k+1}=A_k+a_{k+1},
  \quad \frac{a_{k+1}^2}{A_{k+1}}=\frac1{\tau_k},
  \quad
  v_k=\frac{A_kw_k+a_{k+1}z_k}{A_{k+1}},
  \quad A_{k+1}\tau_k=\frac1{\alpha_k^2}.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
By~\eqref{eq:ahpe_weights}, we have
\begin{equation*}
  \alpha_k
  =\frac{2}{1+\sqrt{1+4A_k\tau_k}}
  =\frac{\sqrt{1+4A_k\tau_k}-1}{2A_k\tau_k}.
\end{equation*}
Thus $\alpha_k$ is the positive root of the quadratic equation
\begin{equation}
  A_k\tau_k\alpha_k^2+\alpha_k=1,
  \qquad \frac{\alpha_k^2}{1-\alpha_k}=\frac1{A_k\tau_k}.
  \label{eq:ahpe_alpha_identity}
\end{equation}
Using~\eqref{eq:ahpe_weights} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_alpha_identity} gives
\begin{equation*}
  A_{k+1}-a_{k+1}
  =(1-\alpha_k)A_{k+1}=A_k,\qquad
  \frac{a_{k+1}^2}{A_{k+1}}
  =\alpha_k^2A_{k+1}
  =\frac{\alpha_k^2A_k}{1-\alpha_k}
  =\frac1{\tau_k}.
\end{equation*}
The definition of $v_k$ and the identities above imply
\begin{gather*}
  v_k=(1-\alpha_k)w_k+\alpha_kz_k
  =\frac{A_k}{A_{k+1}}w_k+\frac{a_{k+1}}{A_{k+1}}z_k
  =\frac{A_kw_k+a_{k+1}z_k}{A_{k+1}},\\
  A_{k+1}\tau_k
  =\frac{A_{k+1}^2}{a_{k+1}^2}
  =\frac1{\alpha_k^2}.
\end{gather*}
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- lemma-30: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_frozen_remainder}
Suppose that either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds.
Fix $w,v,s\in\mathbb{R}^d$, set $y:= v+s$, and let $H(w)$
satisfy~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} at $w$. Under~\eqref{as:lh}, assume additionally that
\begin{equation*}
  \|{v-w} \|+\|{s} \|\leq\rho.
\end{equation*}
Then
\begin{equation}
  \|{\nabla f(y)-\nabla f(v)-H(w)s} \|
  \leq\left(\delta+L(y)\left(\|{v-w} \|+\frac32\|{s} \|\right)\right)\|{s} \|.
  \label{eq:ahpe_frozen_remainder}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-30 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
By Lemmas~\ref{lem:global_taylor_remainders}~\ref{lem:local_taylor_remainders} and assumption of the lemma
\begin{equation*}
  \|{\nabla f(y)-\nabla f(v)-\nabla^2f(y)s} \|
  =\|{\nabla f(y-s)-\nabla f(y)+\nabla^2f(y)s} \|
  \leq\frac{L(y)}2\|{s} \|^2.
\end{equation*}
Also,
\begin{equation*}
  \|{y-w} \|=\|{v+s-w} \|\leq\|{v-w} \|+\|{s} \|,
\end{equation*}
which is at most $\rho$ under~\eqref{as:lh}.
Applying~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} with base point $y$,
together with~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} at $w$, gives
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla^2f(y)-H(w)} \|
  \leq\|{\nabla^2f(y)-\nabla^2f(w)} \|
       +\|{\nabla^2f(w)-H(w)} \|\\
  \leq L(y)\|{y-w} \|+\delta
  \leq\delta+L(y)\left(\|{v-w} \|+\|{s} \|\right).
\end{gather*}
Adding and subtracting $\nabla^2f(y)s$, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla f(y)-\nabla f(v)-H(w)s} \|
  \leq\|{\nabla f(y)-\nabla f(v)-\nabla^2f(y)s} \|
       +\|{\nabla^2f(y)-H(w)} \|\|{s} \|\\
  \leq\frac{L(y)}2\|{s} \|^2
       +\left(\delta+L(y)\left(\|{v-w} \|+\|{s} \|\right)\right)\|{s} \|
  =\left(\delta+L(y)\left(\|{v-w} \|+\frac32\|{s} \|\right)\right)\|{s} \|.
\end{gather*}
This proves~\eqref{eq:ahpe_frozen_remainder}.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_energy}
Let $f$ be convex and differentiable.
Fix $w,z\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and $A\geq0$. Choose $a>0$ and $\tau>0$ such that
\begin{equation*}
  A_+:= A+a,
  \qquad \frac{a^2}{A_+}=\frac1\tau,
  \qquad v:=\frac{A}{A_+}w+\frac{a}{A_+}z.
\end{equation*}
Let $\mathsf{MS}(v,\tau,s)$ in~\eqref{eq:ahpe_appendix_tests} hold, i.e.
\begin{equation}
  \label{eq:app_test}
  \|{\nabla f(v+s)+\tau s} \|\leq\frac{\tau}{2}\|{s} \|,
\end{equation}
and define
\begin{equation*}
  y:= v+s,
  \qquad z_+:= z-a\nabla f(y).
\end{equation*}
Then
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  A_+(f(y)-f^\ast)+\frac12\|{z_+-x^\ast} \|^2
  \leq A(f(w)-f^\ast)+\frac12\|{z-x^\ast} \|^2 -\frac38 A_+\tau\|{s} \|^2.
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:ahpe_energy_step}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
Set $g:=\nabla f(y)$. Squaring~\eqref{eq:app_test} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \|{g} \|^2+2\tau\left\langle g,s\right\rangle+\tau^2\|{s} \|^2
  =\|{g+\tau s} \|^2
  \leq\frac{\tau^2}{4}\|{s} \|^2.
\end{equation*}
Rearranging and dividing by $2\tau>0$, we obtain
\begin{equation}
  \left\langle g,s\right\rangle
  \leq-\frac{1}{2\tau}\|{g} \|^2-\frac{3\tau}{8}\|{s} \|^2.
  \label{eq:ahpe_residual_progress}
\end{equation}
Convexity at $y$ gives
\begin{equation*}
  f(w)\geq f(y)+\left\langle g,w-y\right\rangle,
  \qquad f^\ast\geq f(y)+\left\langle g,x^\ast-y\right\rangle.
\end{equation*}
Multiply these inequalities by $A$ and $a$, respectively, and add them:
\begin{equation*}
  Af(w)+af^\ast
  \geq A_+f(y)+\left\langle g,Aw+ax^\ast-A_+y\right\rangle.
\end{equation*}
The identities $A_+v=Aw+az$ and $y=v+s$ imply
\begin{equation*}
  Aw+ax^\ast-A_+y
  =Aw+ax^\ast-(Aw+az)-A_+s
  =a(x^\ast-z)-A_+s.
\end{equation*}
Substituting this identity and using $A_+=A+a$ yields
\begin{equation}
  A_+(f(y)-f^\ast)
  \leq A(f(w)-f^\ast)+a\left\langle g,z-x^\ast\right\rangle+A_+\left\langle g,s\right\rangle.
  \label{eq:ahpe_convexity_step}
\end{equation}
The update $z_+=z-ag$ gives
\begin{equation}
  \frac12\|{z_+-x^\ast} \|^2
  =\frac12\|{z-x^\ast-ag} \|^2
  =\frac12\|{z-x^\ast} \|^2-a\left\langle g,z-x^\ast\right\rangle
    +\frac{a^2}{2}\|{g} \|^2.
\label{eq:ahpe_distance_step}
\end{equation}
Adding~\eqref{eq:ahpe_convexity_step} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_distance_step} gives 
\begin{equation*}
  A_+(f(y)-f^\ast)+\frac12\|{z_+-x^\ast} \|^2
  \leq A(f(w)-f^\ast)+\frac12\|{z-x^\ast} \|^2
  +A_+\left\langle g,s\right\rangle+\frac{a^2}{2}\|{g} \|^2.
\end{equation*}
Finally,~\eqref{eq:ahpe_residual_progress} and $a^2=A_+/\tau$ give
\begin{equation*}
  A_+\left\langle g,s\right\rangle+\frac{a^2}{2}\|{g} \|^2
  \leq\left(\frac{a^2}{2}-\frac{A_+}{2\tau}\right)\|{g} \|^2
       -\frac38 A_+\tau\|{s} \|^2
  =-\frac38 A_+\tau\|{s} \|^2.
\end{equation*}
Substitution proves~\eqref{eq:ahpe_energy_step}.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_localization}
For every $k\geq1$, the accepted iterates of
Algorithm~\ref{alg:adaptive_ahpe} satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \|{z_k-x^\ast} \|\leq R,
  \label{eq:ahpe_z_bound}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
  \|{w_k-x^\ast} \|\leq\left(1+\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\right) R,
  \qquad
  \|{z_k-w_k} \|\leq\left(2+\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\right) R.
  \label{eq:ahpe_localization}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
By~\eqref{eq:ahpe_energy_budget},
\begin{equation*}
  \frac12\|{z_k-x^\ast} \|^2\leq\mathcal{E}_k\leq\frac{R^2}{2},
\end{equation*}
which gives~\eqref{eq:ahpe_z_bound}.
We prove the bound on $\|{w_k-x^\ast} \|$ by induction.
The initialization bound~\eqref{eq:ahpe_initialization_bound} gives
\begin{gather*}
  \|{w_1-x_0} \|\leq\frac{2}{\sqrt3}R,\\
  \|{w_1-x^\ast} \|
  \leq\|{w_1-x_0} \|+\|{x_0-x^\ast} \|
  \leq\left(1+\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\right) R.
\end{gather*}
Suppose the bound holds for $w_k$. For the next accepted step,
$w_{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)w_k+\alpha_kz_k+s_k$.
Using~\eqref{eq:ahpe_certified_bounds} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_z_bound}, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \|{w_{k+1}-x^\ast} \|
  \leq(1-\alpha_k)\|{w_k-x^\ast} \|
       +\alpha_k\|{z_k-x^\ast} \|+\|{s_k} \|\\
  \leq(1-\alpha_k)\left(1+\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\right) R
       +\alpha_k R+\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\alpha_k R
  =\left(1+\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\right) R.
\end{gather*}
This completes the induction. The bound on $\|{z_k-w_k} \|$ follows from
\begin{equation*}
  \|{z_k-w_k} \|
  \leq\|{z_k-x^\ast} \|+\|{w_k-x^\ast} \|
  \leq\left(2+\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\right) R.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_safe_parameter}
Suppose that $f$ is convex and either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds.
Fix an accepted state $A_k,w_k,z_k$ of Algorithm~\ref{alg:adaptive_ahpe}
and a matrix $H(w_k)$ satisfying~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} at $w_k$.
Every main-loop trial with
\begin{equation}
  \tau\geq\frac{Q(A_k)}{A_k}
  \label{eq:ahpe_safe_parameter}
\end{equation}
satisfies $\mathsf{PD}(w_k,\tau)$ and $\mathsf{MS}(v,\tau,s)$
in~\eqref{eq:ahpe_appendix_tests}, where the trial weights are defined
by~\eqref{eq:ahpe_weights} with $\tau_k=\tau$,
$v=(1-\alpha_k)w_k+\alpha_kz_k$, and $s$ is given
by~\eqref{eq:ahpe_appendix_trial_step} with $w=w_k$.
<!-- end lemma-33 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
Keep $A_k,w_k,z_k,H(w_k)$ fixed and vary $q\geq Q(A_k)$ continuously.
For each $q$, use the weights in~\eqref{eq:ahpe_weights} with
$\tau_k=\tau(q)$, where
\begin{gather*}
  \tau(q):=\frac{q}{A_k},
  \quad
  \alpha(q):=\frac{2}{1+\sqrt{1+4q}}, \quad
  v(q):=(1-\alpha(q))w_k+\alpha(q)z_k.
\end{gather*}
Convexity and~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} give $H(w_k)\succeq-\delta I$.
Since $q\geq Q(A_k)\geq\max\left\lbrace1,8\delta A_k\right\rbrace$, we have
\begin{equation*}
  H(w_k)+\tau(q)I
  \succeq(\tau(q)-\delta)I
  \succeq\frac78\tau(q)I\succ0.
\end{equation*}
Thus, $\mathsf{PD}(w_k,\tau(q))$ holds throughout this range, and
we can define
\begin{gather*}
  s(q):=-\left( H(w_k)+\tau(q)I\right)^{-1}\nabla f(v(q)),
  \qquad y(q):= v(q)+s(q),\\
  d(q):=\|{v(q)-w_k} \|=\alpha(q)\|{z_k-w_k} \|,
  \qquad r(q):=\|{s(q)} \|.
\end{gather*}
All these quantities are continuous because $H(w_k)$ is fixed and the
inverse exists. As $q\to+\infty$,
\begin{gather*}
  \tau(q)\to+\infty,~~\alpha(q)\to0,~~v(q)\to w_k,~~ d(q)\to0,~~
  r(q)\leq\frac{\|{\nabla f(v(q))} \|}{\tau(q)-\delta}\to0,~~ y(q)\to w_k.
\end{gather*}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:ahpe_frozen_remainder} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_appendix_trial_step},
the following conditions are sufficient for the test~\eqref{eq:ahpe_appendix_tests}:
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  d(q)+r(q) \leq\rho~~\text{only under~\eqref{as:lh}},\quad
  \delta+L(y(q))\left( d(q)+\frac32r(q)\right) \leq\frac{\tau(q)}2.
\end{aligned}
  \label{eq:ahpe_sufficient_conditions}
\end{equation}
Indeed, if~\eqref{eq:ahpe_sufficient_conditions} holds, then
Lemma~\ref{lem:ahpe_frozen_remainder} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_appendix_trial_step} give
\begin{gather*}
  \|{\nabla f(y(q))+\tau(q)s(q)} \|
  =\|{\nabla f(y(q))-\nabla f(v(q))-H(w_k)s(q)} \|\\
  \leq\left(\delta+L(y(q))\left( d(q)+\frac32r(q)\right)\right) r(q)
  \leq\frac{\tau(q)}2\|{s(q)} \|.
\end{gather*}
Since $L(y(q))\to L(w_k)$,
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{\delta+L(y(q))\left( d(q)+\frac32r(q)\right)}{\tau(q)}\to0.
\end{equation*}
Hence, all sufficiently large $q$ satisfy~\eqref{eq:ahpe_sufficient_conditions}
strictly.

Let $\mathcal U_k$ be the set of $q\geq Q(A_k)$ for which at least one
condition in~\eqref{eq:ahpe_sufficient_conditions} fails.
If $\mathcal U_k=\emptyset$, the statement follows.
Otherwise, set $q^\dagger:=\sup\mathcal U_k$.
Since the conditions in~\eqref{eq:ahpe_sufficient_conditions} hold for all
sufficiently large $q$, the set $\mathcal U_k$ is bounded above.
Hence, $q^\dagger<+\infty$.
By continuity, $q^\dagger$ lies on the boundary of the admissible set.
Hence, the conditions in~\eqref{eq:ahpe_sufficient_conditions} hold at
$q^\dagger$, and at least one is an equality.
A dagger below denotes evaluation at $q^\dagger$.

The boundary trial therefore satisfies the test~\eqref{eq:ahpe_sufficient_conditions}.
Moreover,~\eqref{eq:ahpe_energy_budget} gives $\mathcal{E}_k\leq\frac{R^2}{2}$.
Consequently, the bounds~\eqref{eq:ahpe_certified_bounds} apply to this trial.
Together with~\eqref{eq:ahpe_localization}, they give
\begin{equation}
  r^\dagger\leq\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\alpha^\dagger R, 
  \quad
  \|{\nabla f(y^\dagger)} \|
  \leq\frac32\tau^\dagger r^\dagger
  \leq\sqrt3\tau^\dagger\alpha^\dagger R, \quad
  d^\dagger=\alpha^\dagger\|{z_k-w_k} \|
  \leq\left(2+\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\right)\alpha^\dagger R.
  \label{eq:ahpe_boundary_bounds}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
  d^\dagger+r^\dagger
  \leq d^\dagger+\frac32r^\dagger
  \leq\left(2+\frac{5}{\sqrt3}\right)\alpha^\dagger R
  \leq5\alpha^\dagger R.
  \label{eq:ahpe_boundary_distances}
\end{equation}
The definition of $\alpha(q)$ gives
\begin{equation*}
  \alpha^\dagger=\frac{2}{1+\sqrt{1+4q^\dagger}}
  \leq\frac1{\sqrt{q^\dagger}}.
\end{equation*}
By~\eqref{eq:ahpe_safe_threshold}, we have $q^\dagger\geq Q(A_k)\geq B^2$.
Under~\eqref{as:lh}, definition~\eqref{eq:ahpe_B} also gives
$B\geq\frac{8R}{\rho}$.
Together with~\eqref{eq:ahpe_boundary_distances}, this gives
\begin{equation*}
  d^\dagger+r^\dagger
  \leq\frac{5R}{\sqrt{q^\dagger}}
  \leq\frac{5R}{B}
  \leq\frac58\rho<\rho.
\end{equation*}
Using $L(y^\dagger)=M_0+M_1\|{\nabla f(y^\dagger)} \|$,
equations~\eqref{eq:ahpe_boundary_bounds} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_boundary_distances}
give
\begin{gather*}
  \frac{\delta+L(y^\dagger)\left( d^\dagger+\frac32r^\dagger\right)}
       {\tau^\dagger}
  \leq\frac{\delta}{\tau^\dagger}
       +\frac{5M_0R\alpha^\dagger}{\tau^\dagger}
       +5\sqrt3M_1R^2(\alpha^\dagger)^2\\
  \leq\frac{\delta A_k}{q^\dagger}
       +\frac{5M_0RA_k}{(q^\dagger)^{3/2}}
       +\frac{5\sqrt3M_1R^2}{q^\dagger}
  \leq\frac18+\frac18+\frac{5\sqrt3}{64}<\frac12,
\end{gather*}
where we used $q^\dagger\geq Q(A_k)$,~\eqref{eq:ahpe_safe_threshold},
and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_B}.
Thus, all conditions in~\eqref{eq:ahpe_sufficient_conditions} are strict
at $q^\dagger$, contradicting its boundary property.
Therefore, $\mathcal U_k=\emptyset$, and every trial
satisfying~\eqref{eq:ahpe_safe_parameter} passes both tests.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- lemma-34: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_backtracking}
Suppose that $f$ is convex,~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} holds, and
either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds.
Every main backtracking loop of Algorithm~\ref{alg:adaptive_ahpe} terminates.
For every $k\geq1$, let $\tau_k$ denote the parameter accepted at iteration $k$.
Then
\begin{equation}
  A_k\tau_k\leq2Q(A_k).
  \label{eq:ahpe_parameter_upper}
\end{equation}
For every $K\geq1$, let $J_K$ be the total number of rejected main trials
during iterations $1,\ldots,K$, excluding initialization. Then
\begin{equation}
  J_K\leq\left\lceil\log_2 Q(A_K)\right\rceil.
  \label{eq:ahpe_rejected_prefix}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-34 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
We prove by induction on $k$ that iteration $k$ is reached after
finitely many trials. The case $k=1$ follows from
Lemma~\ref{lem:pd_ms_backtracking} with $(w_1, \tau_1) = \textnormal{\textsc{MSBacktrack}}(x_0, \tau_0)$ and $\overline{\tau}_0 := \overline{\tau}(x_0)$.
Suppose this holds for some $k\geq1$.
Then~\eqref{eq:ahpe_energy_budget} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_localization} hold.
Since $A_k$ is fixed, repeated doubling reaches
$\tau\geq\frac{Q(A_k)}{A_k}$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:ahpe_safe_parameter}
guarantees acceptance. Thus, iteration $k+1$ is reached after finitely
many trials, completing the induction.

We next track the product of the current weight and trial parameter.
By~\eqref{eq:ahpe_initialization}, before the first main trial this product is
\begin{equation*}
  A_1\tau_1=\frac1{\tau_1}{\tau_1}=1.
\end{equation*}
After accepting iteration $k$, the first trial at iteration $k+1$ uses
$\tau=(1-\alpha_k)\tau_k$. By~\eqref{eq:ahpe_weights}, its product is
\begin{equation*}
  A_{k+1}(1-\alpha_k)\tau_k
  =\frac{A_k}{1-\alpha_k}(1-\alpha_k)\tau_k
  =A_k\tau_k.
\end{equation*}
Every rejected trial doubles $\tau_k$, while $A_k$ remains unchanged.
Therefore,
\begin{equation}
  A_k\tau_k=2^{J_k},\qquad k\geq1.
  \label{eq:ahpe_rejection_product}
\end{equation}
Fix $K\geq1$. The weights increase by~\eqref{eq:ahpe_weights}, and
$Q$ is nondecreasing by~\eqref{eq:ahpe_safe_threshold}. Hence,
$Q(A_i)\leq Q(A_K)$ for every $i\leq K$.
If $J_K=0$, then~\eqref{eq:ahpe_rejection_product} and $Q(A_K)\geq B^2\geq1$
give both~\eqref{eq:ahpe_parameter_upper} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_rejected_prefix}.

Suppose that $J_K\geq1$, and let $i\leq K$ be the iteration at which the
last rejection occurs. For this trial, the product of $A_i$ and the trial
parameter is $2^{J_K-1}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:ahpe_safe_parameter}, the trial
would be accepted if this product were at least $Q(A_i)$. Therefore,
\begin{equation*}
  2^{J_K-1}<Q(A_i)\leq Q(A_K).
\end{equation*}
Multiplying by $2$ and using~\eqref{eq:ahpe_rejection_product}, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
  A_K\tau_K=2^{J_K}<2Q(A_K),
\end{equation*}
which proves~\eqref{eq:ahpe_parameter_upper}.
Taking logarithms in $2^{J_K-1}<Q(A_K)$ gives
$J_K<1+\log_2 Q(A_K)$. Since $J_K$ is an integer,
\begin{equation*}
  J_K\leq\left\lceil\log_2 Q(A_K)\right\rceil,
\end{equation*}
which proves~\eqref{eq:ahpe_rejected_prefix}.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- lemma-35: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_weight_growth}
Under the assumptions of Lemma~\ref{lem:ahpe_backtracking}, suppose that $R>0$.
For the accepted steps of Algorithm~\ref{alg:adaptive_ahpe}, the following
bounds hold for every $k\geq1$.
If $A_k\leq A_{\mathrm{tr}}$, then
\begin{equation}
  A_{k+1}\geq\exp\left(\frac1{3B}\right) A_k.
  \label{eq:ahpe_geometric_growth}
\end{equation}
If $A_k\geq A_{\mathrm{tr}}$, then
\begin{equation}
  \sqrt{Q(A_{k+1})}-\sqrt{Q(A_k)}\geq\frac19.
  \label{eq:ahpe_scale_growth}
\end{equation}
In particular, for any $K\geq1$ with $A_K\geq A_{\mathrm{tr}}$ and
every integer $n\geq0$,
\begin{equation}
  \sqrt{Q(A_{K+n})}\geq\sqrt{Q(A_K)}+\frac n9\geq B+\frac n9.
  \label{eq:ahpe_cumulative_growth}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-35 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
By~\eqref{eq:ahpe_parameter_upper}, the accepted parameter satisfies
$A_k\tau_k\leq2Q(A_k)$. Since $\sqrt{Q(A_k)}\geq B\geq1$,
the definition of $\alpha_k$ in~\eqref{eq:ahpe_weights} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \frac1{\alpha_k}
  =\frac{1+\sqrt{1+4A_k\tau_k}}2
  \leq\frac{1+\sqrt{1+8Q(A_k)}}2
  \leq3\sqrt{Q(A_k)}.
\end{equation*}
Hence,
\begin{equation}
  \alpha_k\geq\frac1{3\sqrt{Q(A_k)}},\qquad k\geq1.
  \label{eq:ahpe_alpha_lower}
\end{equation}
If $A_k\leq A_{\mathrm{tr}}$,
$\max\left\lbrace(40M_0RA_k)^{1/3},\sqrt{8\delta A_k}\right\rbrace \leq B$. Thus, by definition of $Q(A_k)$, we have $B=\sqrt{Q(A_k)}$. By~\eqref{eq:ahpe_alpha_lower}, $\alpha_k\geq\frac1{3B}$.
Using~\eqref{eq:ahpe_weights} and
$1-t\leq\exp(-t)$ for $0\leq t<1$, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
  A_{k+1}=\frac{A_k}{1-\alpha_k}
  \geq\exp(\alpha_k)A_k
  \geq\exp\left(\frac1{3B}\right) A_k,
\end{equation*}
which proves~\eqref{eq:ahpe_geometric_growth}.

Since $A\geq A_{\mathrm{tr}}$, $B\leq\max\left\lbrace(40M_0RA)^{1/3},\sqrt{8\delta A}\right\rbrace=\sqrt{Q(A)}$.
Suppose that $A_k\geq A_{\mathrm{tr}}$.
Since $A_{k+1}>A_k\geq A_{\mathrm{tr}}$, the identity holds
for $A=A_k$ and $A=A_{k+1}$.
Since $0<1-\alpha_k<1$, substitution
of~\eqref{eq:ahpe_weights} gives
\begin{gather*}
  \sqrt{Q(A_{k+1})}
  =\max\left\lbrace
    \frac{(40M_0RA_k)^{1/3}}{(1-\alpha_k)^{1/3}},
    \frac{\sqrt{8\delta A_k}}{(1-\alpha_k)^{1/2}}
  \right\rbrace\\
  \geq\frac{\max\left\lbrace(40M_0RA_k)^{1/3},\sqrt{8\delta A_k}\right\rbrace}
               {(1-\alpha_k)^{1/3}}
  =\frac{\sqrt{Q(A_k)}}{(1-\alpha_k)^{1/3}}.
\end{gather*}
The inequality $(1-t)^{-1/3}\geq1+\frac t3$ for $0\leq t<1$
and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_alpha_lower} now imply
\begin{equation*}
  \sqrt{Q(A_{k+1})}-\sqrt{Q(A_k)}
  \geq\sqrt{Q(A_k)}\left((1-\alpha_k)^{-1/3}-1\right)
  \geq\frac{\alpha_k\sqrt{Q(A_k)}}3
  \geq\frac19.
\end{equation*}
This proves~\eqref{eq:ahpe_scale_growth}.
Finally, if $A_K\geq A_{\mathrm{tr}}$, then $A_j\geq A_{\mathrm{tr}}$
for every $j\geq K$. Summing~\eqref{eq:ahpe_scale_growth} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \sqrt{Q(A_{K+n})}
  =\sqrt{Q(A_K)}
  +\sum_{j=K}^{K+n-1}\left(\sqrt{Q(A_{j+1})}-\sqrt{Q(A_j)}\right)
  \geq\sqrt{Q(A_K)}+\frac n9
  \geq B+\frac n9,
\end{equation*}
which proves~\eqref{eq:ahpe_cumulative_growth}.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
\label{thm:ahpe_convergence_appendix}
Suppose that $f$ is convex,~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} holds, and
either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds. Assume that $R>0$.
All backtracking loops in Algorithm~\ref{alg:adaptive_ahpe} terminate.
For every $\varepsilon>0$, the method generates an iterate $w_N$ satisfying
$f(w_N)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon$ within
\begin{equation}
  N=\mathcal{O}\left(
    B\left(1+\log_+\frac{R^2}
                            {2A_1\max\left\lbrace\varepsilon,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace}\right)
    +\left(\frac{M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{1/3}
    +\sqrt{\frac{\delta R^2}{\varepsilon}}
  \right)
  \label{eq:app_ahpe_iteration_complexity}
\end{equation}
iterations. Under~\eqref{as:gh}, initialization rejects at most
\begin{equation}
  \left\lceil\log_2\max\left\lbrace
    1,\frac{4\delta}{\tau_0},
    \frac{2\sqrt{L(x_0)\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}}{\tau_0}
  \right\rbrace\right\rceil
  \label{eq:app_ahpe_initialization_cost}
\end{equation}
trials. Under~\eqref{as:lh}, the maximum additionally includes
$\frac{2\|{\nabla f(x_0)} \|}{\rho\tau_0}$.
The total number of rejected main-loop trials before producing $w_N$
is at most
\begin{equation}
  \left\lceil\log_2\max\left\lbrace
    B^2,\frac{4\delta R^2}{\varepsilon},
    \left(\frac{20M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/3}
  \right\rbrace\right\rceil.
  \label{eq:app_ahpe_accuracy_rejections}
\end{equation}
Moreover, there exists an integer $K\geq1$ with
\begin{equation}
  K\leq1+\left\lceil
    3B\log_+\frac{R^2}{2A_1\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}
  \right\rceil.
  \label{eq:app_ahpe_transition_index}
\end{equation}
For this $K$,
\begin{gather}
  f(w_k)-f^\ast
  \leq\frac{R^2}{2A_1}\exp\left(-\frac{k-1}{3B}\right),
  \qquad 1\leq k\leq K,
  \label{eq:app_ahpe_far_rate}\\
  f(w_{K+n})-f^\ast
  \leq\max\left\lbrace
    \frac{20M_0R^3}{(B+n/9)^3},
    \frac{4\delta R^2}{(B+n/9)^2}
  \right\rbrace,
  \qquad n=0,1,\ldots.
  \label{eq:app_ahpe_near_rate}
\end{gather}
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Lemmas~\ref{lem:pd_ms_backtracking}
and~\ref{lem:ahpe_backtracking} show that all backtracking loops terminate.
By~\eqref{eq:ahpe_energy_budget},
\begin{equation}
  f(w_k)-f^\ast\leq\frac{\mathcal{E}_k}{A_k}\leq\frac{R^2}{2A_k},
  \qquad k\geq1.
  \label{eq:ahpe_error_certificate}
\end{equation}
Set $K:=\min\left\lbrace k\geq1:A_k\geq A_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace$, with $K=+\infty$
if this set is empty.
If $A_1\geq A_{\mathrm{tr}}$, then $K=1$,
and~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_transition_index} holds.
Otherwise, set
\begin{equation*}
  m:=\left\lceil3B\log\frac{A_{\mathrm{tr}}}{A_1}\right\rceil.
\end{equation*}
If $A_j<A_{\mathrm{tr}}$ for $j=1,\ldots,m$,
then~\eqref{eq:ahpe_geometric_growth} yields
\begin{equation*}
  A_{m+1}\geq A_1\exp\left(\frac{m}{3B}\right)
  \geq A_1\exp\left(\log\frac{A_{\mathrm{tr}}}{A_1}\right)
  =A_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\end{equation*}
The threshold is therefore reached by index $m+1$.
Since $A_{\mathrm{tr}}=\frac{R^2}{2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}$,
this proves~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_transition_index}.

Fix $1\leq k\leq K$.
By the definition of $K$, we have $A_j<A_{\mathrm{tr}}$ for $1\leq j<k$.
Applying~\eqref{eq:ahpe_geometric_growth} successively and
using~\eqref{eq:ahpe_error_certificate} gives
\begin{gather*}
  A_k\geq A_1\exp\left(\frac{k-1}{3B}\right),\\
  f(w_k)-f^\ast\leq\frac{R^2}{2A_k}
  \leq\frac{R^2}{2A_1}\exp\left(-\frac{k-1}{3B}\right).
\end{gather*}
This proves~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_far_rate}.

For every $A\geq A_{\mathrm{tr}}$,
\begin{equation*}
  \sqrt{Q(A)}=\max\left\lbrace(40M_0RA)^{1/3},\sqrt{8\delta A}\right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
Hence, $Q(A)^{3/2}\geq40M_0RA$ and $Q(A)\geq8\delta A$, so
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{20M_0R^3}{Q(A)^{3/2}}\leq\frac{R^2}{2A},
  \qquad
  \frac{4\delta R^2}{Q(A)}\leq\frac{R^2}{2A}.
\end{equation*}
At least one of these inequalities is an equality, because $\sqrt{Q(A)}$ equals
at least one of the two terms defining it. Therefore,
\begin{equation}
  \frac{R^2}{2A}
  =\max\left\lbrace
    \frac{20M_0R^3}{Q(A)^{3/2}},\frac{4\delta R^2}{Q(A)}
  \right\rbrace,
  \qquad A\geq A_{\mathrm{tr}}.
  \label{eq:ahpe_error_scale}
\end{equation}
For $A=A_{K+n}$,
combine~\eqref{eq:ahpe_error_certificate},~\eqref{eq:ahpe_error_scale},
and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_cumulative_growth} to obtain
\begin{gather*}
  f(w_{K+n})-f^\ast\leq\frac{R^2}{2A_{K+n}}
  =\max\left\lbrace
    \frac{20M_0R^3}{Q(A_{K+n})^{3/2}},
    \frac{4\delta R^2}{Q(A_{K+n})}
  \right\rbrace\\
  \leq\max\left\lbrace
    \frac{20M_0R^3}{(B+n/9)^3},
    \frac{4\delta R^2}{(B+n/9)^2}
  \right\rbrace.
\end{gather*}
This proves~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_near_rate}.

It remains to bound the iteration and backtracking counts.
Fix $\varepsilon>0$.
Set
\begin{equation*}
  A_{\varepsilon}:=\frac{R^2}{2\varepsilon},\qquad
  N:=\min\left\lbrace k\geq1:A_k\geq A_{\varepsilon}\right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
By~\eqref{eq:ahpe_cumulative_growth} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_error_scale},
$\frac{R^2}{2A_{K+n}}\to0$ as $n\to+\infty$.
Thus, $N$ is finite, and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_error_certificate} gives
$f(w_N)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon$.

First, suppose that $\varepsilon\geq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$.
Then $A_{\varepsilon}\leq A_{\mathrm{tr}}$, so every iteration with
$A_k<A_{\varepsilon}$ satisfies~\eqref{eq:ahpe_geometric_growth}.
The same argument used to prove~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_transition_index},
with $A_{\varepsilon}$ in place of $A_{\mathrm{tr}}$, gives
\begin{equation*}
  N\leq1+\left\lceil3B\log_+\frac{A_{\varepsilon}}{A_1}\right\rceil
  =1+\left\lceil3B\log_+\frac{R^2}{2A_1\varepsilon}\right\rceil.
\end{equation*}
Now suppose that $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}$. Set
\begin{equation*}
