  n:=\left\lceil9\max\left\lbrace
    \left(\frac{20M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{1/3},
    2\sqrt{\frac{\delta R^2}{\varepsilon}}
  \right\rbrace\right\rceil.
\end{equation*}
Equations~\eqref{eq:ahpe_error_scale} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_cumulative_growth}
give
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{R^2}{2A_{K+n}}
  \leq\max\left\lbrace
    \frac{20M_0R^3}{(B+n/9)^3},
    \frac{4\delta R^2}{(B+n/9)^2}
  \right\rbrace
  \leq\varepsilon.
\end{equation*}
Hence $A_{K+n}\geq A_{\varepsilon}$, and $N\leq K+n$.
Using~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_transition_index}, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
  N\leq1+
  \left\lceil3B\log_+\frac{A_{\mathrm{tr}}}{A_1}\right\rceil
  +\left\lceil9\max\left\lbrace
    \left(\frac{20M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{1/3},
    2\sqrt{\frac{\delta R^2}{\varepsilon}}
  \right\rbrace\right\rceil.
\end{equation*}
Combining the two cases and using~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_transition_error} and $B\geq1$
proves~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_iteration_complexity}.

We now bound the number of rejected trials before producing $w_N$.
If $N=1$, no main trial is needed.
If $N\geq2$, the main iterations needed to compute $w_N$ are
$1,\ldots,N-1$. The minimality of $N$ gives $A_{N-1}<A_{\varepsilon}$.
Since $Q$ is nondecreasing, Lemma~\ref{lem:ahpe_backtracking} yields
\begin{equation*}
  J_{N-1}\leq\left\lceil\log_2Q(A_{N-1})\right\rceil
  \leq\left\lceil\log_2Q(A_{\varepsilon})\right\rceil.
\end{equation*}
Substituting $A_{\varepsilon}=\frac{R^2}{2\varepsilon}$
into~\eqref{eq:ahpe_safe_threshold} gives
\begin{equation*}
  Q(A_{\varepsilon})
  =\max\left\lbrace
    B^2,\frac{4\delta R^2}{\varepsilon},
    \left(\frac{20M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/3}
  \right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
This proves the rejection bound~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_accuracy_rejections}.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:pd_ms_backtracking}, initialization rejects
at most
\begin{equation*}
  \left\lceil
    \log_2\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{\overline\tau_0}{\tau_0}\right\rbrace
  \right\rceil
\end{equation*}
trials, where $\overline\tau_0 = \overline\tau (x_0)$ is defined
in~\eqref{eq:backtrack_upper_bound}.
Substituting~\eqref{eq:backtrack_upper_bound} gives
the initialization bound~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_initialization_cost}
and its counterpart under~\eqref{as:lh}.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{cor:ahpe_oracle_complexity}
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:ahpe_convergence_appendix},
fix $\varepsilon>0$ and let $N$ be the first index with $A_N\geq R^2/(2\varepsilon)$.
Let $\overline\tau_0:=\overline\tau(x_0)$, where $\overline\tau(x)$ is defined in~\eqref{eq:backtrack_upper_bound}.
Then Algorithm~\ref{alg:adaptive_ahpe} computes $w_N$ using at most $N$ Hessian evaluations and at most
\begin{equation*}
  2N+3+\log_{2,+}\frac{\overline\tau_0}{\tau_0}
  +2\log_2\max\left\lbrace B^2,\frac{4\delta R^2}{\varepsilon},\left(\frac{20M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/3}\right\rbrace
\end{equation*}
gradient evaluations.
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Initialization uses one Hessian, the gradient at $x_0$, and at most one gradient per trial.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:pd_ms_backtracking}, it has at most
$2+\log_{2,+}\frac{\overline\tau_0}{\tau_0}$ trials.
Each of the $N-1$ main iterations uses one Hessian $H(w_k)$ and at most two gradients per trial,
$\nabla f(v_k)$ and $\nabla f(v_k+s_k)$, since $v_k$ changes after each rejection.
These iterations have $N-1$ accepted trials, and~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_accuracy_rejections}
bounds the number of rejected ones.
The updates reuse the gradient at the accepted point.
Hence, the number of Hessian evaluations is at most $1+(N-1)=N$, and the number of
gradient evaluations is at most
\begin{gather*}
  1+\left(2+\log_{2,+}\frac{\overline\tau_0}{\tau_0}\right)
  +2\left( N-1+\left\lceil\log_2\max\left\lbrace B^2,\frac{4\delta R^2}{\varepsilon},\left(\frac{20M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/3}\right\rbrace\right\rceil\right)\\
  \leq2N+3+\log_{2,+}\frac{\overline\tau_0}{\tau_0}
  +2\log_2\max\left\lbrace B^2,\frac{4\delta R^2}{\varepsilon},\left(\frac{20M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/3}\right\rbrace.
\end{gather*}
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- lemma-36: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_damped_initialization}
Suppose that $f$ is convex,~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} holds, and
either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds. Initialization in
Algorithm~\ref{alg:ahpe_damped_appendix} (line~\ref{line:ahpe_damped_appendix_initialization}) uses at most
\begin{equation*}
  1+\left\lceil
    \log_2\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{\overline\tau_0}{\eta_0}\right\rbrace
  \right\rceil
\end{equation*}
trials, where $\overline\tau_0 = \overline\tau(x_0)$ from~\eqref{eq:backtrack_upper_bound}, and accepted parameter satisfies
\begin{equation*}
  \eta_0\leq\eta_1\leq\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,2\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace.
\end{equation*} 
The algorithm either returns a minimizer or produces an initial state
$A_1,w_1,z_1,\eta_1$ satisfying $A_1\eta_1=1$ and
\begin{equation}
  A_1(f(w_1)-f^\ast)+\frac12\|{z_1-x^\ast} \|^2
  +\frac38\|{w_1-x_0} \|^2
  \leq\frac{R^2}{2}.
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_initialization_bound}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-36 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
If $\nabla f(x_0)=0$, the algorithm returns $x_0$ without any trials.
Otherwise,
Lemma~\ref{lem:pd_ms_backtracking} with $x=x_0$,
$\eta=\eta_0$, and $\overline\tau(x_0)=\overline\tau_0$ proves the
bound.
For the initialization~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_initialization},
Lemma~\ref{lem:ahpe_energy} applies with $A=0$, $w=z=x_0$,
$a=A_+=A_1=1/\eta_1$, and $\tau=\eta_1$.
The same updates give $y=w_1$ and $z_+=z_1$.
Since $A_1\tau=1$, the lemma yields~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_initialization_bound}.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- lemma-37: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_damped_energy}
Let $f$ be convex.
Every completed main iteration of Algorithm~\ref{alg:ahpe_damped_appendix} satisfies
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal{E}_{k+1}\leq\mathcal{E}_k-\frac38A'_k\eta_k\|{s_k} \|^2,
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_energy_step}
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal{E}_k:= A_k(f(w_k)-f^\ast)+\frac12\|{z_k-x^\ast} \|^2$.
<!-- end lemma-37 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
By~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_trial_weights} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_accepted_weights},
$(a'_k)^2=A'_k/\eta_k$ and $\gamma_k\tau_k=\eta_k$, so
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{a_{k+1}^2}{\gamma_kA'_k}=\frac1{\tau_k},
  \qquad
  v_k=\frac{\gamma_kA_kw_k+a_{k+1}z_k}{\gamma_kA'_k}.
\end{equation*}
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:ahpe_energy} with $A=\gamma_kA_k$,
$a=a_{k+1}$, $A_+=\gamma_kA'_k$, $w=w_k$, $z=z_k$,
and $\tau=\tau_k$. By~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_iterate_updates},
$z_+=z_{k+1}$, so it gives
\begin{equation}
  \gamma_kA'_k(f(y_k)-f^\ast)
  +\frac12\|{z_{k+1}-x^\ast} \|^2
  \leq\gamma_kA_k(f(w_k)-f^\ast)
  +\frac12\|{z_k-x^\ast} \|^2
  -\frac38A'_k\eta_k\|{s_k} \|^2.
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_scaled_energy}
\end{equation}
Since $0<\gamma_k\leq1$ and
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{(1-\gamma_k)A_k}{A_{k+1}}
  +\frac{\gamma_kA'_k}{A_{k+1}}
  =\frac{A_k+\gamma_ka'_k}{A_{k+1}}=1,
\end{equation*}
convexity of $f$ and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_iterate_updates} give
\begin{equation}
  A_{k+1}(f(w_{k+1})-f^\ast)
  \leq(1-\gamma_k)A_k(f(w_k)-f^\ast)
  +\gamma_kA'_k(f(y_k)-f^\ast).
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_convexity}
\end{equation}
Using~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_convexity} and then~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_scaled_energy}, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \mathcal{E}_{k+1}
  =A_{k+1}(f(w_{k+1})-f^\ast)
  +\frac12\|{z_{k+1}-x^\ast} \|^2\\
  \leq(1-\gamma_k)A_k(f(w_k)-f^\ast)
  +\gamma_kA'_k(f(y_k)-f^\ast)
  +\frac12\|{z_{k+1}-x^\ast} \|^2\\
  \leq(1-\gamma_k)A_k(f(w_k)-f^\ast)
  +\gamma_kA_k(f(w_k)-f^\ast)
  +\frac12\|{z_k-x^\ast} \|^2
  -\frac38A'_k\eta_k\|{s_k} \|^2\\
  =\mathcal{E}_k-\frac38A'_k\eta_k\|{s_k} \|^2.
\end{gather*}
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_damped_localization}
For every $k\geq1$, the points $w_k,z_k,v_k$ generated by
Algorithm~\ref{alg:ahpe_damped_appendix} satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \|{z_k-x^\ast} \|\leq R,
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_z_bound}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
  \|{w_k-x^\ast} \|\leq\left(1+\frac2{\sqrt3}\right) R,
  \qquad
  \|{v_k-x^\ast} \|\leq\left(1+\frac2{\sqrt3}\right) R.
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_localization}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
By~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_energy_budget},
\begin{equation*}
  \frac12\|{z_k-x^\ast} \|^2\leq\mathcal{E}_k\leq\frac{R^2}{2},
\end{equation*}
which gives~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_z_bound}.
We prove the bound on $\|{w_k-x^\ast} \|$ by induction.
The initialization bound~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_initialization_bound} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \|{w_1-x^\ast} \|
  \leq\|{w_1-x_0} \|+\|{x_0-x^\ast} \|
  \leq\left(1+\frac2{\sqrt3}\right) R.
\end{equation*}
Suppose the bound holds for $w_k$.
Substituting $y_k=v_k+s_k$ and
$A'_kv_k=A_kw_k+a'_kz_k$ into~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_iterate_updates} yields
\begin{equation*}
  w_{k+1}
  =\frac{(1-\gamma_k)A_kw_k+\gamma_kA'_k(v_k+s_k)}{A_{k+1}}
  =\frac{A_k}{A_{k+1}}w_k
  +\frac{a_{k+1}}{A_{k+1}}z_k
  +\frac{\gamma_kA'_k}{A_{k+1}}s_k.
\end{equation*}
Using~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_certified_bounds},~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_z_bound},
and $\gamma_ka'_k=a_{k+1}$, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  \|{w_{k+1}-x^\ast} \|
  \leq\frac{A_k}{A_{k+1}}\|{w_k-x^\ast} \|
  +\frac{a_{k+1}}{A_{k+1}}\|{z_k-x^\ast} \|
  +\frac{\gamma_kA'_k}{A_{k+1}}\|{s_k} \|\\
  \leq\frac{A_k}{A_{k+1}}\left(1+\frac2{\sqrt3}\right) R
  +\frac{a_{k+1}}{A_{k+1}}R
  +\frac{2a_{k+1}}{\sqrt3A_{k+1}}R
  =\left(1+\frac2{\sqrt3}\right) R.
\end{gather*}
This completes the induction. Finally,
\begin{equation*}
  \|{v_k-x^\ast} \|
  \leq\frac{A_k}{A'_k}\|{w_k-x^\ast} \|
  +\frac{a'_k}{A'_k}\|{z_k-x^\ast} \|
  \leq\frac{A_k}{A'_k}\left(1+\frac2{\sqrt3}\right) R
  +\frac{a'_k}{A'_k}R
  \leq\left(1+\frac2{\sqrt3}\right) R,
\end{equation*}
which proves~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_localization}.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- lemma-39: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_damped_iteration_count}
Suppose that $f$ is convex,~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} holds, and
either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds. Assume that $R>0$ and set
\begin{equation}
  A_{\mathrm{tr}}:=
  \min\left\lbrace\frac{B^{7/2}}{96M_0R},\frac{B^2}{32\delta}\right\rbrace,
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_transition_weight}
\end{equation}
where $B^2/(32\delta)=+\infty$ when $\delta=0$.
The weights $A_k$, $k\geq1$, generated by Algorithm~\ref{alg:ahpe_damped_appendix} satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
    k-1\leq{} \frac{16}{3}B+2\log_2B
    +\left(6B+\frac32\right)
      \log_+\frac{\min\left\lbrace A_k,A_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace}{A_1}
    +35\left(\sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}-B\right).
  \end{aligned}
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_iteration_count}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-39 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
Fix $k\geq1$ and define
\begin{gather*}
  \mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{=}:=
  \left\lbrace i\in\{1,\ldots,k-1\}:\tau_i=\eta_i,
       \ \eta_i\leq2\Lambda(A_i)\right\rbrace,\\
  \mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{>}:=
  \left\lbrace i\in\{1,\ldots,k-1\}:\tau_i>\eta_i,
       \ \eta_i\geq\Lambda(A_i)/2\right\rbrace.
\end{gather*}
We first bound $|\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{=}|$ in terms of $A_k$.
On these iterations, the bound $\eta_i\leq2\Lambda(A_i)$
gives an increase of $A_i$.
For $i\in\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{=}$, we have $\gamma_i=1$, $A_{i+1}=A'_i$,
and $(a'_i)^2=A'_i/\eta_i$. Hence,
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{a'_i}{A_i}
  =\sqrt{\frac{A'_i}{\eta_iA_i^2}}
  \geq\frac1{\sqrt{\eta_iA_i}}
  \geq\frac1{\sqrt{2A_i\Lambda(A_i)}}.
\end{equation*}
Using $\log(1+t)\geq t/(1+t)$ for $t\geq0$ gives
\begin{gather*}
  \log\frac{A_{i+1}}{A_i}
  =\log\left(1+\frac{a'_i}{A_i}\right)
  \geq\log\left(1+\frac1{\sqrt{2A_i\Lambda(A_i)}}\right)
  \geq\frac1{\sqrt{2A_i\Lambda(A_i)}+1}
  \geq\frac1{3\sqrt{A_i\Lambda(A_i)}}.
\end{gather*}
Since $\sqrt{t\Lambda(t)}$ is nondecreasing, each $i\in\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{=}$
therefore satisfies
\begin{gather*}
  \int_{A_i}^{A_{i+1}}\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda(t)}{t}}dt
  =\int_{A_i}^{A_{i+1}}\frac{\sqrt{t\Lambda(t)}}{t}dt
  \geq\sqrt{A_i\Lambda(A_i)}\log\frac{A_{i+1}}{A_i}\geq\frac13.
\end{gather*}
Summing over $\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{=}$ and using the nonnegativity of the integrand,
we obtain
\begin{equation}
    |\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{=}|=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{=}}1
    \leq3\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{=}}\int_{A_i}^{A_{i+1}}\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda(t)}{t}}dt 
    \leq3\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}\int_{A_i}^{A_{i+1}}\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda(t)}{t}}dt 
    =3\int_{A_1}^{A_k}\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda(t)}{t}}dt.
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_down_count}
\end{equation}
We next bound $|\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{>}|$ using~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_energy_budget}.
We first bound the term $\frac38A'_i\eta_i\|{s_i} \|^2$ from below.
For $i\in\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{>}$, we have $\tau_i>\eta_i\geq\frac{\Lambda(A_i)}{2}\geq16\delta$. Thus, by Lemma~\ref{lem:ahpe_damped_movement},~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_movement_lower_bound} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \|{s_i} \|\geq\min\left\lbrace r_0,\frac{\tau_i}{48M_0}\right\rbrace
  \geq\min\left\lbrace r_0,\frac{\Lambda(A_i)}{96M_0}\right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
Since $A'_i\geq A_i$ and $\eta_i\geq\Lambda(A_i)/2$, it follows that
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  \frac38A'_i\eta_i\|{s_i} \|^2
  &\geq\frac3{16}A_i\Lambda(A_i)
  \min\left\lbrace r_0^2,\frac{\Lambda(A_i)^2}{(96M_0)^2}\right\rbrace\\
  &=\frac{3}{16\sqrt{A_i\Lambda(A_i)}}
  \min\left\lbrace \left( A_i\Lambda(A_i)\right)^{3/2}r_0^2,
       \frac{A_i^{3/2}\Lambda(A_i)^{7/2}}{(96M_0)^2}\right\rbrace.
\end{aligned}
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_down_bound}
\end{equation}

We now use the definition of $\Lambda$~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_threshold} to bound both terms in the last minimum.
For $r_0<+\infty$, the definition of $B$ and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_threshold} give
\begin{equation*}
  \left( A_i\Lambda(A_i)\right)^{3/2}r_0^2
  \geq B^3r_0^2
  \geq\left(\frac{R}{r_0}\right)^2r_0^2=R^2.
\end{equation*}
Also,~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_threshold} gives
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{A_i^{3/2}\Lambda(A_i)^{7/2}}{(96M_0)^2}
  \geq\frac{A_i^{3/2}\left((96M_0R)^{4/7}A_i^{-3/7}\right)^{7/2}}{(96M_0)^2}
  =R^2.
\end{equation*}
Substituting these bounds in~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_down_bound} and using that $A_i\leq A_k$
and $A\Lambda(A)$ is nondecreasing, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
  \frac38A'_i\eta_i\|{s_i} \|^2
  \geq\frac{3R^2}{16\sqrt{A_i\Lambda(A_i)}}
  \geq\frac{3R^2}{16\sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}}.
\end{equation*}
Summing over $i\in\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{>}$ and using~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_energy_budget}, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{3R^2}{16\sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}}|\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{>}|
  =\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{>}}\frac{3R^2}{16\sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}}
  \leq\frac38\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{>}}A'_i\eta_i\|{s_i} \|^2
  \leq\frac38\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}A'_i\eta_i\|{s_i} \|^2
  \leq\frac{R^2}{2}.
\end{equation*}
Therefore,
\begin{equation}
  |\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{>}|\leq\frac83\sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}.
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_up_count}
\end{equation}
It remains to bound the number $(k-1)-|\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{=}|-|\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{>}|$ of iterations outside $\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{=}\cup\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{>}$.
For these iterations, there are two cases:
\begin{itemize}
  \item First, if $\tau_i=\eta_i$, then $\eta_i>2\Lambda(A_i)$, $\eta_{i+1}=\frac{\eta_i}{2}$.
  \item Second, if $\tau_i>\eta_i$, then $\eta_i<\frac{\Lambda(A_i)}{2}, \eta_{i+1}=2\eta_i$.
\end{itemize}
To measure the change relative to $\Lambda(A_i)$, set
$V_i:=\left|\log\frac{\eta_i}{\Lambda(A_i)}\right|$.
In the first case, $\eta_{i+1}>\Lambda(A_i)$, so
\begin{equation*}
  \left|\log\frac{\eta_{i+1}}{\Lambda(A_i)}\right|
  =\log\frac{\eta_i}{2\Lambda(A_i)}
  =\log\frac{\eta_i}{\Lambda(A_i)}-\log2
  =V_i-\log2.
\end{equation*}
In the second case, $\eta_{i+1}<\Lambda(A_i)$, so
\begin{equation*}
  \left|\log\frac{\eta_{i+1}}{\Lambda(A_i)}\right|
  =-\log\frac{2\eta_i}{\Lambda(A_i)}
  =-\log\frac{\eta_i}{\Lambda(A_i)}-\log2
  =V_i-\log2.
\end{equation*}
For $i\in\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{=}\cup\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{>}$, the update of $\eta_i$ gives
$\left|\log\frac{\eta_{i+1}}{\Lambda(A_i)}\right|\leq V_i+\log2$.

Since $\Lambda(A_{i+1})\leq\Lambda(A_i)$,
\begin{gather*}
  V_{i+1}
  =\left|\log\frac{\eta_{i+1}}{\Lambda(A_i)}
        +\log\frac{\Lambda(A_i)}{\Lambda(A_{i+1})}\right|
  \leq\left|\log\frac{\eta_{i+1}}{\Lambda(A_i)}\right|
       +\log\frac{\Lambda(A_i)}{\Lambda(A_{i+1})}.
\end{gather*}
Summing over $i=1,\ldots,k-1$ and telescoping the logarithms gives
\begin{gather*}
  V_k-V_1
  \leq\left(|\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{=}|+|\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{>}|\right)\log2
       -\left((k-1)-|\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{=}|-|\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{>}|\right)\log2
       +\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}\log\frac{\Lambda(A_i)}{\Lambda(A_{i+1})}\\
  =\left(2\left(|\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{=}|+|\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{>}|\right)-(k-1)\right)\log2
       +\log\frac{\Lambda(A_1)}{\Lambda(A_k)}.
\end{gather*}
Initialization gives $\eta_1=1/A_1$. Since $A_1\Lambda(A_1)\geq1$,
\begin{equation*}
  V_1=\left|\log\frac1{A_1\Lambda(A_1)}\right|
  =\log\left( A_1\Lambda(A_1)\right).
\end{equation*}
Also, monotonicity of $A\Lambda(A)$ implies
\begin{equation*}
  \log\frac{\Lambda(A_1)}{\Lambda(A_k)}
  =\log\frac{A_k}{A_1}
   +\log\frac{A_1\Lambda(A_1)}{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}
  \leq\log\frac{A_k}{A_1}.
\end{equation*}
Using $V_k\geq0$, combining the logarithms, and dividing by $\log2$, we obtain
\begin{equation}
  k-1\leq2\left(|\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{=}|+|\mathcal{S}_{k-1}^{>}|\right)
  +\log_2\left( A_k\Lambda(A_1)\right).
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_iteration_balance}
\end{equation}
Substituting~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_down_count} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_up_count}
into~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_iteration_balance} gives
\begin{equation}
  k-1\leq6\int_{A_1}^{A_k}\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda(t)}{t}}dt
  +\frac{16}{3}\sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}
  +\log_2\left( A_k\Lambda(A_1)\right).
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_iteration_integral}
\end{equation}
We now estimate the integral and logarithmic term in~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_iteration_integral}.
By~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_threshold} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_transition_weight},
\begin{equation*}
  \sqrt{A\Lambda(A)}=
  \begin{cases}
    B, & 0<A\leq A_{\mathrm{tr}},\\
    \max\left\lbrace(96M_0RA)^{2/7},\sqrt{32\delta A}\right\rbrace,
       & A>A_{\mathrm{tr}}.
  \end{cases}
\end{equation*}
Consider an interval $[u,v]\subset[A_{\mathrm{tr}},+\infty)$ on which the same term attains the maximum.
If $\sqrt{t\Lambda(t)}=(96M_0Rt)^{2/7}$ on this interval, then
\begin{gather*}
  \int_u^v\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda(t)}t}dt
  =(96M_0R)^{2/7}\int_u^v t^{-5/7}dt
  =\frac72\left(\sqrt{v\Lambda(v)}-\sqrt{u\Lambda(u)}\right),\quad 
  \log\frac vu=\frac72\log\frac{\sqrt{v\Lambda(v)}}{\sqrt{u\Lambda(u)}}.
\end{gather*}
If $\sqrt{t\Lambda(t)}=\sqrt{32\delta t}$ on this interval, then
\begin{gather*}
  \int_u^v\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda(t)}t}dt
  =\sqrt{32\delta}\int_u^v t^{-1/2}dt
  =2\left(\sqrt{v\Lambda(v)}-\sqrt{u\Lambda(u)}\right),\quad 
  \log\frac vu=2\log\frac{\sqrt{v\Lambda(v)}}{\sqrt{u\Lambda(u)}}.
\end{gather*}
Both coefficients are at most $7/2$.
Summing over the intervals above $A_{\mathrm{tr}}$, the intermediate endpoint terms cancel in both bounds.
Below $A_{\mathrm{tr}}$, we have $\sqrt{t\Lambda(t)}=B$ and integrate $B/t$.
Thus, for every $A\geq A_1$,
\begin{gather}
  \int_{A_1}^{A}\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda(t)}{t}}dt
  \leq B\log_+\frac{\min\left\lbrace A,A_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace}{A_1}
       +\frac72\left(\sqrt{A\Lambda(A)}-B\right),
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_clipped_integral}\\
  \log\frac{A}{A_1}
  \leq\log_+\frac{\min\left\lbrace A,A_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace}{A_1}
       +\frac72\log\frac{\sqrt{A\Lambda(A)}}B.
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_clipped_log}
\end{gather}
These bounds also hold when $A_1>A_{\mathrm{tr}}$, since $\sqrt{A_1\Lambda(A_1)}\geq B$.
Using $\log_2t\leq\frac32\log t$ for $t\geq1$,~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_clipped_log},
and the monotonicity of $A\Lambda(A)$, we obtain
\begin{gather}
    \log_2\left( A_k\Lambda(A_1)\right)
    =\log_2\frac{A_k}{A_1}+\log_2\left( A_1\Lambda(A_1)\right)
    \leq\frac32\log\frac{A_k}{A_1}
         +2\log_2B+3\log\frac{\sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}}B \notag \\
    \leq2\log_2B+\frac32\log_+\frac{\min\left\lbrace A_k,A_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace}{A_1}
         +\frac{33}{4}\log\frac{\sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}}B.
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_clipped_log_term}
\end{gather}
Substituting~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_clipped_integral} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_clipped_log_term}
into~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_iteration_integral}, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  k-1\leq\frac{16}{3}B+2\log_2B
       +\left(6B+\frac32\right)\log_+\frac{\min\left\lbrace A_k,A_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace}{A_1}\\
  +\frac{79}{3}\left(\sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}-B\right)
       +\frac{33}{4}\log\frac{\sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}}B.
\end{gather*}
Finally, since $\sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}\geq B\geq1$,
\begin{equation*}
  \log\frac{\sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}}B
  \leq\frac{\sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}-B}{B}, \quad 
  \frac{79}{3}+\frac{33}{4B}
  \leq\frac{415}{12}<35.
\end{equation*}
Substituting these inequalities proves~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_iteration_count}.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- theorem-14: body_md -->
\label{thm:ahpe_damped_convergence_appendix}
Suppose that $f$ is convex,~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian} holds, and
either~\eqref{as:gh} or~\eqref{as:lh} holds.
Let $\overline\tau_0:=\overline\tau(x_0)$, where $\overline\tau(x)$ is defined in~\eqref{eq:backtrack_upper_bound}.
For every $\varepsilon>0$, the method generates an iterate $w_N$ satisfying
$f(w_N)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon$ within
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  N\leq{}&2+\frac{16}{3}B+2\log_2B
    +\left(6B+\frac32\right)\log_+\frac{\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace R^2}{\max\left\lbrace\varepsilon,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace}\\
    &+35\left(\max\left\lbrace B,\left(\frac{48M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/7},
      4\sqrt{\frac{\delta R^2}{\varepsilon}}\right\rbrace-B\right)
\end{aligned}
  \label{eq:app_ahpe_damped_outer_complexity}
\end{equation}
outer iterations, including initialization, each using at most one Hessian evaluation.
Moreover, set
\begin{equation}
  K:=2+\left\lfloor
    \frac{16}{3}B+2\log_2B
    +\left(6B+\frac32\right)\log_+\frac{\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace R^2}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}}
  \right\rfloor.
  \label{eq:app_ahpe_damped_transition_index}
\end{equation}
For this $K$,
\begin{gather}
  f(w_k)-f^\ast
  \leq\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace R^2
    \exp\left(-\frac{\max\left\lbrace0,k-1-\frac{16}{3}B-2\log_2B\right\rbrace}{6B+\frac32}\right),
  \qquad 1\leq k<K,
  \label{eq:app_ahpe_damped_far_rate}\\
  f(w_{K+n})-f^\ast
  \leq\max\left\lbrace\frac{48M_0R^3}{(B+n/35)^{7/2}},
    \frac{16\delta R^2}{(B+n/35)^2}\right\rbrace,
  \qquad n=0,1,\ldots.
  \label{eq:app_ahpe_damped_near_rate}
\end{gather}
<!-- end theorem-14 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
Lemmas~\ref{lem:pd_ms_backtracking} and~\ref{lem:ahpe_damped_initialization}
show that all backtracking loops terminate.
If initialization returns a minimizer, all claims are immediate.
By~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_energy_budget},
\begin{equation}
  f(w_k)-f^\ast\leq\frac{\mathcal{E}_k}{A_k}\leq\frac{R^2}{2A_k}.
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_error_certificate}
\end{equation}
Since $a_{k+1}>0$, the $A_k$ strictly increase.

Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and set $A_\varepsilon:= R^2/(2\varepsilon)$.
If $A_1\geq A_\varepsilon$, initialization suffices by~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_error_certificate}.
Otherwise, by~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_iteration_count}, unless a minimizer is returned earlier,
there exists a first index $N$ with $A_N\geq A_\varepsilon$.
Then $N\geq2$, $A_{N-1}<A_\varepsilon\leq A_N$, and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_error_certificate}
gives $f(w_N)-f^\ast\leq\varepsilon$.
Applying~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_iteration_count} at $N-1$
and using monotonicity of its right-hand side, we obtain
\begin{gather*}
  N\leq2+\frac{16}{3}B+2\log_2B
  +\left(6B+\frac32\right)\log_+\frac{\min\left\lbrace A_\varepsilon,A_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace}{A_1}
  +35\left(\sqrt{A_\varepsilon\Lambda(A_\varepsilon)}-B\right).
\end{gather*}
By~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_damped_scales} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_transition_weight},
$A_{\mathrm{tr}}=R^2/(2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}})$. Hence,
\begin{gather*}
  \log_+\frac{\min\left\lbrace A_\varepsilon,A_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace}{A_1}
  =\log_+\frac{R^2}{2A_1\max\left\lbrace\varepsilon,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace},\\
  \sqrt{A_\varepsilon\Lambda(A_\varepsilon)}
  =\max\left\lbrace B,\left(\frac{48M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/7},
    4\sqrt{\frac{\delta R^2}{\varepsilon}}\right\rbrace.
\end{gather*}
Next, by Lemma~\ref{lem:ahpe_damped_initialization} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_initialization} we have 
\begin{equation}
  \frac{1}{A_1} = \eta_1 \leq \max\left\lbrace\eta_0, 2 \overline{\tau}_0\right\rbrace \leq 2\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace.
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_initial_weight}
\end{equation}
Hence,
\begin{equation}
  \frac{R^2}{2A_1}\leq\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace R^2,
  \qquad
  2\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace A_{\mathrm{tr}}=\frac{\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace R^2}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}},
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_initial_scales}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation*}
  \log_+\frac{R^2}{2A_1\max\left\lbrace\varepsilon,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace}
  \leq\log_+\frac{\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace R^2}{\max\left\lbrace\varepsilon,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace}.
\end{equation*}
Substituting these estimates proves~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_damped_outer_complexity}.
If a zero gradient is queried before reaching $A_\varepsilon$, let $N$ count the
outer iterations up to that return. The last completed weight still satisfies
$A_{N-1}<A_\varepsilon$, so the same estimate applies, and the returned point is a minimizer.
There is one Hessian evaluation during initialization and at most one on each
main iteration, since all inner trials reuse that Hessian.

We now prove~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_damped_far_rate} and~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_damped_near_rate}
for iterates produced before a zero-gradient return.
The right-hand side of~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_iteration_count} is nonincreasing in $A_1$,
and $1/A_1\leq2\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace$ by~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_initial_weight}.
Hence,~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_iteration_count} remains valid with $1/A_1$ replaced by $2\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace$.
First, let $1\leq k<K$. If $A_k\leq A_{\mathrm{tr}}$, then
$\sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}=B$, and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_iteration_count} gives
\begin{equation*}
  k-1\leq\frac{16}{3}B+2\log_2B
  +\left(6B+\frac32\right)\log\left(2\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace A_k\right).
\end{equation*}
If $A_k>A_{\mathrm{tr}}$, then~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_damped_transition_index},~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_initial_scales},
and $2\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace A_k\geq1$ give
\begin{gather*}
  k-1\leq K-2
  \leq\frac{16}{3}B+2\log_2B
    +\left(6B+\frac32\right)\log_+\left(2\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace A_{\mathrm{tr}}\right)\\
  \leq\frac{16}{3}B+2\log_2B
    +\left(6B+\frac32\right)\log\left(2\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace A_k\right).
\end{gather*}
Thus, in both cases, since $\log\left(2\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace A_k\right)\geq0$,
\begin{equation*}
  \log\left(2\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace A_k\right)
  \geq\frac{\max\left\lbrace0,k-1-\frac{16}{3}B-2\log_2B\right\rbrace}{6B+\frac32}.
\end{equation*}
Combining this bound with~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_error_certificate}
proves~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_damped_far_rate}.

Next, let $k=K+n$ with $n\geq0$.
By~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_damped_transition_index} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_initial_scales},
\begin{equation*}
  \frac{16}{3}B+2\log_2B
  +\left(6B+\frac32\right)\log_+\left(2\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace A_{\mathrm{tr}}\right)+n<k-1.
\end{equation*}
Since $\min\left\lbrace A_k,A_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\rbrace\leq A_{\mathrm{tr}}$,~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_iteration_count} also gives
\begin{equation*}
  k-1\leq\frac{16}{3}B+2\log_2B
  +\left(6B+\frac32\right)\log_+\left(2\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace A_{\mathrm{tr}}\right)
  +35\left(\sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}-B\right).
\end{equation*}
Combining these inequalities yields
\begin{equation*}
  \sqrt{A_k\Lambda(A_k)}>B+\frac n{35}\geq B.
\end{equation*}
Therefore, by~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_threshold},
\begin{gather*}
  \max\left\lbrace(96M_0RA_k)^{2/7},\sqrt{32\delta A_k}\right\rbrace>B+\frac n{35},\quad
  \frac1{A_k}\leq
  \max\left\lbrace\frac{96M_0R}{(B+n/35)^{7/2}},
    \frac{32\delta}{(B+n/35)^2}\right\rbrace.
\end{gather*}
Multiplying the last inequality by $R^2/2$ and using~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_error_certificate}
proves~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_damped_near_rate}.
After a zero-gradient return, the output sequence consists of minimizers,
so both rate bounds continue to hold.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{cor:ahpe_damped_oracle_complexity}
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:ahpe_damped_convergence_appendix},
fix $\varepsilon>0$. Let $N$ be the number of outer iterations, including initialization,
until $A_N\geq R^2/(2\varepsilon)$ or an earlier zero-gradient return.
Then Algorithm~\ref{alg:ahpe_damped_appendix} uses at most $N$ Hessian evaluations and at most
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  &7N+\log_{2,+}\frac{\overline\tau_0}{\eta_0}
    +30\sqrt{\frac{2\delta R^2}{\varepsilon}}
    +120\left(\frac{2M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/7}\\
  &+8B\log_{2,+}\frac{\delta+\overline g/r_0}{\delta+M_0r_0}
    \left(1+\log_+\frac{4\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace R^2}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/3}
\end{aligned}
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_gradient_count}
\end{equation}
gradient evaluations.
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- lemma-40: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_damped_summability}
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:ahpe_damped_convergence_appendix},
every completed main iteration of Algorithm~\ref{alg:ahpe_damped_appendix} satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \eta_iA_i\geq\frac12,\qquad
 A_{i+1}\leq(2+\sqrt3)A_i<4A_i.
 \label{eq:ahpe_damped_weight_overshoot}
\end{equation}
For every $m\geq1$ and $A=A_{m+1}$,
\begin{gather}
 \sum_{i=1}^{m}\eta_i^{-1/2}\leq5\sqrt A,\qquad
 \sum_{i=1}^{m}\left(\frac{\|{s_i} \|}{\eta_i}\right)^{2/7}
 \leq20(RA)^{2/7},
 \label{eq:ahpe_damped_weighted_sums}\\
 \sum_{i=1}^{m}\frac1{\sqrt{\eta_iA_i}}
 \leq8\log6+4\log\frac A{A_1}.
 \label{eq:ahpe_damped_logarithmic_sum}
\end{gather}
<!-- end lemma-40 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
Initialization gives $\eta_1A_1=1$. If $\tau_i>\eta_i$, then
$\eta_{i+1}=2\eta_i$ and $A_{i+1}>A_i$.
If $\tau_i=\eta_i$, then $A_{i+1}=A'_i$, $a'_i\geq1/\eta_i$, and
\begin{equation*}
 \eta_{i+1}A_{i+1}=\frac12\eta_iA'_i
 =\frac12(\eta_i a'_i)^2\geq\frac12.
\end{equation*}
Induction proves the first bound in~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_weight_overshoot}.
Since $\eta_iA_i\geq1/2$ and $0<\gamma_i\leq1$,
\begin{equation*}
 \frac{A_{i+1}}{A_i}\leq\frac{A'_i}{A_i}
 =1+\frac{1+\sqrt{1+4\eta_iA_i}}{2\eta_iA_i}
 \leq2+\sqrt3<4.
\end{equation*}
On every iteration with $\tau_i=\eta_i$, we have $a'_i=\sqrt{A_{i+1}/\eta_i}$ and
\begin{equation*}
 \sqrt{A_{i+1}}-\sqrt{A_i}
 =\frac{a'_i}{\sqrt{A_{i+1}}+\sqrt{A_i}}
 =\frac{\sqrt{A_{i+1}}}{\sqrt{\eta_i}\left(\sqrt{A_{i+1}}+\sqrt{A_i}\right)}
 \geq\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\eta_i}}.
\end{equation*}
All weight increments are nonnegative, so
\begin{equation*}
 \sum_{\substack{1\leq i\leq m\\\tau_i=\eta_i}}\eta_i^{-1/2}
 \leq2(\sqrt A-\sqrt{A_1}).
\end{equation*}
The update of $\eta_i$ gives $\eta_{i+1}^{-1/2}=\sqrt2\eta_i^{-1/2}$ when $\tau_i=\eta_i$,
and $\eta_{i+1}^{-1/2}=\eta_i^{-1/2}/\sqrt2$ otherwise.
Telescoping and $\eta_1^{-1/2}=\sqrt{A_1}$ yield
\begin{gather*}
 (1-1/\sqrt2)\sum_{\substack{1\leq i\leq m\\\tau_i>\eta_i}}\eta_i^{-1/2}
 =(\sqrt2-1)\sum_{\substack{1\leq i\leq m\\\tau_i=\eta_i}}\eta_i^{-1/2}
 +\eta_1^{-1/2}-\eta_{m+1}^{-1/2},\\
 \sum_{i=1}^{m}\eta_i^{-1/2}
 \leq(1+\sqrt2)\sum_{\substack{1\leq i\leq m\\\tau_i=\eta_i}}\eta_i^{-1/2}
 +(2+\sqrt2)\sqrt{A_1}
 \leq2(1+\sqrt2)\sqrt A-\sqrt2\sqrt{A_1}
 \leq5\sqrt A.
\end{gather*}
Set $S_0=\sqrt{A_1}$ and $S_i=S_0+\sum_{j=1}^{i}\eta_j^{-1/2}$.
Applying the preceding bound to each shorter prefix gives
\begin{equation}
 S_m\leq6\sqrt A,\qquad
 S_{i-1}\leq6\sqrt{A_i},\qquad
 S_i\leq(6+\sqrt2)\sqrt{A_i}\leq8\sqrt{A_i}.
 \label{eq:ahpe_damped_inclusive_sums}
\end{equation}
Here $\eta_i^{-1/2}\leq\sqrt{2A_i}$ follows from~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_weight_overshoot}.
Since $\eta_i^{-1/2}=S_i-S_{i-1}$, integration of the decreasing function $1/t$
yields
\begin{equation*}
 \sum_{i=1}^{m}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\eta_iA_i}}
 \leq8\sum_{i=1}^{m}\frac{S_i-S_{i-1}}{S_i}
 \leq8\int_{S_0}^{S_m}\frac{dt}{t}
 \leq8\log6+4\log\frac A{A_1}.
\end{equation*}
This proves~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_logarithmic_sum}.

For the second bound in~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_weighted_sums},
H\"older's inequality gives
\begin{gather*}
 \sum_{i=1}^{m}\left(\frac{\|{s_i} \|}{\eta_i}\right)^{2/7}
 =\sum_{i=1}^{m}\left( A_i\eta_i\|{s_i} \|^2\right)^{1/7}
       \left(\frac{1}{\eta_i^{1/2}A_i^{1/6}}\right)^{6/7}
 \leq\left(\sum_{i=1}^{m}A_i\eta_i\|{s_i} \|^2\right)^{1/7}
      \left(\sum_{i=1}^{m}\frac{1}{\eta_i^{1/2}A_i^{1/6}}\right)^{6/7},\\
 \sum_{i=1}^{m}\frac{1}{\eta_i^{1/2}A_i^{1/6}}
 \leq2\sum_{i=1}^{m}\frac{S_i-S_{i-1}}{S_i^{1/3}}
 \leq2\int_{S_0}^{S_m}t^{-1/3}dt
 \leq3S_m^{2/3}
 \leq3\cdot6^{2/3}A^{1/3}.
\end{gather*}
The last display uses~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_inclusive_sums}.
Substituting these bounds and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_step_energy} gives
\begin{equation*}
 \sum_{i=1}^{m}\left(\frac{\|{s_i} \|}{\eta_i}\right)^{2/7}
 \leq(4R^2/3)^{1/7}
       (3\cdot6^{2/3}A^{1/3})^{6/7}
 \leq20(RA)^{2/7}.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- lemma-41: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_damped_long_count}
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:ahpe_damped_convergence_appendix},
for $m\geq1$ and $A=A_{m+1}$, define
\begin{equation*}
 \mathcal I_m:=
 \left\lbrace i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:\tau_i>\eta_i,\ \|{s_i} \|>r_0\right\rbrace.
\end{equation*}
Then
\begin{equation}
 |\mathcal I_m|\leq8B\left(1+\log\frac A{A_1}\right)^{2/3}.
 \label{eq:ahpe_damped_long_count}
\end{equation}
If $r_0=+\infty$, then $\mathcal I_m$ is empty.
<!-- end lemma-41 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
Let $r_0<+\infty$. By~\eqref{eq:app_ahpe_damped_scales}, $(R/r_0)^{2/3}\leq B$.
H\"older's inequality,~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_step_energy},
and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_logarithmic_sum} give
\begin{gather*}
 |\mathcal I_m|
 \leq r_0^{-2/3}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_m}\|{s_i} \|^{2/3}
 =r_0^{-2/3}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_m}
 \left( A_i\eta_i\|{s_i} \|^2\right)^{1/3}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\eta_iA_i}}\right)^{2/3}\\
 \leq r_0^{-2/3}
 \left(\sum_{i=1}^{m}A_i\eta_i\|{s_i} \|^2\right)^{1/3}
 \left(\sum_{i=1}^{m}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\eta_iA_i}}\right)^{2/3}
 \leq(4/3)^{1/3}B
 \left(8\log6+4\log\frac A{A_1}\right)^{2/3}.
\end{gather*}
Since $(4/3)^{1/3}(8\log6)^{2/3}<8$ and $8\log6>4$,
this proves~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_long_count}.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- lemma-42: body_md -->
\label{lem:ahpe_damped_rejection_sum}
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:ahpe_damped_convergence_appendix},
let $b_i:=\log_2(\tau_i/\eta_i)$ be the number of rejected trials
in main iteration $i$, including failed $\mathsf{PD}$ tests.
For every $m\geq1$ and $A=A_{m+1}$,
\begin{equation}
  \sum_{i=1}^{m}b_i\leq{}5m+30\sqrt{\delta A}+120(M_0RA)^{2/7}
  +8B\log_{2,+}\frac{\delta+\overline g/r_0}{\delta+M_0r_0}
    \left(1+\log\frac{A}{A_1}\right)^{2/3},
  \label{eq:ahpe_damped_rejection_sum}
\end{equation}
where the last term is absent if $r_0=+\infty$.
<!-- end lemma-42 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
If $\tau_i=\eta_i$, then $b_i=0$. Let $\tau_i>\eta_i$.
If $\|{s_i} \|\leq r_0$, then Lemma~\ref{lem:ahpe_damped_movement} gives
$\tau_i\leq8\delta+24M_0\|{s_i} \|$.
If $\|{s_i} \|>r_0$, then~\eqref{as:inexact_hessian}, convexity,
and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_gradient_bound} give
\begin{gather*}
  (\tau_i-\delta)\|{s_i} \|^2
  \leq\left\langle(H(v_i)+\tau_iI)s_i,s_i\right\rangle
  =-\left\langle\nabla f(v_i),s_i\right\rangle
  \leq\overline g\|{s_i} \|,\\
  \tau_i\leq\delta+\frac{\overline g}{r_0}
  \leq\max\left\lbrace1,\frac{\delta+\overline g/r_0}{\delta+M_0r_0}\right\rbrace
  \left(\delta+M_0\|{s_i} \|\right).
\end{gather*}
Since $8\delta+24M_0\|{s_i} \|\leq32\eta_i\left(1+\frac{\delta}{\eta_i}\right)\left(1+\frac{M_0\|{s_i} \|}{\eta_i}\right)$,
in both cases
\begin{equation*}
  b_i\leq5+\log_2\left(1+\frac{\delta}{\eta_i}\right)
  +\log_2\left(1+\frac{M_0\|{s_i} \|}{\eta_i}\right)
  +\mathbf1_{\{i\in\mathcal I_m\}}\log_{2,+}\frac{\delta+\overline g/r_0}{\delta+M_0r_0}.
\end{equation*}
Since $\log(1+x)=\int_0^x\frac{dt}{1+t}\leq\frac{x^p}{p}$ for $x\geq0$ and $p\in(0,1]$,
we have $\log_2(1+x)\leq6x^p$ for $p\in\left\lbrace\frac12,\frac27\right\rbrace$. Hence,
\begin{equation*}
  \sum_{i=1}^{m}b_i\leq5m+6\sqrt\delta\sum_{i=1}^{m}\eta_i^{-1/2}
  +6M_0^{2/7}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\left(\frac{\|{s_i} \|}{\eta_i}\right)^{2/7}
  +|\mathcal I_m|\log_{2,+}\frac{\delta+\overline g/r_0}{\delta+M_0r_0}.
\end{equation*}
Substituting~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_weighted_sums} and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_long_count}
proves~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_rejection_sum}.
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{lem:ahpe_damped_initialization}, initialization rejects at most
$1+\log_{2,+}\frac{\overline\tau_0}{\eta_0}$ trials.
If $A_1\geq R^2/(2\varepsilon)$, then $N=1$ and there are no main iterations.
Otherwise, the minimality of $N$ and~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_weight_overshoot} give
$A_N<4A_{N-1}<2R^2/\varepsilon$. Together with~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_initial_weight}, this gives
\begin{gather*}
  \sqrt{\delta A_N}\leq\sqrt{\frac{2\delta R^2}{\varepsilon}},\quad
  (M_0RA_N)^{2/7}\leq\left(\frac{2M_0R^3}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/7}, \quad
  \frac{A_N}{A_1}\leq\frac{4\max\left\lbrace\eta_0,\overline\tau_0\right\rbrace R^2}{\varepsilon}.
\end{gather*}
Substituting these bounds into~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_rejection_sum} with $m=N-1$
and adding the initialization rejections, we obtain that the total number of rejected
trials is at most the right-hand side of~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_gradient_count} with $7N$ replaced by $5N$.
Each outer iteration makes one call $\textnormal{\textsc{MSBacktrack}}(x,\eta)$, which uses $H(x)$, $\nabla f(x)$,
and one gradient for each trial with a positive definite matrix.
The updates reuse the gradient at the accepted point.
Hence, the method uses at most $N$ Hessian evaluations, and the number of gradient
evaluations is at most $2N$ plus the number of rejected trials.
This proves~\eqref{eq:ahpe_damped_gradient_count}.
<!-- end proof-60 -->
